Performance The portable expression materializes parsed input and one string per record before joining. These are in-memory string checks, not a streaming or bounded-memory export benchmark. The capture API returns text; octet encoding, BOM, canonical digest/signature correctness and transport framing need independent checks. ## 15. Known Uses The partner import is a realistic invoice interchange pattern, not a claim of a named deployment. Canonical XML or JSON intended for cryptographic use requires a verified canonicalization component; none is supplied by this worked example. ## 16. Related Features See [the function-composition disposition](fn-apply-templates.md), [the manifest](../examples/cases.json), [completeness audit](../COMPLETENESS-AUDIT.md) and [supplementary audit](../SUPPLEMENTARY-COVERAGE-AUDIT.md). Existing serialization remains useful; the remaining draft controls are deferred.

sections.1:
**Serialization 4.0 parameter additions — Deferred, with a supported XSLT solidus control.** [REQ-118 tier-4 decision](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) remains; it must not imply that all serialization is missing. Bosak engine 1.1.2 reviewed against [revision 23218073](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/232180733358fc4239229267763854fda0fa2791).

Primary references: [Serialization 4.0 parameters](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xslt-xquery-serialization-40/Overview.html#serparam), [Serialization 3.1](https://www.w3.org/TR/xslt-xquery-serialization-31/). Immutable review source: [serialization XML at e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xslt-xquery-serialization-40/src/xslt-xquery-serialization.xml), section `serparam`. This is a review pin, not recovery of the missing historical adopted snapshot.
sections.2: Choose an invoice interchange format with predictable record boundaries, URI escaping and output layout. Record parameter-by-parameter behavior instead of equating accepted options with implemented serialization.
sections.3: Canonical output, JSON Lines, configurable indentation/line endings and CSV serialization controls. These are serialization parameters, distinct from XPath CSV parsing functions.
sections.4: The pinned source adds escape-solidus (issue 530/PR 534), json-lines (1471/1497), canonical (938/2259), layout controls (1234/2719) and CSV controls (2748/2794). This disposition covers those nine parameter additions, not every change to Serialization 4.0: GNodes, CSV data-model shapes, numeric/JSON rules, HTML defaults and other revisions require separate reviews.
sections.5: A partner imports one JSON invoice per physical line. Invoice identifiers, currency-labelled totals and URIs must survive serialization. A pretty JSON array cannot substitute for JSON Lines. Canonical output has a different purpose—stable representation for signing/digesting—and must use a verified canonicalization implementation.
sections.6:
| Path | Verified boundary |
|---|---|
| `fn:serialize` maps in XPath 3.1/4.0 | Nine new keys leave tested output unchanged; map-valued invalid options are tolerated |
| `fn:serialize` escape-solidus false | Still emits escaped solidus; tested default also escapes it |
| XSLT 3.0/4.0 output escape-solidus yes/no | Controls URI string escaping in the verified JSON outputs |
| `fn:serialize` json-lines true, two maps | `SERE0023` |
| XSLT json-lines yes, two strings | JSON array `["INV-1042","INV-1043"]`, not separate lines |
| `fn:serialize` method csv | Tested scalar sequence equals XML-family serialization; CSV is not established |
| XSLT method csv | `XTSE1570` |
| Explicit per-record serialization + LF joining | Portable invoice JSON Lines; empty and reordered cases verified |

Successful XPath 4.0 probes also assert the same default 3.1 outcome. XSLT error fixtures assert markers from compilation or capture; no detection-stage promise follows.
sections.7: Use existing XML/JSON/text serialization for ordinary exports. Build JSON Lines explicitly by serializing each record and joining the strings. Avoid these ignored options when a consumer requires canonical bytes, a custom layout or CSV. Do not assume that parser support for CSV delivers a CSV serializer.
sections.8:
The pinned nine-parameter boundary is:

| Parameter | Pinned draft contract | Bosak scope and evidence |
|---|---|---|
| [canonical](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xslt-xquery-serialization-40/Overview.html#XML_CANONICAL) | XML/XHTML Canonical XML 1.1; JSON canonicalization has its own rules | No handling in inspected option/property parsers. XML examples retain z-before-a attributes and an empty-element tag, so are not canonical XML |
| [json-lines](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xslt-xquery-serialization-40/Overview.html#id-json-lines) | Serialize top-level items as successive JSON records separated by line endings | No option handling; XPath error and XSLT array behavior differ |
| [escape-solidus](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xslt-xquery-serialization-40/Overview.html#JSON_ESCAPE-SOLIDUS) | Boolean controls escaping `/` as `\/` in JSON strings; adaptive has a separate parameter section | XSLT JSON yes/no verified; fn option ignored. Adaptive behavior not certified |
| [indent-unit](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xslt-xquery-serialization-40/Overview.html#XML_INDENT-UNIT) | Spaces or tabs (including literal `\t` escape), when indent is true | No handling. Current equality probes use default indent=false and do not prove an indented-layout mismatch; source inspection establishes missing control |
| [indent-attributes](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xslt-xquery-serialization-40/Overview.html#XML_INDENT-ATTRIBUTES) | Boolean refinement when indent=true; draft permits optional attribute line breaks | No handling. Absence of line breaks alone would not prove a draft violation |
| [line-ending](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xslt-xquery-serialization-40/Overview.html#XML_LINE-ENDING) | LF, CR or CRLF; `\n`/`\r` escape notation is recognized; applies after mapping/normalization | No handling. XSLT text with requested CRLF retains LF in the tested capture |
| [csv-separator](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xslt-xquery-serialization-40/Overview.html#CSV_SEPARATOR) | Single separator character for CSV fields | No handling; CSV method boundary tested separately |
| [csv-quote-character](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xslt-xquery-serialization-40/Overview.html#CSV_QUOTE-CHARACTER) | CSV quoting control | No handling; cannot infer support from ignored JSON/text options |
| [csv-header](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xslt-xquery-serialization-40/Overview.html#CSV_HEADER) | Boolean controls writing the header from the supplied CSV structure | No handling; neither method path provides verified CSV output |

XSLT text tolerance probes for canonical/layout/CSV keys deliberately test acceptance only. They do not show those parameters working in applicable methods. XML canonical and newline-bearing text probes provide stronger observed boundaries. Canonicalization entails more than sorting attributes; the examples are counterexamples, not a substitute implementation.
sections.9: The invoice batch is a JSON object with an invoices array. Each record carries ID, currency, a precomputed numeric total and a URI. The JSON serializer escapes data; string-join supplies the record separator. The manifest records exact outputs/errors and compatibility metadata.
sections.10: The portable expression parses the complete batch, selects its invoice members, serializes each separately with method=json and joins them using codepoints-to-string(10). Empty selection yields an empty string. Reordering invoices changes line order while retaining values. There is no terminal newline in this example; add one explicitly if the receiver requires it.
sections.11: The portable output is valid JSON Lines with escaped URI solidi and exactly two lines for the main input. An escaped solidus decodes to the same URI. Exact map-key order is observed fixture output, not a general stable-order or canonicalization guarantee. fn CSV fallback and XSLT JSON sequence-as-array are separate existing behavior; this slice records them without engine changes.
sections.12:
Source evidence at the reviewed revision: [XdmSerializer.cs](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/232180733358fc4239229267763854fda0fa2791/src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/XdmSerializer.cs), `ApplyParameter` ignores unrecognized map keys, and `Serialize` routes methods other than json/adaptive through XML-family serialization. Its JSON path retains its default escaping independently of the ignored new key. [OutputProperties.cs](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/232180733358fc4239229267763854fda0fa2791/src/Bosak.Xslt/Stylesheet/OutputProperties.cs) stores and parses EscapeSolidus but does not store the other additions. [ResultTreeSerializer.cs](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/232180733358fc4239229267763854fda0fa2791/src/Bosak.Xslt/Runtime/ResultTreeSerializer.cs) forwards that flag to [XdmJsonSerializer.cs](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/232180733358fc4239229267763854fda0fa2791/src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Json/XdmJsonSerializer.cs), whose sequence path can serialize multiple items as an array.

Named existing evidence: `Capture_MethodFidelity_XmlHtmlTextJson` in [XsltCaptureTests.cs](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/232180733358fc4239229267763854fda0fa2791/tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Capture/XsltCaptureTests.cs), and `Output_Text_Method_Serializes_Only_Text` in [StylesheetTests.cs](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/232180733358fc4239229267763854fda0fa2791/tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/StylesheetTests.cs). Those tests establish ordinary paths, not the nine additions. The catalog adds 52 named cases without changing engine/API/harness or promoting manual gates.
sections.13:
Complete partner invoice input (totals are already calculated; no tax or currency conversion occurs here):

```json
{"invoices":[{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30,"uri":"https://partner.example/invoices/1042"},{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12,"uri":"https://partner.example/invoices/1043"}]}
```

Portable XPath 3.1 JSON Lines export:

```xpath
(: Complete invoice batch; serialize each record separately and join with LF. :)
let $batch := parse-json('{"invoices":[{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30,"uri":"https://partner.example/invoices/1042"},{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12,"uri":"https://partner.example/invoices/1043"}]}')
return string-join($batch?invoices?* ! serialize(., map{'method':'json'}), codepoints-to-string(10))
```

Exact output, including one LF between the records and no terminal LF:

```text
{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30,"uri":"https:\/\/partner.example\/invoices\/1042"}
{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12,"uri":"https:\/\/partner.example\/invoices\/1043"}
```

Empty input:

```json
{"invoices":[]}
```

The complete [empty expression](../examples/serialization-parameters/portable-json-lines-empty.xpath) returns the empty string. Reordered input:

```json
{"invoices":[{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12,"uri":"https://partner.example/invoices/1043"},{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30,"uri":"https://partner.example/invoices/1042"}]}
```

The [complete reordered expression](../examples/serialization-parameters/portable-json-lines-reordered.xpath) returns:

```text
{"id":"INV-1043","currency":"USD","total":12,"uri":"https:\/\/partner.example\/invoices\/1043"}
{"id":"INV-1042","currency":"EUR","total":30,"uri":"https:\/\/partner.example\/invoices\/1042"}
```

Observed fn:serialize solidus control boundary:

```xpath
serialize(map{'uri':'https://partner.example/invoices/1042'}, map{'method':'json','escape-solidus':false()})
```

Exact result (false is ignored):

```text
{"uri":"https:\/\/partner.example\/invoices\/1042"}
```

```xml
<invoices><invoice id="INV-1042" currency="EUR" total="30" uri="https://partner.example/invoices/1042"/><invoice id="INV-1043" currency="USD" total="12" uri="https://partner.example/invoices/1043"/></invoices>
```

**C09 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-1.md) records 3 contract groups with exact sample/context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Name and Classification **Implemented bounded XSLT4.0 surface in public1.23.2; complete declaration contract not certified.** This existing path is retained for links; deferred describes its historical dossier, not all present behavior. [Current pinned review](../TYPE-PATTERN-GRAMMAR.md). ## 2. Intent Give an existing permitted type a stylesheet-context name without inventing a new nominal record identity. ## 3. Also Known As Named item-type alias; enumeration or structural-record alias in the reviewed forms. It does not itself request a generated constructor. ## 4. History / Supersedes The earlier REQ-118 deferral and1.2.0 implementation logs remain in the [historical snapshot](../../history/REQ126-ITEM-TYPE-SNAPSHOT-20261021.md). Enumeration-alias delivery isf53bc80f; structural-record aliases are669c862a. Current review provenance does not reconstruct the original adopted draft or promote every deferred declaration contract. ## 5. Motivation An intake classifier can name an integer quantity or permitted status set, while keeping validation and routing policy visible. ## 6. Language Alignment An alias is not a C# nominal class. Instance-of tests the supplied value; an XSLT @as binding can first perform conversion. Identical textual values or fields do not imply every type check agrees. ## 7. Applicability Use only the declared/verified aliases in a supporting host. Use ordinary3.1 types and explicit predicates in a portable3.0 stylesheet. ## 8. Structure Example declarations: `xsl:item-type name="t:status" as="enum('ready','queued')"` and `name="t:shape" as="record(x as xs:integer)"`. These are descriptive reviewed forms, not a complete grammar. ## 9. Participants [Stylesheet](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Stylesheet/Stylesheet.cs), the XPath type system and the compiled stylesheet context resolve names. No new public registration API is introduced here. ## 10. Collaborations Combine aliases with bindings and type/pattern checks; compare the [intake report](../examples/intake-types/README.md) and [record identity reference](xslt-record-type.md). ## 11. Consequences Reduces repeated type syntax but adds a host/context dependency. Expanded names matter; enum treat mismatch raises XPDY0050. Do not treat successful coercion as evidence that an unconverted map already carried an annotation. ## 12. Implementation **C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S8-patterns. Fresh version-4 stylesheets in both hosts cover array/member sequences, map missing-versus-empty/surplus keys, aliases, annotated records and nominal identity. Predicates can fail to match without propagating their dynamic errors in the tested forms. No claim of complete declaration/import/package visibility, every composite pattern, generic JNode dispatch or earlier-profile promotion. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows. New manifest checks use default Legacy host and effective version4.0, hence frozen XPath40. Legacy3.0 declaration/pattern refusals are explicit. Host selection, module/package identity, imports and authoring contexts need their own applicable tests; no exhaustive cross-context claim follows. No engine behavior changes. ## 13. Sample Code [structural-binding.xsl](../examples/intake-types/structural-binding.xsl) returns true|false for converted versus original map. [enum-allowed](../examples/intake-types/enum-allowed.xsl) and [enum-rejected](../examples/intake-types/enum-rejected.xsl) distinguish allowed values. The complete report has normal, empty and reordered cases. ## 14. Performance Notes Cost follows the value/type/pattern being checked and any conversion/materialization. Field/member walks and predicates can add work; no benchmark, universal speedup or measured memory claim is supplied. ## 15. Known Uses [Xslt40ItemTypeTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40ItemTypeTests.cs) and [Xslt40StructuralRecordAliasTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40StructuralRecordAliasTests.cs); new intake-types enum/alias/structural rows. Missing @as and duplicates are explicit diagnostic controls. No new GatedSets membership; AC-03 remains partial. ## 16. experimental/fn-scan.md.text:
fn:scan

Catalog entry — Functions · Experimental

**C09 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-1.md) records 4 contract groups with exact sample/context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Verified bounded Experimental contract**. Experimental gate retry does not promote frozen API availability; no bounded-memory or general callback-conversion promise. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. **C06 host/profile review — 26 October 2026:** [Bounded reconciliation](../HOST-PROFILE-RECONCILIATION.md) maps this entry to current pinned instruction/host rules and named tests. Seven workpackages remain; instruction comparison, complete static-mode evidence and host/adoption limits remain explicit. No acceptance or profile promotion. Earlier notices remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **`fn:scan`** — **Experimental** (ships only at the `XPath40Experimental` level; static XPST0017 at both `XPath31` *and* frozen `XPath40`). Spec: F&O 4.0 §2.5.15, added by qt4cg Issue 2823 / PR 2824 (31 July 2026). Landed: REQ-123 S1 (1.1.0 track), level-plumbing slice 2026-10-09. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [F&O 4.0: fn:scan](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-scan). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. Draft evolution: [QT4CG PR #2824](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/pull/2824) records the scan proposal referenced by the adoption dossier. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #98](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/98), [immutable mainline revision `bd18e42f`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/bd18e42f33b5e69817f059f6429f4b08e639a5a3) (2026-10-09). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Return every intermediate accumulator of a left fold as a **sequence of single-member arrays**: `fn:scan($input, $init, $action)` yields `[$init]`, then `[$action($acc, $item, $pos)]` for each input item — N input items produce N+1 arrays. There is no additional outer array. ## 3. Also Known As "Prefix scan", "running fold". **Do not implement** `scan-left` / `scan-right`: those names never existed in the accepted draft — the pair was consolidated into the single left-fold `fn:scan` before stabilization (see [mapping-arrow-gtgt.md](../rejected/mapping-arrow-gtgt.md) for the sibling rename story). ## 4. History / Supersedes Supersedes hand-threaded accumulation of intermediate states in 3.1. The [complete stock-ledger baseline](../examples/fn-scan/before.xpath) uses `fold-left` and `array:append`; the [experimental case](../examples/fn-scan/main.xpath) uses `fn:scan`. Both display `100,120,85,95` for an opening stock of 100 units and movements of +20, -35, and +10. | Before (3.1) | After (4.0-Exp) | |---|---| | `fold-left($movements, [100], function($states, $delta) { array:append($states, $states(array:size($states)) + $delta) })` | `fn:scan($movements, 100, function($balance, $delta) { $balance + $delta })` | ## 5. Motivation Fold returns its final accumulator; stock ledgers and running totals need every intermediate state. A 3.1 fold must explicitly retain that history. Scan expresses the history requirement directly and includes the initial state for comparison. ## 6. Language Alignment Direct prior art: Haskell `scanl`, Clojure `reductions`, F# `Seq.scan`, Kotlin `runningFold`. Drift warning: XPath returns a **sequence of single-member arrays**, allowing each accumulator to hold a sequence without flattening it into the other states. Arity-2 callbacks receive accumulator and item only; the runtime can supply position to an arity-3 callback. ## 7. Applicability Use for: running aggregations, incremental derivations, anything where each input item emits a new accumulator state. Do **not** use for: anything that must compile at frozen `XPath40` or 3.1 (static XPST0017); final-state-only folds (`fn:fold-left` is clearer and one array shorter); unstable-surface intolerance — this function postdates the June-2026 churn line and its exact shape may still move. ## 8. Structure ``` fn:scan(input as item()*, init as item()*, action as fn(*)) as array(*)* ``` ## 9. Participants - `FunctionLibrary` — experimental-only signature template (`IsXPath40ExperimentalOnly`), invisible to `fn:function-lookup` / dynamic dispatch below the experimental level. - `EvaluationContext.IsXPath40Experimental` — runtime level flag. - Version gate (`XPath31Expression`) — static XPST0017 in call form *and* named-function-ref form at both lower levels. ## 10. Collaborations - The **experimental level plumbing** (REQ-123 S1) is the collaboration that matters: `fn:scan` was the first function gated exclusively to `XPath40Experimental`, and it established the template every later experimental addition follows (dedicated signature templates, lookup invisibility, call+ref static errors). - Destructuring `let` ([destructuring-let.md](../operators-and-syntax/destructuring-let.md)) is the natural consumer of each emitted single-member array's shape in surrounding code. ## 11. Consequences Benefits: direct expression of all intermediate states; the callback position parameter enables position-aware accumulations. Retaining the history requires storage for its states; no constant-memory guarantee is implied. Liabilities: **experimental-tier semantics may change as the draft moves** — the N+1 / single-member-array shape is precisely the kind of detail a WG review adjusts. Pin your usage to a Bosak version and re-run the qt4tests `fn-scan` set (if promoted by then) on upgrades. ## 12. Implementation **C04 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Expression/call/focus reconciliation](../EXPRESSION-CALL-FOCUS-RECONCILIATION.md) covers REQ123-scan. scan is Experimental-only in calls and lookup, with N+1 single-member-array states and empty input retaining the seed. Its existing gate retry is not frozen API promotion. No new function syntax or frozen promotion. C02 callback semantics and C06 host/profile ownership remain distinct from membership in GatedSets. This is bounded production/profile evidence, not full grammar or AC-04 acceptance. **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles N+1 accumulator states retain single-member array boundaries; Empty input retains the initial state; Position-aware callback; Experimental-only availability. **Boundaries:** No frozen-profile adoption or constant-memory guarantee; generic function coercion beyond verified callbacks is not certified. sections.2: Return every intermediate accumulator of a left fold as a **sequence of single-member arrays**: `fn:scan($input, $init, $action)` yields `[$init]`, then `[$action($acc, $item, $pos)]` for each input item — N input items produce N+1 arrays. There is no additional outer array.
sections.3: "Prefix scan", "running fold". **Do not implement** `scan-left` / `scan-right`: those names never existed in the accepted draft — the pair was consolidated into the single left-fold `fn:scan` before stabilization (see [mapping-arrow-gtgt.md](../rejected/mapping-arrow-gtgt.md) for the sibling rename story).
sections.4:
Supersedes hand-threaded accumulation of intermediate states in 3.1. The
[complete stock-ledger baseline](../examples/fn-scan/before.xpath) uses
`fold-left` and `array:append`; the [experimental case](../examples/fn-scan/main.xpath)
uses `fn:scan`. Both display `100,120,85,95` for an opening stock of 100 units
and movements of +20, -35, and +10.

| Before (3.1) | After (4.0-Exp) |
|---|---|
| `fold-left($movements, [100], function($states, $delta) { array:append($states, $states(array:size($states)) + $delta) })` | `fn:scan($movements, 100, function($balance, $delta) { $balance + $delta })` |
sections.5:
Fold returns its final accumulator; stock ledgers and running totals need every
intermediate state. A 3.1 fold must explicitly retain that history. Scan expresses
the history requirement directly and includes the initial state for comparison.
sections.6: Direct prior art: Haskell `scanl`, Clojure `reductions`, F# `Seq.scan`, Kotlin `runningFold`. Drift warning: XPath returns a **sequence of single-member arrays**, allowing each accumulator to hold a sequence without flattening it into the other states. Arity-2 callbacks receive accumulator and item only; the runtime can supply position to an arity-3 callback.
sections.7:
Use for: running aggregations, incremental derivations, anything where each input item emits a new accumulator state.

Do **not** use for: anything that must compile at frozen `XPath40` or 3.1 (static XPST0017); final-state-only folds (`fn:fold-left` is clearer and one array shorter); unstable-surface intolerance — this function postdates the June-2026 churn line and its exact shape may still move.

functions/atomic-equal.md.text:
Atomic equality

Practical reference: Frozen 4.0

**C09 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-1.md) records 3 contract groups with exact sample/context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited atomic equality contract**. Do not generalize to document/map deep equality or all comparator/type combinations. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Atomic equality** - **Frozen 4.0**. Delivery family: [REQ-118](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) / [REQ-123 registry](../../FEATURE_REQUESTS.md). Section provenance: See the linked REQ dossiers and implementation evidence. [Primary implementation evidence](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) records the shipped behavior; this entry adds executable user-facing examples under REQ-126, rather than announcing a new engine feature. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [fn:atomic-equal](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-atomic-equal). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #108](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/108), [immutable mainline revision `cbf7f88c`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/cbf7f88ce8364334040a819f96967622992f24a2) (2026-10-10). That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Make the equality policy for individual atomic values explicit, including NaN. ## 3. Also Known As Use the name and spelling in this entry and its executable files. Related functions or instruction forms are described in the primary test evidence; no additional alias is adopted here. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1, use type-specific comparisons and deliberate NaN handling. Compare the [complete earlier-version baseline](../examples/atomic-equal/before.xpath) with the [complete expression](../examples/atomic-equal/main.xpath). Both yield `true` for this synthetic input. They demonstrate this task, not universal equivalence of the two mechanisms. ## 5. Motivation A telemetry feed uses NaN for unavailable measurements and compares two snapshots. Make the equality policy for individual atomic values explicit, including NaN. Keeping this task explicit makes it possible to choose the feature for a practical reason and verify what the receiving application will see. ## 6. Language Alignment Read the behavior as XPath/XSLT semantics. Similar vocabulary in another programming language is not a compatibility promise. This is atomic-value equality, not document or map equality. Do not silently replace every general comparison with it. ## 7. Applicability Use this form when solving the stated task and the consumer permits the declared compatibility level. Keep the earlier baseline when the application requires 3.1 expressions or portable 3.0 stylesheets. This is atomic-value equality, not document or map equality. Do not silently replace every general comparison with it. ## 8. Structure ```xquery fn:atomic-equal(xs:double('NaN'), xs:double('NaN')) ``` This is the worked case's syntax, not a replacement for the full language grammar. Required namespaces and surrounding context are supplied in the linked complete files. ## 9. Participants XPath31Expression, CompileOptions, the parser/compiler, and the shared runtime/function library provide the public execution path. [Primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) identify the feature's implementation contract. The examples use public APIs only. ## 10. Collaborations The case combines source values, the named feature, and explicit output formatting. [Worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md) show how selection, construction, and business rejection fit into larger transformations. ## 11. Consequences Benefit: Make the equality policy for individual atomic values explicit, including NaN. Tradeoff: the declared compatibility level and edge rules become part of the consumer contract. This is atomic-value equality, not document or map equality. Do not silently replace every general comparison with it. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Atomic equality distinguishes value-family policy and NaN; Atomic input/type errors remain distinct from deep node/map equality. **Boundaries:** Representative atomic families only; do not generalize the sample to structural equality or every derived atomic type. Follow-up groups: F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Compile the after/edge expressions at XPathCompatibility.XPath40. The baseline uses XPath31. The example harness checks default-mode refusal for successful 4.0 cases; negative cases pin the declared error. See [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs): it executes the published files from the [case manifest](../examples/cases.json). This documentation slice changes no engine source. ## 13. Sample Code Input is synthetic and declared directly in the complete expression. The [complete expression](../examples/atomic-equal/main.xpath) yields `true`. The [edge case](../examples/atomic-equal/edge.xpath) yields `false`. No external resources or application variables are required. See the [example runner](../examples/README.md) for commands and host context. ## 14. Performance Notes Expected class: small scalar comparison overhead, including atomic type classification. It does not traverse a document tree. These are implementation expectations, not measured deltas. No benchmark is claimed; use the repository benchmark harness before making workload-specific speed or memory claims. ## 15. Known Uses Executable example IDs: `atomic-equal-main`, `atomic-equal-edge`, `atomic-equal-before` in `CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome`. Existing unit evidence: [primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). functions/batch-extrema.md.text:
Batch Extrema and Component Codes

Frozen 4.0 — changed existing-function contracts and observed limits

**C09 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-1.md) records 4 contract groups with exact sample/context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Blocked for full current-draft extrema parity**. C02-F06/F08: current mixed-type selection/identity and plain-duration ordering are not fully implemented. Original observed fixtures remain observations. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification [fn:min](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-min) and [fn:max](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-max) already exist in XPath 3.1. Their changed 4.0 contracts are outside the 117-name inventory of 4.0-only functions. Bosak's QName extension was delivered in [PR #114](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/114), [33894747](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/33894747f04da970a1f3c0f17fa960fa1f620605). Reviewed 2026-10-12 against immutable [QT4CG F&O source e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This review does not recover the historical adopted draft. ## 2. Intent Report a quality-control batch's accepted decimal range and the endpoints of its namespace-aware component-code inventory. Preserve rejected row identifiers and make empty batches explicit. ## 3. Also Known As Minimum, maximum and extrema describe these functions. Component-code endpoints are namespace/local-name ordering, not a severity ranking or business priority. ## 4. History / Supersedes The stable [3.1 min](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions-31/#func-min) and [3.1 max](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions-31/#func-max) contracts use numeric promotion and a narrower set of orderable types. The reviewed 4.0 draft compares converted values through the broader `fn:compare` ordering and returns a selected converted input value. Bosak adds QName extrema, but its shared numeric and duration paths retain earlier behavior. The 3.1 report below uses explicit namespace/local-name folds instead of calling extrema on QNames. ## 5. Motivation Imported readings need a useful range without allowing malformed values to silently become NaN. Namespaced component codes also need a deterministic index boundary independent of the XML prefix chosen by a sender. Both tasks benefit from explicit conversion and ordering policies. ## 6. Language Alignment Bosak registers one- and two-argument forms of both functions. Empty input returns an empty sequence. Untyped atomic values are converted to doubles; explicitly supplied strings remain strings. Thus untyped XML numbers `2` and `10` have a numeric range, while string values `'2'` and `'10'` have a lexical range. Numeric NaN contaminates either extreme; the application must screen it when missing measurements should be excluded. Mixing number and string raises `FORG0006` in these fixtures. QNames are ordered by namespace URI and then local name in codepoint order. Prefixes do not determine ordering. Equivalent QNames may carry different prefixes, so the report prints expanded names rather than asserting a chosen prefix. The draft leaves the chosen representative of equal extrema unspecified. The second argument selects string collation. Bosak accepts the demonstrated empty-collation form in both profiles; only the 4.0 draft's default-on-empty contract is claimed. Complete synthetic input:


### XPath 4.0 report

[Runnable file](../examples/batch-extrema/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $rows := parse-xml('<batch xmlns:q="urn:qa:codes" xmlns:e="urn:erp:codes"><reading id="A" value="2.5" code="q:low"/><reading id="B" value="7.5" code="q:high"/><reading id="C" value="5" code="e:normal"/><reading id="D" value="invalid" code="q:invalid"/><reading id="E" value="" code="q:missing"/></batch>')/batch/reading
return let $valid := $rows[@value castable as xs:decimal]
return let $invalid := $rows[not(@value castable as xs:decimal)]
return let $values := $valid/@value ! xs:decimal(.)
return let $codes := $rows ! resolve-QName(string(@code), .)
return let $label := function($q) { if (empty($q)) then '-' else concat('Q{', namespace-uri-from-QName($q), '}', local-name-from-QName($q)) }
return let $first := min($codes)
return let $last := max($codes)
return let $low := min($values)
return let $high := max($values)
return concat('accepted=', string-join($valid/@id, ','), '; rejected=', string-join($invalid/@id, ','), '; min=', if (empty($low)) then '-' else string($low), '; max=', if (empty($high)) then '-' else string($high), '; first-code=', $label($first), '; last-code=', $label($last))
```

```text
accepted=A,B,C; rejected=D,E; min=2.5; max=7.5; first-code=Q{urn:erp:codes}normal; last-code=Q{urn:qa:codes}missing
```

A, B and C supply valid decimals; D and E remain rejected identifiers. The ERP

name. This explains the code endpoints without assigning a business rank.

### XPath 3.1 comparison

[Runnable file](../examples/batch-extrema/baseline.xpath):

```xpath

return let $valid := $rows[@value castable as xs:decimal]
return let $invalid := $rows[not(@value castable as xs:decimal)]
return let $values := $valid/@value ! xs:decimal(.)
return let $codes := $rows ! resolve-QName(string(@code), .)
return let $label := function($q) { if (empty($q)) then '-' else concat('Q{', namespace-uri-from-QName($q), '}', local-name-from-QName($q)) }
return let $cp := 'http://www.w3.org/2005/xpath-functions/collation/codepoint'
return let $less := function($a, $b) {
  let $ns := compare(namespace-uri-from-QName($a), namespace-uri-from-QName($b), $cp)
  return if ($ns eq 0) then compare(local-name-from-QName($a), local-name-from-QName($b), $cp) lt 0 else $ns lt 0
}
return let $first := fold-left($codes, (), function($best, $next) { if (empty($best)) then $next else if ($less($next, $best)) then $next else $best })
return let $last := fold-left($codes, (), function($best, $next) { if (empty($best)) then $next else if ($less($best, $next)) then $next else $best })
return let $low := min($values)
return let $high := max($values)
return concat('accepted=', string-join($valid/@id, ','), '; rejected=', string-join($invalid/@id, ','), '; min=', if (empty($low)) then '-' else string($low), '; max=', if (empty($high)) then '-' else string($high), '; first-code=', $label($first), '; last-code=', $label($last))
```

Exact output:

```text
accepted=A,B,C; rejected=D,E; min=2.5; max=7.5; first-code=Q{urn:erp:codes}normal; last-code=Q{urn:qa:codes}missing
```

The fold comparator performs two comparisons, preserving the namespace/local-name
ordering even when one namespace URI is a prefix of another. The numeric part
uses the same explicit decimal normalization policy as the 4.0 report.

functions/bounded-retries.md.text:
Bounded Retry State

Frozen 4.0 — precondition and postcondition loops with an attempt budget

**C09 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-1.md) records 4 contract groups with exact sample/context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Verified finite callback contract**. No automatic delay, timeout, retry ceiling or unbounded termination guarantee. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Bounded retry state — Frozen 4.0.** [fn:while-do](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-while-do) and [fn:do-until](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-do-until). Initial engine delivery: [PR #88](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/88), [revision 0a928bb8](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/0a928bb81b81d0631cc681f86bba83259c0ed790), REQ-118 4.0-S5. Definitions reviewed **2026-10-11** against immutable [QT4CG function source a014e1b4](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This review pin does not recover the unavailable historical adopted specification snapshot. ## 2. Intent Advance an invoice-submission state until it is accepted or its attempt budget is consumed. Keep the status, attempt count and response history visible in the result so acceptance can be distinguished from budget exhaustion. ## 3. Also Known As Precondition loop (`while-do`) and postcondition loop (`do-until`). These are explanatory terms, not alternative function names. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 can carry state through a bounded `fold-left`, skipping updates after acceptance. The complete comparison below returns the same report for the illustrated responses. It still visits every position in the fixed range; it is not a general early-terminating loop. Recursive helper functions are another option in a host language that supports named function declarations. ## 5. Motivation Electronic invoice gateways commonly acknowledge a submission before later reporting acceptance. An application must stop checking once accepted and must also stop when its configured attempt budget is used. Treating exhausted attempts as success would hide invoices still awaiting acceptance. The fixture uses recorded responses to make that state transition reproducible. ## 6. Language Alignment `while-do($input, $predicate, $action)` tests the current value before updating it. False or empty returns that value immediately; true calls the action and repeats with the new value. Position starts at one and increments after an action. `do-until($input, $action, $predicate)` always calls the action first, then tests its new value using the same position. True returns it; false or empty repeats at the next position. Note the opposite meanings of a true predicate and the opposite callback argument order. Both callbacks receive the **whole current `item()*` value**, not individual members of a sequence. Actions may return any sequence, including empty. Predicates return `xs:boolean?`; a status string is not a boolean and raises XPTY0004. Callback arguments must be callable. The examples use two-argument inline functions to show both state and position explicitly. ## 7. Applicability Use for repeated pure state transformations with a clear stopping condition. The sample assumes a nonnegative integer attempt limit, starts attempts at zero, and recognizes only `accepted` as success. Missing response/status is normalized to `pending`; other statuses remain unsuccessful and consume the budget. A production integration should separately classify permanent rejection and validate gateway responses according to its own protocol. The XPath consumes an already supplied response fixture. The host application owns actual requests, idempotency keys, persistence, timeouts, delays and any backoff policy. Here an attempt means one recorded status check; it does not mean resubmitting the invoice. No network request or sleep occurs in the expression. ## 8. Structure A state map contains `attempts`, `status` and a sequence-valued `trace`. The action reads the response at the current one-based position and constructs a replacement map. The predicate combines status with the finite attempt limit. The final report exposes acceptance or exhaustion independently. ## 9. Participants The submission fixture provides ordered responses. The initial state supplies an empty trace and zero attempts. The action advances state. The predicate owns the stopping rule. The report presents the final state for the caller. ## 10. Collaborations For `while-do`, continue while not accepted **and** below the limit. For `do-until`, stop when accepted **or** at the limit. An outer zero-budget guard is essential for `do-until`, because the function itself always runs its action. The initially-accepted cases show why replacing one form with the other can change behavior: `while-do` does nothing, whereas `do-until` performs a new check. ## 11. Consequences A finite budget plus an action that increments attempts guarantees termination for these fixtures, even if no response ever reports acceptance. The loops have no implicit maximum iteration count or delay. An unchanged state with a predicate that never stops could run indefinitely; every runnable case here has a bound or a predicate that terminates on its first call. Exceptions propagate; the functions do not automatically convert them into retryable outcomes. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Before-versus-after predicate timing and callback argument order; Whole-sequence state, one-based iteration positions and empty results; Boolean/empty predicate result, callback errors and finite example termination. **Boundaries:** No implicit timeout, retry delay or iteration ceiling; only bounded terminating examples are supplied. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Compile the new function calls with `CompileOptions.Compatibility40`. The default 3.1 profile rejects them; compile the `fold-left` comparison with `Compatibility31`. The existing [catalog harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) verifies exact result strings, exception-message markers and default-profile refusal for successful 4.0 cases. The custom `ATTEMPT` fixture includes that code in its description: it verifies message propagation, not typed error-code metadata. All inputs are inline; no variables, context item or external files are needed. ## 13. Sample Code Complete synthetic input: a gateway status-check sequence for invoice INV-2048. The third response remains unread because the second response is accepted. ```xml ``` ### Test before the action [Runnable while-do expression](../examples/bounded-retries/while-main.xpath): ```xpath let $responses := parse-xml('')/submission/response let $limit := 3 let $initial := map {'attempts': 0, 'status': 'pending', 'trace': ()} let $advance := function($state, $position) { let $status := string(($responses[$position]/@status, 'pending')[1]) return map {'attempts': $state?attempts + 1, 'status': $status, 'trace': ($state?trace, $status)} } let $final := while-do($initial, function($state, $position) { $state?status ne 'accepted' and $state?attempts lt $limit }, $advance) return concat('status=', $final?status, '; attempts=', $final?attempts, '; exhausted=', $final?status ne 'accepted' and $final?attempts ge $limit, '; trace=', string-join($final?trace, ',')) ``` Exact output: ```text status=accepted; attempts=2; exhausted=false; trace=pending,accepted ``` ### Test after the action [Runnable do-until expression](../examples/bounded-retries/until-main.xpath): ```xpath let $responses := parse-xml('')/submission/response let $limit := 3 let $initial := map {'attempts': 0, 'status': 'pending', 'trace': ()} let $advance := function($state, $position) { let $status := string(($responses[$position]/@status, 'pending')[1]) return map {'attempts': $state?attempts + 1, 'status': $status, 'trace': ($state?trace, $status)} } let $final := if ($limit le 0) then $initial else do-until($initial, $advance, function($state, $position) { $state?status eq 'accepted' or $state?attempts ge $limit }) return concat('status=', $final?status, '; attempts=', $final?attempts, '; exhausted=', $final?status ne 'accepted' and $final?attempts ge $limit, '; trace=', string-join($final?trace, ',')) ``` Exact output: ```text status=accepted; attempts=2; exhausted=false; trace=pending,accepted ``` ### XPath 3.1 comparison [Runnable bounded fold](../examples/bounded-retries/baseline.xpath): ```xpath let $responses := parse-xml('')/submission/response return let $limit := 3 return let $initial := map {'attempts': 0, 'status': 'pending', 'trace': ()} return let $advance := function($state, $position) { let $status := string(($responses[$position]/@status, 'pending')[1]) return map {'attempts': $state?attempts + 1, 'status': $status, 'trace': ($state?trace, $status)} } return let $final := fold-left(1 to $limit, $initial, function($state, $position) { if ($state?status eq 'accepted') then $state else $advance($state, $position) }) return concat('status=', $final?status, '; attempts=', $final?attempts, '; exhausted=', $final?status ne 'accepted' and $final?attempts ge $limit, '; trace=', string-join($final?trace, ',')) ``` Exact output: ```text status=accepted; attempts=2; exhausted=false; trace=pending,accepted ``` ### Exhausted budget Replace the accepted response with pending. Complete input: ```xml ``` Both [while-do](../examples/bounded-retries/while-exhausted.xpath) and [do-until](../examples/bounded-retries/until-exhausted.xpath) report: ```text status=pending; attempts=3; exhausted=true; trace=pending,pending,pending ``` ### All boundary and callback fixtures Every file embeds its full input and each report below is exact. | Runnable case | Result or diagnostic marker | |---|---| | [while-main](../examples/bounded-retries/while-main.xpath) | `status=accepted; attempts=2; exhausted=false; trace=pending,accepted` | | [until-main](../examples/bounded-retries/until-main.xpath) | `status=accepted; attempts=2; exhausted=false; trace=pending,accepted` | | [baseline](../examples/bounded-retries/baseline.xpath) | `status=accepted; attempts=2; exhausted=false; trace=pending,accepted` | | [while-exhausted](../examples/bounded-retries/while-exhausted.xpath) | `status=pending; attempts=3; exhausted=true; trace=pending,pending,pending` | | [while-one-attempt](../examples/bounded-retries/while-one-attempt.xpath) | `status=pending; attempts=1; exhausted=true; trace=pending` | | [while-zero-budget](../examples/bounded-retries/while-zero-budget.xpath) | `status=pending; attempts=0; exhausted=true; trace=` | | [while-missing-status](../examples/bounded-retries/while-missing-status.xpath) | `status=accepted; attempts=2; exhausted=false; trace=pending,accepted` | | [until-exhausted](../examples/bounded-retries/until-exhausted.xpath) | `status=pending; attempts=3; exhausted=true; trace=pending,pending,pending` | | [until-one-attempt](../examples/bounded-retries/until-one-attempt.xpath) | `status=pending; attempts=1; exhausted=true; trace=pending` | | [until-zero-budget](../examples/bounded-retries/until-zero-budget.xpath) | `status=pending; attempts=0; exhausted=true; trace=` | | [until-missing-status](../examples/bounded-retries/until-missing-status.xpath) | `status=accepted; attempts=2; exhausted=false; trace=pending,accepted` | | [while-initially-accepted](../examples/bounded-retries/while-initially-accepted.xpath) | `status=accepted; attempts=0; exhausted=false; trace=` | | [until-initially-accepted](../examples/bounded-retries/until-initially-accepted.xpath) | `status=accepted; attempts=2; exhausted=false; trace=pending,accepted` | | [while-empty-decision](../examples/bounded-retries/while-empty-decision.xpath) | `0` | | [until-empty-decision](../examples/bounded-retries/until-empty-decision.xpath) | `2` | | [until-empty-state](../examples/bounded-retries/until-empty-state.xpath) | `1,2` | | [while-sequence-state](../examples/bounded-retries/while-sequence-state.xpath) | `1,2,3,4` | | [while-nonboolean](../examples/bounded-retries/while-nonboolean.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | | [while-noncallable-action](../examples/bounded-retries/while-noncallable-action.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | | [while-noncallable-predicate](../examples/bounded-retries/while-noncallable-predicate.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | | [while-action-error](../examples/bounded-retries/while-action-error.xpath) | `ATTEMPT` | | [until-nonboolean](../examples/bounded-retries/until-nonboolean.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | | [until-noncallable-action](../examples/bounded-retries/until-noncallable-action.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | | [until-noncallable-predicate](../examples/bounded-retries/until-noncallable-predicate.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | | [until-action-error](../examples/bounded-retries/until-action-error.xpath) | `ATTEMPT` | A zero budget reports exhausted without performing a check. A budget of one stops after pending. An initially accepted state stays unchanged with `while-do`, but the `do-until` variant consumes pending then accepted responses. A missing first status uses pending and still reaches acceptance on attempt two. The sequence-state fixtures prove that callbacks receive the whole sequence; the empty-state fixture proves that empty input does not skip a do-until action. An empty decision stops while-do immediately but continues do-until until its second, true decision. Nonboolean/noncallable fixtures raise XPTY0004; an action exception propagates without being retried automatically. ## 14. Performance The main expressions perform at most the configured number of actions and stop early on acceptance. They are synchronous state transformations, with no built-in scheduling or wait. The trace grows with completed attempts and keeps those statuses in memory. The bounded 3.1 fold visits all budget positions even after acceptance, while avoiding further action calls. No benchmark or general streaming claim is implied. ## 15. Known Uses This is a synthetic reference workflow, not a claim about a particular deployed gateway. Existing unit evidence includes [`WhileDo_PredicateInitiallyFalse_NeverCallsAction`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`WhileDo_WholeSequenceIsTheValue`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`WhileDo_PositionIncrementsFromOne`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`WhileDo_EmptyPredicateResultMeansFalse`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`WhileDo_ActionError_Propagates`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`DoUntil_ActionEvaluatedBeforePredicate`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`DoUntil_EmptyInput_StillRunsAction`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), and [`DoUntil_PositionIncrementsFromOne`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs). The [4.0 gate runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs) assigns both exact sets `fn-while-do` and `fn-do-until` to GatedSets. This documentation delivery changes no gate membership. ## 16. Related Features [Ordered queue prefix](ordered-queue-prefix.md) stops sequence selection at a boundary; these loops repeatedly replace an entire state value instead. [Higher-order selection](higher-order-selection.md) describes callback-based selection. [The completeness audit](../COMPLETENESS-AUDIT.md) records coverage limits and the remaining dependency traversal and partial-application families.

Complete synthetic input: a gateway status-check sequence for invoice INV-2048.
The third response remains unread because the second response is accepted.

```xml
<submission id="INV-2048">
  <response status="pending"/>
  <response status="accepted"/>
  <response status="pending"/>
</submission>
```

### Test before the action

[Runnable while-do expression](../examples/bounded-retries/while-main.xpath):

```xpath
let $responses := parse-xml('<submission id="INV-2048"><response status="pending"/><response status="accepted"/><response status="pending"/></submission>')/submission/response
let $limit := 3
let $initial := map {'attempts': 0, 'status': 'pending', 'trace': ()}
let $advance := function($state, $position) {
  let $status := string(($responses[$position]/@status, 'pending')[1])
  return map {'attempts': $state?attempts + 1,
              'status': $status,
              'trace': ($state?trace, $status)}
}
let $final := while-do($initial, function($state, $position) { $state?status ne 'accepted' and $state?attempts lt $limit }, $advance)
return concat('status=', $final?status, '; attempts=', $final?attempts, '; exhausted=', $final?status ne 'accepted' and $final?attempts ge $limit, '; trace=', string-join($final?trace, ','))
```

```text
status=accepted; attempts=2; exhausted=false; trace=pending,accepted
```

```xpath
  return map {'attempts': $state?attempts + 1,
              'status': $status,
              'trace': ($state?trace, $status)}
}
let $final := if ($limit le 0) then $initial else do-until($initial, $advance, function($state, $position) { $state?status eq 'accepted' or $state?attempts ge $limit })
return concat('status=', $final?status, '; attempts=', $final?attempts, '; exhausted=', $final?status ne 'accepted' and $final?attempts ge $limit, '; trace=', string-join($final?trace, ','))
```

A zero budget reports exhausted without performing a check. A budget of one
stops after pending. An initially accepted state stays unchanged with `while-do`,
but the `do-until` variant consumes pending then accepted responses. A missing
first status uses pending and still reaches acceptance on attempt two.
The sequence-state fixtures prove that callbacks receive the whole sequence;
the empty-state fixture proves that empty input does not skip a do-until action.
An empty decision stops while-do immediately but continues do-until until its
second, true decision. Nonboolean/noncallable fixtures raise XPTY0004; an action
exception propagates without being retried automatically.
sections.14:
The main expressions perform at most the configured number of actions and
stop early on acceptance. They are synchronous state transformations, with no
built-in scheduling or wait. The trace grows with completed attempts and keeps
those statuses in memory. The bounded 3.1 fold visits all budget positions even
after acceptance, while avoiding further action calls. No benchmark or general
streaming claim is implied.

functions/configured-label-callbacks.md.text:
Configured Label Callbacks

Frozen 4.0 — bind policy arguments and pass through unchanged values

**C09 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-1.md) records 4 contract groups with exact sample/context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited frozen binding / draft adoption boundary**. C02-F01/F02/F08: ignored nonpositive draft keys remain unmet; metadata-dependent conversion timing is not universally eager. No exact fn-partial-apply gate. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Configured label callbacks — Frozen 4.0.** [fn:partial-apply](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-partial-apply) and [fn:identity](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-identity). Initial engine delivery: [PR #88](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/88), [revision 0a928bb8](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/0a928bb81b81d0631cc681f86bba83259c0ed790), REQ-118 4.0-S5. Definitions reviewed **2026-10-11** against immutable [QT4CG function source a014e1b4](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This review pin does not recover the unavailable historical adopted specification snapshot. The original identity registration follow-up is [eedcb321](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/eedcb321848ff7e9381c34fd72cb42db4994992f). ## 2. Intent Configure a shipping-label formatter once by binding its prefix and case policy, then reuse the resulting one-argument callback for every customer name. Use an identity callback when already formatted labels should pass through unchanged. ## 3. Also Known As Argument binding and a pass-through callback describe the two operations. They introduce no function aliases. Partial application binds selected arguments; it does not execute the formatter at binding time. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 supports placeholder partial application: `$format('SHIP: ', ?, true())`. The complete comparison below produces the same callback and report. The 4.0 function accepts a runtime map of argument positions without requiring a statically known arity, and can bind every argument to produce a zero-argument function. The earlier identity equivalent is `function($value) { $value }`. ## 5. Motivation A dispatch batch can share a label prefix and capitalization rule while each record supplies a different name. Passing all configuration arguments on every call obscures that fixed policy. Binding policy values exposes a simple callback that fits `for-each`. An identity callback lets the same processing stage accept already formatted labels without changing their content. ## 6. Language Alignment `partial-apply($function, $arguments)` takes a callable and a map with positive integer keys identifying **one-based** argument positions. Unbound parameters retain their original relative order. Binding all parameters gives arity zero; an empty map returns the original callable. Keys beyond the function's arity are ignored, rather than reporting a misspelled configuration position. String, zero and negative keys raise XPTY0004 in the demonstrated cases. Maps and arrays are callable too, and can have their single lookup argument bound. Supplied values undergo function conversion when parameter metadata permits. Some Bosak built-ins lack that metadata; their conversion errors may surface when the resulting function is invoked. The bound-type-error fixture exercises that call, rather than claiming all validation happens eagerly. `identity($input)` returns the same `item()*` value, including an empty sequence, a whole sequence or a container. For nodes it preserves identity, rather than copying. `identity#1` supplies a function item where a callback is required. ## 7. Applicability Use for reusable callbacks configured by runtime policy, or for binding all arguments into a deferred zero-argument call. A fixed, statically known function may be clearer with 3.1 placeholders. Validate configuration positions separately if silently ignored high keys would hide errors. The label case assumes nonempty customer names validated upstream. It normalizes whitespace and applies a simple uppercase policy; it is not a postal-address validator or a complete label layout. ## 8. Structure The base formatter has parameters `(prefix, name, uppercase)`. Binding positions one and three leaves `(name)`, which `for-each` calls for each supplied name. The formatter returns a text label. The optional pass-through stage uses `identity#1` for labels already prepared by an earlier stage. ## 9. Participants Customer attributes provide names. A configuration map supplies fixed argument values. The base formatter implements policy. The bound callback is reused by `for-each`. Identity supplies unchanged values in the alternative stage. ## 10. Collaborations Construct the bound callback outside the per-customer loop. Leave the varying name argument unbound, and check `function-arity` to make that contract explicit. If only the middle name argument is bound, the remaining callback parameters are `(prefix, uppercase)`, in that order. Bind every argument for a deferred call and invoke it with `()` to obtain the label. ## 11. Consequences Policy becomes explicit and reusable. Binding creates a callable, not its final result; invoking it performs formatting. Identity preserves values without normalization or validation. For node values it preserves the original node, and for maps/arrays it does not flatten their contents. No shipping action or file output occurs in these expressions. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles One-based binding, residual argument order, all-bound and empty-map identity; Callable maps/arrays and bound-value conversion; String/nonpositive/out-of-arity key boundaries in the released profile. **Boundaries:** Current draft permits nonpositive integer keys and ignores them; the frozen positive-key refusal remains explicit. Follow-up groups: F01, F02, F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Compile new calls with `CompileOptions.Compatibility40`; default XPath 3.1 rejects them. The placeholder and inline-identity comparisons use `Compatibility31`. The existing [catalog harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) checks exact report/error markers and default-profile refusal for successful 4.0 fixtures. The source and customer inputs are complete, inline expressions. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** [URI/import utility review](../URI-UTILITY-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md), pinned to F&O e7ee4ab8, and [detailed import/link README](../examples/utility-contracts/README.md) supply 105 checks across five families: keyword modes, component/options/escaping, one-pass UTF-8 decoding, collation availability, identity, NaN and type/cardinality boundaries, plus complete XPath 3.1/4.0 reports. Keywords remain unavailable. Boolean-option/record tolerance and empty query-map precedence remain follow-ups. All 37 absent-keyword families now have first targeted review, with metadata still absent; this does not close D2. Source/public version is 1.1.3; original delivery/unit/gate and historical adopted-pin limits remain. ## 13. Sample Code Full synthetic dispatch input: ```xml ``` [Complete XPath 4.0 formatter](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/main.xpath): ```xpath let $names := parse-xml('')/dispatch/customer/@name ! string(.) let $format := function($prefix, $name, $uppercase) { concat($prefix, if ($uppercase) then upper-case(normalize-space($name)) else normalize-space($name)) } let $label := partial-apply($format, map {1: 'SHIP: ', 3: true()}) return concat('arity=', function-arity($label), '; labels=', string-join(for-each($names, $label), ' | ')) ``` Exact output: ```text arity=1; labels=SHIP: ADA | SHIP: GRACE ``` [Complete XPath 3.1 placeholder comparison](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/baseline.xpath): ```xpath let $names := parse-xml('')/dispatch/customer/@name ! string(.) return let $format := function($prefix, $name, $uppercase) { concat($prefix, if ($uppercase) then upper-case(normalize-space($name)) else normalize-space($name)) } return let $label := $format('SHIP: ', ?, true()) return concat('arity=', function-arity($label), '; labels=', string-join(for-each($names, $label), ' | ')) ``` Exact output: ```text arity=1; labels=SHIP: ADA | SHIP: GRACE ``` ### Already formatted labels [Complete pass-through expression](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/identity-labels.xpath): ```xpath let $labels := ('SHIP: ADA', 'SHIP: GRACE') return string-join(for-each($labels, identity#1), ' | ') ``` Exact output: ```text SHIP: ADA | SHIP: GRACE ``` The [3.1 identity callback comparison](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/identity-baseline.xpath) uses `function($label) { $label }` and produces the identical output. ### Complete fixture inventory Each file supplies its complete input and exact report or error marker. | Runnable case | Exact result or diagnostic marker | |---|---| | [main](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/main.xpath) | `arity=1; labels=SHIP: ADA | SHIP: GRACE` | | [baseline](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/baseline.xpath) | `arity=1; labels=SHIP: ADA | SHIP: GRACE` | | [preserve-case](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/preserve-case.xpath) | `arity=1; labels=SHIP: Ada | SHIP: Grace` | | [empty-input](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/empty-input.xpath) | `arity=1; labels=` | | [all-bound](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/all-bound.xpath) | `arity=0; label=SHIP: ADA` | | [empty-bindings](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/empty-bindings.xpath) | `arity=3; label=SHIP: ADA` | | [remaining-order](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/remaining-order.xpath) | `arity=2; label=PICK: Ada` | | [ignored-high-key](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/ignored-high-key.xpath) | `arity=1; labels=SHIP: ADA | SHIP: GRACE` | | [bound-sequence](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/bound-sequence.xpath) | `FRAME+MOTOR` | | [callable-map](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/callable-map.xpath) | `ready` | | [callable-array](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/callable-array.xpath) | `express` | | [string-key](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/string-key.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | | [zero-key](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/zero-key.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | | [negative-key](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/negative-key.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | | [noncallable](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/noncallable.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | | [bound-type-error](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/bound-type-error.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | | [identity-labels](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/identity-labels.xpath) | `SHIP: ADA | SHIP: GRACE` | | [identity-baseline](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/identity-baseline.xpath) | `SHIP: ADA | SHIP: GRACE` | | [identity-empty](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/identity-empty.xpath) | `0` | | [identity-node](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/identity-node.xpath) | `true` | | [identity-sequence](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/identity-sequence.xpath) | `FRAME,MOTOR` | | [identity-container](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/identity-container.xpath) | `true` | The case-preserving fixture binds `false()` and retains Ada/Grace capitalization. The empty dispatch fixture reports arity one and no labels. The all-bound fixture produces arity zero and one label when invoked. The remaining-order fixture binds Ada and calls the remaining `(prefix, uppercase)` parameters. The high-key fixture shows that position 99 is ignored. Sequence-valued bindings remain a single argument value, as the FRAME+MOTOR string-join example verifies. Identity cases cover empty, sequence, node and nested-container values. ## 14. Performance Bind configuration once and reuse the resulting function. Bosak captures bound argument values in a wrapper; this is not a memoization cache for formatter results. Label work still occurs on each invocation. Identity returns its supplied value unchanged. No benchmark or allocation-free pipeline claim follows from these examples. ## 15. Known Uses This batch-label workflow is a reproducible synthetic example. Existing evidence includes [`PartialApply_InlineFunctionBase`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`PartialApply_EmptyMap_ReturnsFunctionUnchanged`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`PartialApply_BindingAllArguments_YieldsZeroArityFunction`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`PartialApply_KeysBeyondArity_AreIgnored`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`PartialApply_ArrayAsFunction`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`PartialApply_BoundValueCoercion_FailsAtCallTimeWhenNoTypeMetadata`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`PartialApply_NonIntegerKey_RaisesXpty0004`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), and [`Identity_ReturnsArgumentUnchanged`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs). The [4.0 runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs) assigns exact `fn-identity` to GatedSets; no exact `fn-partial-apply` set is assigned. These 22 executable fixtures and named tests provide separate evidence. No gate membership changes are included. ## 16. Related Features [Higher-order selection](higher-order-selection.md) describes consumers of callbacks. [Product dependency closure](product-dependency-closure.md) applies a captured resolver callback to graph nodes. [Bounded retry state](bounded-retries.md) uses two-argument state callbacks. [The completeness audit](../COMPLETENESS-AUDIT.md) tracks remaining names, separate from exhaustive signature coverage.

sections.13:
Full synthetic dispatch input:

```xml
<dispatch>
  <customer name="  Ada  "/>
  <customer name="Grace"/>
</dispatch>
```

[Complete XPath 4.0 formatter](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $names := parse-xml('<dispatch><customer name="  Ada  "/><customer name="Grace"/></dispatch>')/dispatch/customer/@name ! string(.)
let $format := function($prefix, $name, $uppercase) { concat($prefix, if ($uppercase) then upper-case(normalize-space($name)) else normalize-space($name)) }
let $label := partial-apply($format, map {1: 'SHIP: ', 3: true()})
return concat('arity=', function-arity($label), '; labels=', string-join(for-each($names, $label), ' | '))
```

Exact output:

```text
arity=1; labels=SHIP: ADA | SHIP: GRACE
```

[Complete XPath 3.1 placeholder comparison](../examples/configured-label-callbacks/baseline.xpath):

```xpath
let $names := parse-xml('<dispatch><customer name="  Ada  "/><customer name="Grace"/></dispatch>')/dispatch/customer/@name ! string(.)

return let $label := $format('SHIP: ', ?, true())
return concat('arity=', function-arity($label), '; labels=', string-join(for-each($names, $label), ' | '))
```

```text

```

