functions/consecutive-partition.md.text:
Consecutive partitioning

Frozen 4.0

**C09 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-1.md) records 3 contract groups with exact sample/context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Verified bounded consecutive partition contract**. No arbitrary callback conversion or stable grouping after prefiltering guarantee. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Consecutive partitioning — Frozen 4.0.** [Bosak PR #88](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/88) / [immutable revision `0a928bb8`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/0a928bb81b81d0631cc681f86bba83259c0ed790). This is the shipped engine delivery. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [fn:partition](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-partition). Historical adopted specification source revision was not retained; this remains an explicit provenance gap. ## 2. Intent Split a dispatch queue into bounded batches while preserving arrival order. ## 3. Also Known As Use the exact spellings in the linked examples; no undocumented aliases are adopted. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 requires explicit recursion or stateful grouping logic to split at a boundary depending on the current partition. Grouping by route would merge nonadjacent orders, so it is not a semantics-preserving replacement for consecutive partitioning. partition returns a sequence of arrays. Its split callback receives the current nonempty partition sequence, next item and one-based input position. A true result starts the next partition before that item. Empty input returns no partitions; a singleton returns one array and the callback is not invoked for its first item. The worked chapter combines capacity and route-change boundaries. ## 5. Motivation Split a dispatch queue into bounded batches while preserving arrival order. The order-routing chapter places validation before dispatch so rejected records stay available for repair. ## 6. Language Alignment This is consecutive splitting, not SQL GROUP BY and not a two-way accepted/rejected partition. Nonadjacent equal routes remain separate; filtering before splitting changes which boundaries are visible. ## 7. Applicability Use when the consumer opts into XPath40 and needs the exact validation or ordering contract described here. Keep the XPath 3.1 baseline when that opt-in is unavailable. ## 8. Structure ```xquery string-join(partition(('NORTH','NORTH','NORTH','SOUTH','NORTH'), function($current,$next,$position) { count($current) ge 2 or $current[1] ne $next }) ! string-join(?*, ','), '|') ``` This complete expression demonstrates the stated contract, not the full grammar. ## 9. Participants The public XPath API compiles at the manifest mode and evaluates without application variables. The routing chapter additionally supplies an XML document context. ## 10. Collaborations The routing planner passes an XDM map to portable XSLT through a required parameter. See [the full chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md). ## 11. Consequences partition returns a sequence of arrays. Its split callback receives the current nonempty partition sequence, next item and one-based input position. A true result starts the next partition before that item. Empty input returns no partitions; a singleton returns one array and the callback is not invoked for its first item. The worked chapter combines capacity and route-change boundaries. This is consecutive splitting, not SQL GROUP BY and not a two-way accepted/rejected partition. Nonadjacent equal routes remain separate; filtering before splitting changes which boundaries are visible. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Consecutive partition arrays preserve source order and nonadjacent groups; Split callback receives current partition, next item and original one-based position; Empty/singleton input avoids unnecessary predicate invocation. **Boundaries:** Not SQL grouping or a two-way filter; callback conversion beyond the tested signature remains a separate boundary. Follow-up groups: F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) runs the exact files, asserts declared results/errors, and checks default-3.1 refusal for successful 4.0 forms. No engine code changes or conformance promotions are included. ## 13. Sample Code [main.xpath](../examples/consecutive-partition/main.xpath): returns `NORTH,NORTH|NORTH|SOUTH|NORTH` at mode 40. [edge.xpath](../examples/consecutive-partition/edge.xpath): returns `0` at mode 40. [singleton.xpath](../examples/consecutive-partition/singleton.xpath): returns `1` at mode 40. ## 14. Performance Notes Duplicate checks and index selection may traverse the input; some/every may finish early. Partitioning creates arrays and retains input items. These are qualitative expectations, not benchmark results. Stateful or expensive callbacks change workload costs. ## 15. Known Uses Executable IDs: `consecutive-partition-main`, `consecutive-partition-edge`, `consecutive-partition-singleton`. [`Partition_FixedSizeGroups`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`Partition_SplitsOnValueChange`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`Partition_EmptyInput_ReturnsEmpty`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs) `fn-partition` is in GatedSets. [Gate runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs). ## 16. Related Features [Catalog index](../README.md), [routing chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md), [structural records](../type-system/structural-records.md), [experimental scan](../experimental/fn-scan.md).

functions/csv-parsing.md.text:
CSV parsing

Practical reference: Frozen 4.0

**C09 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-1.md) records 4 contract groups with exact sample/context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited frozen CSV/options contract**. C02-F03/F12: namespaced unknown options and newer index/get policy remain unsupported/not adopted; no remote/schema completeness. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **CSV parsing** - **Frozen 4.0**. Delivery family: [REQ-118](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) / [REQ-123 registry](../../FEATURE_REQUESTS.md). Section provenance: REQ-123 CSV cluster; local FunctionLibrary CSV implementation. [Primary implementation evidence](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) records the shipped behavior; this entry adds executable user-facing examples under REQ-126, rather than announcing a new engine feature. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [fn:parse-csv](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-parse-csv), [fn:csv-doc](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-csv-doc), [fn:csv-to-xml](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-csv-to-xml). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #104](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/104), [immutable mainline revision `e0024f5d`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/e0024f5d1d00c410e65ebf04f4caf89e770eb8ec) (2026-10-09). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Use the parsed row array rather than splitting on commas, which would split a quoted product name. ## 3. Also Known As Use the name and spelling in this entry and its executable files. Related functions or instruction forms are described in the primary test evidence; no additional alias is adopted here. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1, use a dedicated CSV reader or an explicitly tested parser; tokenize is not a general CSV parser. Compare the [complete earlier-version baseline](../examples/csv-parsing/before.xpath) with the [complete expression](../examples/csv-parsing/main.xpath). Both yield `FILTER,BLUE / 12` for this synthetic input. They demonstrate this task, not universal equivalence of the two mechanisms. ## 5. Motivation A supplier exports product codes and quantities as quoted CSV cells. Use the parsed row array rather than splitting on commas, which would split a quoted product name. Keeping this task explicit makes it possible to choose the feature for a practical reason and verify what the receiving application will see. ## 6. Language Alignment Read the behavior as XPath/XSLT semantics. Similar vocabulary in another programming language is not a compatibility promise. This reduced example has one data row and no header. Validate numeric quantities separately; parsing CSV is not business validation. ## 7. Applicability Use this form when solving the stated task and the consumer permits the declared compatibility level. Keep the earlier baseline when the application requires 3.1 expressions or portable 3.0 stylesheets. This reduced example has one data row and no header. Validate numeric quantities separately; parsing CSV is not business validation. **Options/defaults follow-up - 23 October 2026:** [Bounded review](../CSV-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md) and [complete supplier import](../examples/csv-contracts/README.md) add99 catalog cases plus25 local-resource tests for published1.23.8. Omitted/empty options, headers, delimiters, ragged rows, validation and resource paths are covered. Non-positive selection conflicts with the current draft and frozen upstream test; unknown namespaced QName options also differ. These are explicit observations, not new support or full conformance. Historical adoption remains unassigned. ## 8. Structure ```xquery let $row := fn:parse-csv('"FILTER,BLUE",12')?rows[1] return $row?1 || ' / ' || $row?2 ``` This is the worked case's syntax, not a replacement for the full language grammar. Required namespaces and surrounding context are supplied in the linked complete files. ## 9. Participants XPath31Expression, CompileOptions, the parser/compiler, and the shared runtime/function library provide the public execution path. [Primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) identify the feature's implementation contract. The examples use public APIs only. ## 10. Collaborations The case combines source values, the named feature, and explicit output formatting. [Worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md) show how selection, construction, and business rejection fit into larger transformations. ## 11. Consequences Benefit: Use the parsed row array rather than splitting on commas, which would split a quoted product name. Tradeoff: the declared compatibility level and edge rules become part of the consumer contract. This reduced example has one data row and no header. Validate numeric quantities separately; parsing CSV is not business validation. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Absence versus empty/blank text and returned row/column records; Separator, quote, comment, trim, header and selection options; Local-resource base URI, encoding, errors and callback get bounds. **Boundaries:** Frozen positive selection/get indices differ from the current draft; unknown namespaced options remain unsupported; no remote-resource or schema-completeness claim. Follow-up groups: F03, F12. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Compile the after/edge expressions at XPathCompatibility.XPath40. The baseline uses XPath31. The example harness checks default-mode refusal for successful 4.0 cases; negative cases pin the declared error. The baseline starts with a host-parsed array; it is not a replacement CSV parser. See [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs): it executes the published files from the [case manifest](../examples/cases.json). This documentation slice changes no engine source. ## 13. Sample Code Input is synthetic and declared directly in the complete expression. The [complete expression](../examples/csv-parsing/main.xpath) yields `FILTER,BLUE / 12`. The [edge case](../examples/csv-parsing/edge.xpath) yields `FILTER,BLUE / 0`. No external resources or application variables are required. See the [example runner](../examples/README.md) for commands and host context. ## 14. Performance Notes Expected class: input-size dependent. Parsing constructs row/cell values; the quantity cast and downstream business checks are separate costs. These are implementation expectations, not measured deltas. No benchmark is claimed; use the repository benchmark harness before making workload-specific speed or memory claims. ## 15. Known Uses **Revision-specific index evidence:** [Audit](../CSV-INDEX-CONTRACT.md) reproduces124/0 frozen and117/7 current-upstream native cases. Upstream already changed selection and `get` expectations; adopting that contract is separate from this evidence-only audit. The original `observed-*` cases remain unchanged. Current applicable evidence: all `csv-contract-*` IDs in the [manifest](../examples/cases.json), the25 public API tests in [CsvResourceContractTests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/CsvResourceContractTests.cs) (`LocalResource_UsesOptions`, `LocalResource_EncodingAndEmptyRows`, `LocalResource_PreservesErrors`, `MissingResource_RaisesFout1170`, `Keywords_ReadLocalResource`, `EmptySource_BypassesOptionInspection`) and existing [CsvTests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/CsvTests.cs). All99 exact IDs are recorded in [the machine review](../CSV-CONTRACT-REVIEW.json). The existing `fn-parse-csv`, `fn-csv-to-xml`, `fn-csv-doc` gated sets apply within their frozen scope; `parse-csv-912` does not establish the opposite current-draft rule. No gate promotion or full current-draft certification follows. Executable example IDs: `csv-parsing-main`, `csv-parsing-edge`, `csv-parsing-before` in `CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome`. Existing unit evidence: [primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Chapter-level evidence does not promote a qt4tests set into GatedSets; conformance status remains owned by the harness and delivery records. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Compile_CsvFunctions_DefaultOptions_ThrowXpst0017`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_ParseCsv_FrozenXPath40_Works`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Named promoted sets: `fn-csv-doc`, `fn-csv-to-xml`, `fn-parse-csv`. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features See the [catalog index](../README.md), [worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md), and the alternatives in section 4. The case may be used independently of the larger chapters. *Created 2026-10-11: verified practical catalog example and earlier-version baseline.*

functions/customer-reference-matching.md.text:
Customer-reference Matching

21 October 2026

**C09 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-1.md) records 4 contract groups with exact sample/context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited equality/collation contracts**. C02-F01/F09: no deep-equal options maps, complete UCA/normalization, metadata or full comparator acceptance. Other three fn sets are not gated. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Customer-reference equality and collation — existing 3.1 functions with reviewed 4.0 contracts.** Covers fn:distinct-values, fn:index-of, fn:deep-equal, fn:compare and fn:contains-token. Functions are not4.0-only names; this adds no name to the 117-name inventory. [REQ-126](../../FEATURE_REQUESTS.md) equality/collation documentation slice; [review and source pins](../EQUALITY-COLLATION-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md), source base `5de2cfc5213529cdef419b9b7dec3cf9b6c03f7f`. Keyword syntax requires4.0. Unsupported draft forms are explicitly separated from supported calls. Documentation delivery: [Bosak PR #398](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/398). The review and verification receipts preserve source/specification pins, named cases, original findings and test hashes. ## 2. Intent Match synthetic customer references under an explicit business collation, retain every matching position, test whole tag tokens and verify report order. Start with the [complete customer example](../examples/equality-contracts/README.md). ## 3. Also Known As Equivalence classes, positional lookup, structural equality, three-way comparison and token membership are different operations, not interchangeable function aliases. The current compare parameter-name drift is not an accepted rename of the specification. ## 4. History / Supersedes All five names exist in 3.1. The [positional3.1 report](../examples/equality-contracts/report-normal-31.xpath) and [keyword4.0 report](../examples/equality-contracts/report-normal-40.xpath) give the same stated output.4.0 expands compare to atomic operands and deep-equal to optional options; this review does not claim full implementation of those declarations. Current pins do not reconstruct historical adoption. ## 5. Motivation Case-insensitive matching does not imply accent folding, Unicode normalization, substring matching, unordered sequence equality or case-insensitive map keys. Make each import policy observable instead of conflating those decisions. ## 6. Language Alignment JavaScript Set and .NET Distinct are only rough analogies. XPath distinct-value representative/order rules are not a promise of insertion order; index-of returns all one-based positions; deep-equal is sequence/order-sensitive and does not mean reference identity. NaN behavior differs between value equality and deep equality. Culture/default comparer behavior from host languages must not silently select a business collation. ## 7. Applicability Use supported explicit string collations for a declared reference/tag contract. Use codepoint comparison for identifiers whose spelling must remain exact. Do not use this miniature report as identity verification, a production schema, or fuzzy customer matching. Validate required/unique IDs separately. ## 8. Structure ```xquery distinct-values($references, $collation) index-of($references, $target, $collation) compare($reference, $target, $collation) eq 0 contains-token($tags, $token, $collation) deep-equal($actualIds, $expectedIds) ``` Full argument types/defaults and options differences are in the [signature audit](../audit-equality-collation-contracts.json). These shapes show supported positional examples, not the complete grammar. ## 9. Participants The parser/binder handles keyword syntax and compatibility gates; FunctionLibrary registers overloads and metadata; EvaluationContext supplies default collation/timezone; the standard functions implement equality and atomization. The unchanged [catalog runner](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) executes each published file. ## 10. Collaborations parse-xml supplies controlled input; simple mapping projects strings without imposing path-node order; explicit NFC normalization is optional policy, not collation preprocessing. The report combines all five operations while keeping membership, positions, identity and order separate. ## 11. Consequences Explicit policy makes reports reproducible for the supplied supported collations. Case folding can collapse distinct business identifiers if chosen incorrectly. ASCII collation does not fold Ä/ä or normalize combining marks. A distinct count is deliberately used without relying on which duplicate spelling or order is returned. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Explicit collations, duplicate representatives and one-based matching positions; Sequence-order-sensitive deep equality and NaN behavior; Empty index-of collation correction and compare keyword boundary. **Boundaries:** Deep-equal map options are unsupported; supported collations do not imply normalization or complete UCA behavior. Follow-up groups: F01, F09. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Original reviewed implementation: [FunctionLibrary at the immutable source base](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/5de2cfc5213529cdef419b9b7dec3cf9b6c03f7f/src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs), including DistinctValues_2, IndexOf_3, DeepEqual_3, Compare_2/3 and ContainsToken. This documentation slice changes no engine code. Current compare keywords differ from the draft, two families lack metadata, empty positional index collation is corrected in source1.23.2 only at4.0 while deep-equal options maps still refuse; see the separate findings. Keyword grammar refuses at XPath31; the five positional functions remain available there, with compare's earlier string contract. **Index-of source correction:** [Empty-collation default evidence](../INDEX-OF-EMPTY-COLLATION.md) records27 new standard-library checks, unchanged3.1 refusal and the corrected manifest case. The original source/audit pins above remain historical evidence. ## 13. Sample Code The [self-contained walkthrough](../examples/equality-contracts/README.md) contains complete input, both expressions and exact normal/empty/reordered output. Normal output is `references=3;positions=1,2;ids=C1,C2;vip=2;expected-order=true`.58 manifest checks include modes, empty/invalid arguments, NaN, Unicode, maps and six full reports. Observed-gap fixtures are labelled separately and retain normative expected outcomes. ## 14. Performance Notes The report scans the supplied customer sequence several times. No benchmark, asymptotic guarantee for every collation, or comparison with host collections is claimed. Large/import-streaming design remains a separate task; ad-hoc timings are not performance evidence. ## 15. Known Uses The [manifest](../examples/cases.json) and CatalogExampleTests verify the named equality-contract cases. QT3 sets: [distinct-values](https://github.com/w3c/qt3tests/blob/201a6e466940cdfc727f4babfedcde5332b9f578/fn/distinct-values.xml), [index-of](https://github.com/w3c/qt3tests/blob/201a6e466940cdfc727f4babfedcde5332b9f578/fn/index-of.xml), [deep-equal](https://github.com/w3c/qt3tests/blob/201a6e466940cdfc727f4babfedcde5332b9f578/fn/deep-equal.xml), [compare](https://github.com/w3c/qt3tests/blob/201a6e466940cdfc727f4babfedcde5332b9f578/fn/compare.xml), [contains-token](https://github.com/w3c/qt3tests/blob/201a6e466940cdfc727f4babfedcde5332b9f578/fn/contains-token.xml). Corresponding qt4 files exist at the same fn paths under [qt4tests](https://github.com/qt4cg/qt4tests/blob/68910080d2d4d4092a1c6a908998ceec64ffc6d4/catalog.xml). Current [GatedSets](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs) includes fn-compare/fn-contains-token; fn-distinct-values/fn-index-of/fn-deep-equal are not gated. Membership is source evidence, not a new conformance run. No gate is invented or promoted; AC-03's catalog-wide acceptance remains unresolved. ## 16. Related Features [Sequence distinctness](sequence-distinctness.md), [shipment-event sequence checks](shipment-event-sequences.md), [typed measurement comparison](measurement-comparison.md), [ordering/default contracts](../ORDER-DEFAULT-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md), [complete review](../EQUALITY-COLLATION-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md). **Validation:** Release build succeeds with the pre-existing conformance Program.cs:1868 CS8604 warning. All **10,304 solution tests pass**, including 7,363 XSLT tests and2,636 manifest rows. The 58 new focused checks overlap these totals. [Verification receipt](../EQUALITY-COLLATION-VERIFICATION.json) preserves all ten TRX hashes. Manual engine gates were not rerun: engine/harness source, gate membership and package version are unchanged.

functions/customer-text-cleanup.md.text:
Customer Text Cleanup

Frozen 4.0 — real-world import text contracts

**C10 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-2.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited text contract; incomplete grapheme segmentation**. Grapheme segmentation is approximate; missing keywords, implicit trim focus and unknown-option validation are not supported contracts. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Customer text cleanup — Frozen 4.0.** [fn:trim-space](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-trim-space), [fn:pad-string](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-pad-string), [fn:characters](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-characters), [fn:graphemes](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-graphemes) and [fn:char](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-char). Initial char/characters delivery: [PR #82](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/82), [40ebaa79](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/40ebaa79032b17fc45d6d3bb3e58cb00e2fda742), REQ-118 S0/S1 part 1. Remaining string functions: [PR #83](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/83), [532d04f4](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/532d04f4672df430d93752e3158fc3cdfd4c7c39), S1 part 2. Definitions reviewed **2026-10-12** against immutable [QT4CG source e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). The eight reviewed function definitions are unchanged from the earlier a014e1b4 review pin. This does not recover unavailable historical adopted specification snapshots. ## 2. Intent Trim import padding from a customer label while preserving its interior spacing and Unicode spelling. Report codepoint and grapheme counts separately, and pad an export value to a minimum codepoint length. ## 3. Also Known As Boundary trimming, minimum-length padding and character segmentation are descriptive terms. No function aliases are registered. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 can trim XML whitespace with two anchored regular-expression replacements, split codepoints with string-to-codepoints/codepoints-to-string, and append repeated padding explicitly. The complete comparison returns the same cleaned and padded label. It omits the grapheme count: XPath 3.1 has no direct standard grapheme-segmentation function. `normalize-space` would also collapse interior runs and therefore implements a different cleanup rule. ## 5. Motivation A customer name can contain deliberately repeated interior spaces, a combining accent and a supplementary character. Treating UTF-16 storage units, Unicode codepoints and displayed clusters as interchangeable gives misleading length checks. The report makes the import/export contract explicit. ## 6. Language Alignment `trim-space` removes XML whitespace (space, tab, CR and LF) at the selected start/end/both boundary. It preserves interior whitespace and does not remove NBSP. Empty input returns an empty string. `pad-string` defaults to end padding with spaces; options select side and padding. It never truncates. Both-side odd padding puts the extra character at the end. `characters` returns one string per Unicode codepoint; `graphemes` groups supported combining/ZWJ sequences into clusters. Neither performs Unicode normalization. `char` constructs a string from a positive codepoint, recognized entity name or supported escape; some entity names return multiple codepoints. It is not an HTML document decoder. Bosak's [Graphemes_1/GraphemeClusterClass implementation](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs) approximates segmentation: it does not distinguish Hangul jamo, Prepend, regional-indicator or full Indic/extended-pictographic classes. These verified combining-mark and ZWJ cases do not establish complete Unicode grapheme conformance. ## 7. Applicability Use for import boundary cleanup and codepoint-length export rules. The fixture's target length is a minimum of ten codepoints, not bytes, screen columns or grapheme clusters. Padding does not make emoji and Latin characters equally wide in a font. A Unicode normalization policy or complete grapheme implementation is a separate requirement. The examples do not truncate customer names or claim to validate them. ## 8. Structure Read a name element, trim its boundaries, count codepoints and supported grapheme clusters, then append dots to reach ten codepoints. Construct an em-dash separator with char(8212). ## 9. Participants The customer element supplies unnormalized text. Cleanup preserves interior content. Segmentation describes length under two models. Padding produces the export field. A report shows all outputs. ## 10. Collaborations Trim before padding. Keep the original combining sequence when preservation is required. Use count(characters(...)) for the specified codepoint contract; do not substitute grapheme count for that minimum-length rule. ## 11. Consequences The fixture retains two interior spaces and a decomposed accent. Its eight codepoints form seven supported grapheme clusters; two dots reach ten codepoints. Oversized values remain unchanged. Invalid side/padding options and unsupported char values raise the demonstrated errors. Known grapheme limitations remain documented rather than being certified by these samples. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles XML boundary whitespace, interior preservation, nontruncating codepoint padding; Character/entity conversion and supported grapheme clusters; Defaults, empty values, side options and invalid input. **Boundaries:** Grapheme segmentation is approximate; missing keywords, implicit trim focus and unknown-option validation are not supported contracts. Follow-up groups: F01, F02, F03, F13. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Compile new calls with CompileOptions.Compatibility40; the default 3.1 profile rejects them. The comparison uses Compatibility31. The [catalog harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) verifies exact text/error markers and default-profile refusal for successful 4.0 cases. Unicode inputs are inline XML character references so their intended values are explicit. **Supplementary text-contract review (2026-10-12):** [Eight-family contract review](../TEXT-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md) and [detailed label/filename README](../examples/text-contracts/README.md) supply explicit keyword refusals at 3.1/4.0/experimental, positional defaults/empty/invalid cases and complete paired reports. Numeric substring/option tolerance and validation boundaries remain observed follow-ups; the review does not implement keywords or certify full Unicode/coercion conformance. ## 13. sections.2: Trim import padding from a customer label while preserving its interior spacing and Unicode spelling. Report codepoint and grapheme counts separately, and pad an export value to a minimum codepoint length.
sections.3: Boundary trimming, minimum-length padding and character segmentation are descriptive terms. No function aliases are registered.
sections.4: XPath 3.1 can trim XML whitespace with two anchored regular-expression replacements, split codepoints with string-to-codepoints/codepoints-to-string, and append repeated padding explicitly. The complete comparison returns the same cleaned and padded label. It omits the grapheme count: XPath 3.1 has no direct standard grapheme-segmentation function. `normalize-space` would also collapse interior runs and therefore implements a different cleanup rule.
sections.5: A customer name can contain deliberately repeated interior spaces, a combining accent and a supplementary character. Treating UTF-16 storage units, Unicode codepoints and displayed clusters as interchangeable gives misleading length checks. The report makes the import/export contract explicit.
sections.6:
`trim-space` removes XML whitespace (space, tab, CR and LF) at the selected start/end/both boundary. It preserves interior whitespace and does not remove NBSP. Empty input returns an empty string. `pad-string` defaults to end padding with spaces; options select side and padding. It never truncates. Both-side odd padding puts the extra character at the end.

`characters` returns one string per Unicode codepoint; `graphemes` groups supported combining/ZWJ sequences into clusters. Neither performs Unicode normalization. `char` constructs a string from a positive codepoint, recognized entity name or supported escape; some entity names return multiple codepoints. It is not an HTML document decoder.

Bosak's [Graphemes_1/GraphemeClusterClass implementation](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs) approximates segmentation: it does not distinguish Hangul jamo, Prepend, regional-indicator or full Indic/extended-pictographic classes. These verified combining-mark and ZWJ cases do not establish complete Unicode grapheme conformance.
sections.7: Use for import boundary cleanup and codepoint-length export rules. The fixture's target length is a minimum of ten codepoints, not bytes, screen columns or grapheme clusters. Padding does not make emoji and Latin characters equally wide in a font. A Unicode normalization policy or complete grapheme implementation is a separate requirement. The examples do not truncate customer names or claim to validate them.
sections.8: Read a name element, trim its boundaries, count codepoints and supported grapheme clusters, then append dots to reach ten codepoints. Construct an em-dash separator with char(8212).
sections.9: The customer element supplies unnormalized text. Cleanup preserves interior content. Segmentation describes length under two models. Padding produces the export field. A report shows all outputs.
sections.10: Trim before padding. Keep the original combining sequence when preservation is required. Use count(characters(...)) for the specified codepoint contract; do not substitute grapheme count for that minimum-length rule.
sections.11: The fixture retains two interior spaces and a decomposed accent. Its eight codepoints form seven supported grapheme clusters; two dots reach ten codepoints. Oversized values remain unchanged. Invalid side/padding options and unsupported char values raise the demonstrated errors. Known grapheme limitations remain documented rather than being certified by these samples.

Complete synthetic input; the name contains e followed by combining acute, two interior spaces and a truck emoji:

```xml
<customer><name>  José  🚚  </name></customer>
```

### Complete XPath 4.0 expression

[Runnable file](../examples/customer-text-cleanup/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $name := string(parse-xml('<customer><name>  José  🚚  </name></customer>')/customer/name)
let $label := trim-space($name)
return concat('label=[', $label, ']; codepoints=', count(characters($label)), '; graphemes=', count(graphemes($label)), '; export=[', pad-string($label, 10, map {'padding': '.'}), ']; separator=', char(8212))
```

```text
label=[José  🚚]; codepoints=8; graphemes=7; export=[José  🚚..]; separator=—
```


Exact output:

```text
label=[José  🚚]; codepoints=8; export=[José  🚚..]; separator=—
```

functions/element-to-map.md.text:
Element-to-map conversion

Practical reference: Frozen 4.0

**C10 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-2.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited verified frozen contract**. The published simple-content example does not certify every conversion-plan record, name collision, namespace, schema annotation or option; use only tested layouts/options. Current-draft escape-names decoding is unsupported; the new option is not adopted automatically into frozen or Experimental profiles. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Element-to-map conversion** - **Frozen 4.0**. Delivery family: [REQ-118](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) / [REQ-123 registry](../../FEATURE_REQUESTS.md). Section provenance: See the linked REQ dossiers and implementation evidence. [Primary implementation evidence](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/ElementMapTests.cs) records the shipped behavior; this entry adds executable user-facing examples under REQ-126, rather than announcing a new engine feature. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [fn:element-to-map](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-element-to-map), [fn:element-to-map-plan](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-element-to-map-plan). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #106](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/106), [immutable mainline revision `1bb73147`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/1bb731474c6ba48dded66441183c676a0ebf9761) (2026-10-09). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Describe the conversion shape explicitly before passing data into a map-oriented pipeline. ## 3. Also Known As Use the name and spelling in this entry and its executable files. Related functions or instruction forms are described in the primary test evidence; no additional alias is adopted here. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1, construct the desired map explicitly from XML selectors. Compare the [complete earlier-version baseline](../examples/element-to-map/before.xpath) with the [complete expression](../examples/element-to-map/main.xpath). Both yield `FILTER-A` for this synthetic input. They demonstrate this task, not universal equivalence of the two mechanisms. ## 5. Motivation An integration adapter needs an XML product code as a map field. Describe the conversion shape explicitly before passing data into a map-oriented pipeline. Keeping this task explicit makes it possible to choose the feature for a practical reason and verify what the receiving application will see. ## 6. Language Alignment Read the behavior as XPath/XSLT semantics. Similar vocabulary in another programming language is not a compatibility promise. Layout and typing options matter for attributes and repeated children. This example deliberately uses a single simple-content element. ## 7. Applicability Use this form when solving the stated task and the consumer permits the declared compatibility level. Keep the earlier baseline when the application requires 3.1 expressions or portable 3.0 stylesheets. Layout and typing options matter for attributes and repeated children. This example deliberately uses a single simple-content element. ## 8. Structure ```xquery fn:element-to-map(parse-xml('FILTER-A')/sku)?sku ``` This is the worked case's syntax, not a replacement for the full language grammar. Required namespaces and surrounding context are supplied in the linked complete files. ## 9. Participants XPath31Expression, CompileOptions, the parser/compiler, and the shared runtime/function library provide the public execution path. [Primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/ElementMapTests.cs) identify the feature's implementation contract. The examples use public APIs only. ## 10. Collaborations The case combines source values, the named feature, and explicit output formatting. [Worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md) show how selection, construction, and business rejection fit into larger transformations. ## 11. Consequences Benefit: Describe the conversion shape explicitly before passing data into a map-oriented pipeline. Tradeoff: the declared compatibility level and edge rules become part of the consumer contract. Layout and typing options matter for attributes and repeated children. This example deliberately uses a single simple-content element. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Simple-content XML-to-map shape; Plans/layout/name policy are explicit conversion choices; Wrong input, option and keyword boundaries. **Boundaries:** The published simple-content example does not certify every conversion-plan record, name collision, namespace, schema annotation or option; use only tested layouts/options. Current-draft escape-names decoding is unsupported; the new option is not adopted automatically into frozen or Experimental profiles. Follow-up groups: F01, F14. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Compile the after/edge expressions at XPathCompatibility.XPath40. The baseline uses XPath31. The example harness checks default-mode refusal for successful 4.0 cases; negative cases pin the declared error. See [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs): it executes the published files from the [case manifest](../examples/cases.json). This documentation slice changes no engine source. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** Keyword drift: implemented input differs from pinned element; the [signature audit](../SIGNATURE-CONTRACT-AUDIT.md) publishes paired success/refusal files. Positional conversion remains separate evidence. ## 13. Sample Code Input is synthetic and declared directly in the complete expression. The [complete expression](../examples/element-to-map/main.xpath) yields `FILTER-A`. The [edge case](../examples/element-to-map/edge.xpath) yields `0`. No external resources or application variables are required. See the [example runner](../examples/README.md) for commands and host context. ## 14. Performance Notes Expected class: tree-size dependent conversion. Selected layout and repeated-child representation affect allocations. These are implementation expectations, not measured deltas. No benchmark is claimed; use the repository benchmark harness before making workload-specific speed or memory claims. ## 15. Known Uses Executable example IDs: `element-to-map-main`, `element-to-map-edge`, `element-to-map-before` in `CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome`. Existing unit evidence: [primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/ElementMapTests.cs). Chapter-level evidence does not promote a qt4tests set into GatedSets; conformance status remains owned by the harness and delivery records. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Evaluate_ElementToMap_FrozenXPath40_Works`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Named promoted sets: `fn-element-to-map`, `fn-element-to-map-plan`. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features See the [catalog index](../README.md), [worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md), and the alternatives in section 4. Higher-order selection

Frozen 4.0

**C10 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-2.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited verified frozen contract**. Callable/subtyping combinations beyond the verified signatures remain unsupported in this consumer reference. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Higher-order selection — Frozen 4.0.** [Bosak PR #88](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/88) / [immutable revision `0a928bb8`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/0a928bb81b81d0631cc681f86bba83259c0ed790). This is the shipped engine delivery. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [fn:some](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-some), [fn:every](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-every), [fn:index-where](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-index-where). Historical adopted specification source revision was not retained; this remains an explicit provenance gap. ## 2. Intent Validate order lines and locate every rejected line without losing its original position. ## 3. Also Known As Use the exact spellings in the linked examples; no undocumented aliases are adopted. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 offers `some ... satisfies` and `every ... satisfies` quantified expressions. Positional `for` expressions can locate failures, as the linked baseline demonstrates. Function forms make the predicate a reusable function item; neither syntax nor callback contracts are interchangeable automatically. some/every test whether any/all items satisfy a predicate; index-where returns one-based matching positions. The two-argument callbacks receive item and position. Empty predicate results mean false; arbitrary nonboolean callback results are errors. Empty input gives some=false, every=true and no positions. An explicit existence check is needed when an empty order is invalid. ## 5. Motivation Validate order lines and locate every rejected line without losing its original position. The order-routing chapter places validation before dispatch so rejected records stay available for repair. ## 6. Language Alignment Do not confuse fn:some/fn:every function calls with the XPath 3.1 quantified-expression grammar. Callback positions refer to the input sequence, not document sibling positions. ## 7. Applicability Use when the consumer opts into XPath40 and needs the exact validation or ordering contract described here. Keep the XPath 3.1 baseline when that opt-in is unavailable. ## 8. Structure ```xquery string-join(index-where((2, 0, 3), function($quantity, $position) { $quantity le 0 }) ! string(.), ',') ``` This complete expression demonstrates the stated contract, not the full grammar. ## 9. Participants The public XPath API compiles at the manifest mode and evaluates without application variables. The routing chapter additionally supplies an XML document context. ## 10. Collaborations The routing planner passes an XDM map to portable XSLT through a required parameter. See [the full chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md). ## 11. Consequences some/every test whether any/all items satisfy a predicate; index-where returns one-based matching positions. The two-argument callbacks receive item and position. Empty predicate results mean false; arbitrary nonboolean callback results are errors. Empty input gives some=false, every=true and no positions. An explicit existence check is needed when an empty order is invalid. Do not confuse fn:some/fn:every function calls with the XPath 3.1 quantified-expression grammar. Callback positions refer to the input sequence, not document sibling positions. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Any/all/position selection and vacuous empty results; Item and one-based position callbacks; Boolean/empty result conversion and invalid callback arity. **Boundaries:** Callable/subtyping combinations beyond the verified signatures remain unsupported in this consumer reference. Follow-up groups: F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) runs the exact files, asserts declared results/errors, and checks default-3.1 refusal for successful 4.0 forms. No engine code changes or conformance promotions are included. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** [Comparison/selection review](../SELECTION-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md), pinned to F&O e7ee4ab8, and [detailed warehouse README](../examples/selection-contracts/README.md) supply 68 checks: keyword modes, collation/default/key/predicate, atomization, result/cardinality boundaries and complete 3.1/4.0 reports. duplicate-values/highest/lowest keywords remain unavailable; index-where keywords work. Map tolerance and tested extrema NaN results remain explicit engine follow-ups. Extrema return boundary-equal items, not all distinct records sharing its key. Initial delivery/unit/gate and historical adopted-pin limits are unchanged. ## 13. Sample Code [main.xpath](../examples/higher-order-selection/main.xpath): returns `2` at mode 40. [edge.xpath](../examples/higher-order-selection/edge.xpath): returns `false/true` at mode 40. [before.xpath](../examples/higher-order-selection/before.xpath): returns `2` at mode 31. ## 14. Performance Notes Duplicate checks and index selection may traverse the input; some/every may finish early. Partitioning creates arrays and retains input items. These are qualitative expectations, not benchmark results. Stateful or expensive callbacks change workload costs. ## 15. Known Uses Executable IDs: `higher-order-selection-main`, `higher-order-selection-edge`, `higher-order-selection-before`. [`Some_PositionArgument_IsOneBased`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`Every_EmptyInput_ReturnsTrue`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`IndexWhere_ReturnsAscendingPositions`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs) The exact-name sets `fn-some`, `fn-every` and `fn-index-where` are not in the current GatedSets; named unit tests and published examples provide evidence. [Gate runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs). ## 16. Related Features [Catalog index](../README.md), [routing chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md), [structural records](../type-system/structural-records.md), [experimental scan](../experimental/fn-scan.md).

functions/import-array-batches.md.text:
Import batches with arrays

Frozen 4.0 — verified reference contracts

**C10 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-2.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited verified frozen contract**. array:members/of-members are JNode functions owned by C05, not replacements for member/item concatenation. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Import batches with arrays — Frozen 4.0.** Shipped in [Bosak PR #84](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/84) at immutable revision [`f7f55b4e`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/f7f55b4e3a6e92da26ac607e34f46aede695cb19). Functions: [array:build](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-array-build), [array:empty](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-array-empty), [array:items](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-array-items), [array:slice](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-array-slice). Definitions reviewed 2026-10-11 against immutable [QT4CG function source `a014e1b4`](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This is a review pin, not evidence of the historical adopted snapshot, which remains unavailable. ## 2. Intent Keep every order’s product-code sequence in one array member, select a two-order import batch, and concatenate the lines only at the export boundary. One order can contain several lines without becoming several orders. ## 3. Also Known As Exact spellings are `array:build`, `array:empty`, `array:items` and `array:slice`. No aliases are introduced. `array:items` performs one-level concatenation; `array:flatten` is the recursive alternative. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 uses `fold-left` and `array:append` to construct one member per order, then `array:subarray` for the illustrated forward batch and `?*` for one-level concatenation. `array:subarray` is not a general substitute for negative bounds, reverse slices, strides or forgiving out-of-range selection. ## 5. Motivation Flattening line sequences before batching destroys order boundaries. Building one array member per callback invocation preserves them even when a callback returns several items or the empty sequence. ## 6. Language Alignment Array members can be arbitrary XPath sequences, unlike a simple list of scalar JSON values. Addresses are one-based. Slice end positions are inclusive, unlike Python and JavaScript slices; negative values count from the end. `array:items` concatenates one level and retains nested arrays, while `array:flatten` is recursive. ## 7. Applicability Use for bounded selections from an already materialized batch. `array:empty([()])` is false: there is one member even though it contains no items. Distinguish no orders from an order with no lines, and validate that business condition separately. ## 8. Structure ```xquery array:build($orders, function($order,$position){$order?lines}) array:slice($members, $start, $end, $step) array:empty($members) array:items($members) ``` Positional and shorter callback forms are exercised by the exact files below. This entry covers the illustrated contracts rather than every arity or option. ## 9. Participants Existing `FunctionLibrary` frozen registrations select these names only at `XPathCompatibility.XPath40` or higher. The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) compiles each file at its declared mode and checks default XPath31 refusal for successful 4.0 forms. ## 10. Collaborations The map family indexes products while this array family preserves order boundaries. The [sequence-selection family](order-sequence-selection.md) uses the same slice position rules for ordinary sequences. ## 11. Consequences Each callback result is one array member. `array:items` loses those boundaries, so call it only when flattening one level is intended. `[]`, `[()]` and `[[]]` have different member counts. Empty bounds or zero select defaults; a negative step defaults the omitted start/end to opposite sequence ends. An omitted/zero step chooses direction from the resolved bounds. An explicit incompatible direction returns an empty array, and out-of-range bounds do not raise the `array:subarray` bounds error. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles One callback result per member and one-level item concatenation; Zero members versus empty/nested members; Inclusive/negative slice bounds, default/zero step and empty direction result. **Boundaries:** array:members/of-members are JNode functions owned by C05, not replacements for member/item concatenation. Follow-up groups: F01, F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Implementation: [FunctionLibrary.cs](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs); [named unit tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs); [manifest](../examples/cases.json). Names refuse XPST0017 in default XPath31; the comparisons remain valid at XPath31. Source/package version stays 1.1.1. This reference work changes no engine code. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** [Container review](../CONTAINER-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md), pinned to F&O e7ee4ab8, and [detailed stock-feed README](../examples/container-contracts/README.md) supply 89 checks covering six families: keyword modes, empty/default/member/item shapes, nested values, node identity, callback arity/results and complete XPath 3.1/4.0 reports. Keywords remain unavailable. map:filter boolean-result enforcement remains an engine follow-up. Source/public version is 1.1.3; original delivery/unit/gate evidence and historical adopted-pin limits are unchanged. The map result-shape corrections already shipped in 1.1.2. ## 13. Sample Code Input is declared inside each expression: reduced order/product records, no document focus, external variables or resource access. Namespace prefixes `map` and `array` use the standard public API bindings. Outputs are exact text projections of XDM results, not serialized supplier or ERP formats. **Main — mode 40:** [main.xpath](../examples/import-array-batches/main.xpath) ```xquery (: One array member holds all product codes for one order. :) let $orders := (map{'id':'ORD-101','lines':('FILTER-A','SEAL-B')}, map{'id':'ORD-102','lines':('VALVE-C')}, map{'id':'ORD-103','lines':('HOSE-D','CLIP-E')}), $members := array:build($orders, function($order,$position){$order?lines}), $batch := array:slice($members, 1, 2) return concat('orders=', array:size($batch), ';lines=', string-join(array:items($batch), ',')) ``` Expected text: ```text orders=2;lines=FILTER-A,SEAL-B,VALVE-C ``` **Baseline — mode 31:** [baseline.xpath](../examples/import-array-batches/baseline.xpath) ```xquery let $orders := (map{'id':'ORD-101','lines':('FILTER-A','SEAL-B')}, map{'id':'ORD-102','lines':('VALVE-C')}, map{'id':'ORD-103','lines':('HOSE-D','CLIP-E')}), $members := fold-left($orders, [], function($array,$order){array:append($array,$order?lines)}), $batch := array:subarray($members, 1, 2) return concat('orders=', array:size($batch), ';lines=', string-join($batch?*, ',')) ``` Expected text: ```text orders=2;lines=FILTER-A,SEAL-B,VALVE-C ``` **Edge — mode 40:** [edge.xpath](../examples/import-array-batches/edge.xpath) ```xquery let $batch := array:slice(array:build(()), 1, 2) return concat(array:size($batch), '/', array:empty($batch), '/', count(array:items($batch))) ``` Expected text: ```text 0/true/0 ``` **Additional executable contracts:** | Case | Mode | Expected text or error | |---|---|---| | [empty-member](../examples/import-array-batches/empty-member.xpath) | 40 | `true/false/false/0` | | [nested-array](../examples/import-array-batches/nested-array.xpath) | 40 | `3/true` | | [positions](../examples/import-array-batches/positions.xpath) | 40 | `1:ORD-101|2:ORD-102` | | [reverse](../examples/import-array-batches/reverse.xpath) | 40 | `ORD-103,ORD-102,ORD-101` | | [out-of-range](../examples/import-array-batches/out-of-range.xpath) | 40 | `true` | | [negative-bounds](../examples/import-array-batches/negative-bounds.xpath) | 40 | `ORD-102,ORD-103` | | [step](../examples/import-array-batches/step.xpath) | 40 | `ORD-101,ORD-103` | | [incompatible-direction](../examples/import-array-batches/incompatible-direction.xpath) | 40 | `0` | ## 14. Performance Notes Construction retains one member per input item; slicing creates a selected-member array. This implementation materializes input and positions. None of the examples establishes bounded-memory streaming. ## 15. Known Uses [`ArrayBuild_ResultSequenceBecomesSingleMember`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs); [`ArrayBuild_ActionReceivesItemAndPosition`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs); [`ArrayEmpty_OnlyZeroMemberArrayIsEmpty`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs); [`ArrayItems_ConcatenatesMembersNonRecursively`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs); [`ArraySlice_StartEndStep`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs); [`ArraySlice_OutOfBoundsYieldsEmptyArrayNoError`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs). Exact sets `array-build`, `array-items` and `array-slice` are in GatedSets. No exact `array-empty` set is assigned; its named unit and manifest checks remain separate evidence. No sets are promoted by this step. See the [actual gate runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs). Existing 1.1.1 release gate counts are historical evidence; no engine gates are rerun for this documentation slice. ## 16. Related Features [Array member iteration](../operators-and-syntax/array-member-iteration.md), [product maps](product-map-index.md), [sequence selection](order-sequence-selection.md). [Completeness audit](../COMPLETENESS-AUDIT.md).

Definitions reviewed 2026-10-11 against immutable [QT4CG function source `a014e1b4`](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This is a review pin, not evidence of the historical adopted snapshot, which remains unavailable.
sections.2: Keep every order’s product-code sequence in one array member, select a two-order import batch, and concatenate the lines only at the export boundary. One order can contain several lines without becoming several orders.
sections.3: Exact spellings are `array:build`, `array:empty`, `array:items` and `array:slice`. No aliases are introduced. `array:items` performs one-level concatenation; `array:flatten` is the recursive alternative.
sections.4: XPath 3.1 uses `fold-left` and `array:append` to construct one member per order, then `array:subarray` for the illustrated forward batch and `?*` for one-level concatenation. `array:subarray` is not a general substitute for negative bounds, reverse slices, strides or forgiving out-of-range selection.
sections.5: Flattening line sequences before batching destroys order boundaries. Building one array member per callback invocation preserves them even when a callback returns several items or the empty sequence.
sections.6: Array members can be arbitrary XPath sequences, unlike a simple list of scalar JSON values. Addresses are one-based. Slice end positions are inclusive, unlike Python and JavaScript slices; negative values count from the end. `array:items` concatenates one level and retains nested arrays, while `array:flatten` is recursive.
sections.7: Use for bounded selections from an already materialized batch. `array:empty([()])` is false: there is one member even though it contains no items. Distinguish no orders from an order with no lines, and validate that business condition separately.
sections.8:
```xquery
array:build($orders, function($order,$position){$order?lines})
array:slice($members, $start, $end, $step)
array:empty($members)
array:items($members)
```

Positional and shorter callback forms are exercised by the exact files below. This entry covers the illustrated contracts rather than every arity or option.
sections.9: Existing `FunctionLibrary` frozen registrations select these names only at `XPathCompatibility.XPath40` or higher. The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) compiles each file at its declared mode and checks default XPath31 refusal for successful 4.0 forms.
sections.10: The map family indexes products while this array family preserves order boundaries. The [sequence-selection family](order-sequence-selection.md) uses the same slice position rules for ordinary sequences.
sections.11: Each callback result is one array member. `array:items` loses those boundaries, so call it only when flattening one level is intended. `[]`, `[()]` and `[[]]` have different member counts. Empty bounds or zero select defaults; a negative step defaults the omitted start/end to opposite sequence ends. An omitted/zero step chooses direction from the resolved bounds. An explicit incompatible direction returns an empty array, and out-of-range bounds do not raise the `array:subarray` bounds error.
sections.12:
**C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles One callback result per member and one-level item concatenation; Zero members versus empty/nested members; Inclusive/negative slice bounds, default/zero step and empty direction result. **Boundaries:** array:members/of-members are JNode functions owned by C05, not replacements for member/item concatenation. Follow-up groups: F01, F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). **Main — mode 40:** [main.xpath](../examples/import-array-batches/main.xpath)

```xquery
(: One array member holds all product codes for one order. :)
let $orders := (map{'id':'ORD-101','lines':('FILTER-A','SEAL-B')}, map{'id':'ORD-102','lines':('VALVE-C')}, map{'id':'ORD-103','lines':('HOSE-D','CLIP-E')}),
    $members := array:build($orders, function($order,$position){$order?lines}),
    $batch := array:slice($members, 1, 2)
return concat('orders=', array:size($batch), ';lines=', string-join(array:items($batch), ','))
```

```text
orders=2;lines=FILTER-A,SEAL-B,VALVE-C
```

```text
0/true/0
```

functions/import-file-names.md.text:
Import File Names

Frozen 4.0 — real-world import text contracts

**C10 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-2.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited verified frozen contract**. Do not rely on tolerated typed-numeric string arguments; no grapheme-position or path-authorization contract. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Import file names — Frozen 4.0.** [fn:substring-before-last](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-substring-before-last), [fn:substring-after-last](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-substring-after-last), and [fn:index-of-substring](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-index-of-substring). Initial delivery: [PR #83](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/83), [532d04f4](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/532d04f4672df430d93752e3158fc3cdfd4c7c39), REQ-118 S1 part 2. Definitions reviewed **2026-10-12** against immutable [QT4CG source e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). The eight reviewed function definitions are unchanged from the earlier a014e1b4 review pin. This does not recover unavailable historical adopted specification snapshots. ## 2. Intent Split an import path at its final slash and a file name at its final dot, preserving earlier dots. Report dot positions to make the chosen extension boundary explicit. ## 3. Also Known As Last-delimiter extraction and substring-position search are descriptive terms; no aliases are registered. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 can enumerate matching codepoint positions, select the last one and slice with substring. The complete comparison implements the illustrated slash/dot contract. It is scoped to this path with present delimiters; a general helper must also handle missing and empty delimiters explicitly. ## 5. Motivation An import directory can contain dots and a file can have multiple suffixes. Splitting at the first dot would mistake invoice.batch.xml for extension batch.xml. A final-boundary rule gives stem invoice.batch and extension xml, matching the stated importer policy. ## 6. Language Alignment Last-substring functions return the parts before or after the last match under the chosen collation. If no match exists, both return an empty string. With an empty delimiter, before-last returns the input and after-last returns empty. They accept an optional collation; the case uses the default codepoint collation. index-of-substring reports one-based codepoint positions, includes overlapping matches, and has no collation argument. An empty substring matches each boundary through length+1. Empty source with a nonempty needle produces no positions; an empty source and empty needle produce one boundary. These are codepoint positions, not UTF-16 storage indices or grapheme-cluster indices. ## 7. Applicability Use for a declared lexical slash/dot import convention. The main fixture assumes a nonempty slash-separated path with a final filename and a dot extension. It does not access files, normalize Windows paths, parse URIs or classify compound archives. For archive.tar.gz the final extension is gz; recognizing tar.gz as a compound format requires a separate policy. URI percent escapes and query/fragment boundaries belong to [URI component parsing](invoice-api-uris.md). ## 8. Structure Select the text path, derive directory and final filename, then derive stem/extension and all dot positions from that filename. Dots in the directory do not affect extension selection. ## 9. Participants The file record supplies text. Last-match functions select boundaries. Position search exposes filename delimiters. The report shows the exact import classification. ## 10. Collaborations Extract the filename before searching its dots. Apply presence guards in a production importer if a missing delimiter must preserve the whole filename rather than produce empty. Use an explicit collation for case-insensitive text delimiters; the index function remains codepoint matching. ## 11. Consequences Earlier separators and dots remain in the preceding parts. Overlapping delimiters can select a later start than a non-overlapping tokenizer would. No delimiter is an empty-result contract, not an automatic whole-filename fallback. No path authorization or file operation occurs. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Last delimiter, overlap and one-based codepoint positions; Empty needle/source, default collation and malformed collation; Experimental absent-pattern correction with frozen refusal retained. **Boundaries:** Do not rely on tolerated typed-numeric string arguments; no grapheme-position or path-authorization contract. Follow-up groups: F01, F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Use CompileOptions.Compatibility40 for the new calls and Compatibility31 for the comparison. Default 3.1 rejects new names. The [catalog harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) verifies exact report/error markers and default-profile refusal for successful 4.0 cases. All inputs are inline. **Supplementary text-contract review (2026-10-12):** [Eight-family contract review](../TEXT-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md) and [detailed label/filename README](../examples/text-contracts/README.md) supply explicit keyword refusals at 3.1/4.0/experimental, positional defaults/empty/invalid cases and complete paired reports. Numeric substring/option tolerance and validation boundaries remain observed follow-ups; the review does not implement keywords or certify full Unicode/coercion conformance. ## 13. Sample Code Complete synthetic file record: ```xml ``` ### Complete XPath 4.0 expression [Runnable file](../examples/import-file-names/main.xpath): ```xpath let $path := string(parse-xml('')/file/@path) let $directory := substring-before-last($path, '/') let $name := substring-after-last($path, '/') return concat('directory=', $directory, '; file=', $name, '; stem=', substring-before-last($name, '.'), '; extension=', substring-after-last($name, '.'), '; dots=', string-join(index-of-substring($name, '.') ! string(.), ',')) ``` Exact output: ```text directory=incoming/2026.10; file=invoice.batch.xml; stem=invoice.batch; extension=xml; dots=8,14 ``` ### Complete XPath 3.1 comparison [Runnable file](../examples/import-file-names/baseline.xpath): ```xpath let $path := string(parse-xml('')/file/@path) return let $positions := function($value, $needle) { for $p in 1 to string-length($value) return if (substring($value, $p, string-length($needle)) eq $needle) then $p else () } return let $slash := $positions($path, '/')[last()] return let $directory := substring($path, 1, $slash - 1) return let $name := substring($path, $slash + 1) return let $dots := $positions($name, '.') return let $dot := $dots[last()] return concat('directory=', $directory, '; file=', $name, '; stem=', substring($name, 1, $dot - 1), '; extension=', substring($name, $dot + 1), '; dots=', string-join($dots ! string(.), ',')) ``` Exact output: ```text directory=incoming/2026.10; file=invoice.batch.xml; stem=invoice.batch; extension=xml; dots=8,14 ``` ### Boundary and error inventory Each file embeds its complete input. Brackets make significant spaces visible. | Runnable case | Exact result or diagnostic marker | |---|---| | [main](../examples/import-file-names/main.xpath) | `directory=incoming/2026.10; file=invoice.batch.xml; stem=invoice.batch; extension=xml; dots=8,14` | | [baseline](../examples/import-file-names/baseline.xpath) | `directory=incoming/2026.10; file=invoice.batch.xml; stem=invoice.batch; extension=xml; dots=8,14` | | [compound-extension](../examples/import-file-names/compound-extension.xpath) | `gz` | | [missing-delimiter](../examples/import-file-names/missing-delimiter.xpath) | `[]|[]` | | [empty-delimiter](../examples/import-file-names/empty-delimiter.xpath) | `[invoice]|[]` | | [overlapping](../examples/import-file-names/overlapping.xpath) | `before=a; after=[]; positions=1,2` | | [no-matches](../examples/import-file-names/no-matches.xpath) | `0` | | [empty-search](../examples/import-file-names/empty-search.xpath) | `1,2,3,4` | | [empty-source](../examples/import-file-names/empty-source.xpath) | `0` | | [empty-both](../examples/import-file-names/empty-both.xpath) | `[]|[]` | | [supplementary-position](../examples/import-file-names/supplementary-position.xpath) | `1,3` | | [explicit-collation](../examples/import-file-names/explicit-collation.xpath) | `-c` | | [multi-item-source](../examples/import-file-names/multi-item-source.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | The overlapping fixture reports matches at positions one and two in aaa for aa. Supplementary-character positions verify codepoints. The case-insensitive collation fixture tests a textual delimiter separately from the path rule. Missing/empty delimiters and empty source inputs are distinct cases. ## 14. Performance Position search materializes match positions and text extraction works on supplied strings. The 3.1 comparison scans candidate positions explicitly. No benchmark, filesystem access or universal complexity claim follows. ## 15. Known Uses **Experimental empty-argument correction (source1.24.1):** [Contract](../INDEX-OF-SUBSTRING-CONTRACT.md), [38 public API controls](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/SubstringExperimentalContractTests.cs) and [two host controls](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/SubstringExperimentalHostBoundaryTests.cs) verify the newer absent-pattern result only under `XPath40Experimental`. Frozen `fn-index-of-substring` case021 still requires XPTY0004; current upstream case021 remains a diagnostic failure in the frozen runner. No current-gate promotion or historical provenance recovery is claimed. This importer rule is synthetic. Existing evidence includes [`IndexOfSubstring_SpecExamples`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`IndexOfSubstring_EmptySubstring_MatchesEveryPosition`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`IndexOfSubstring_PositionsInCodepoints`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`SubstringBeforeLast_SpecExamples`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`SubstringAfterLast_SpecExamples`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), and [`SubstringAfterLast_WithCollation`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs). The [4.0 runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs) assigns exact fn-index-of-substring to GatedSets. No exact before-last/after-last assignment is claimed. These 13 executable cases provide separate evidence. Gate membership is unchanged. ## 16. Related Features [Customer text cleanup](customer-text-cleanup.md) distinguishes codepoints and supported grapheme clusters. [Invoice API URIs](invoice-api-uris.md) handles URI boundaries. [The audit](../COMPLETENESS-AUDIT.md) separates reference coverage from exhaustive collation/signature conformance.
