sections.13:
Complete synthetic file record:

```xml
<file path="incoming/2026.10/invoice.batch.xml"/>
```

### Complete XPath 4.0 expression

[Runnable file](../examples/import-file-names/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $path := string(parse-xml('<file path="incoming/2026.10/invoice.batch.xml"/>')/file/@path)
let $directory := substring-before-last($path, '/')
let $name := substring-after-last($path, '/')
return concat('directory=', $directory, '; file=', $name, '; stem=', substring-before-last($name, '.'), '; extension=', substring-after-last($name, '.'), '; dots=', string-join(index-of-substring($name, '.') ! string(.), ','))
```

Exact output:

```text
directory=incoming/2026.10; file=invoice.batch.xml; stem=invoice.batch; extension=xml; dots=8,14
```

### Complete XPath 3.1 comparison

[Runnable file](../examples/import-file-names/baseline.xpath):

```xpath
let $path := string(parse-xml('<file path="incoming/2026.10/invoice.batch.xml"/>')/file/@path)
return let $positions := function($value, $needle) { for $p in 1 to string-length($value) return if (substring($value, $p, string-length($needle)) eq $needle) then $p else () }
return let $slash := $positions($path, '/')[last()]
return let $directory := substring($path, 1, $slash - 1)
return let $name := substring($path, $slash + 1)
return let $dots := $positions($name, '.')
return let $dot := $dots[last()]
return concat('directory=', $directory, '; file=', $name, '; stem=', substring($name, 1, $dot - 1), '; extension=', substring($name, $dot + 1), '; dots=', string-join($dots ! string(.), ','))
```

Exact output:

```text
directory=incoming/2026.10; file=invoice.batch.xml; stem=invoice.batch; extension=xml; dots=8,14
```

Each file embeds its complete input. Brackets make significant spaces visible.

Invoice API URIs

Frozen 4.0 — parse components, build routes and decode values

**C10 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-2.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited verified frozen contract**. Use validated typed Boolean options and remove raw query when deliberately supplying an empty query map. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Invoice API URIs — Frozen 4.0.** [fn:parse-uri](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-parse-uri), [fn:build-uri](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-build-uri), and [fn:decode-from-uri](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-decode-from-uri). Initial engine delivery: [PR #84](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/84), [revision f7f55b4e](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/f7f55b4e3a6e92da26ac607e34f46aede695cb19), REQ-118 4.0-S2. Definitions reviewed **2026-10-11** against immutable [QT4CG function source a014e1b4](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This review pin does not recover the unavailable historical adopted specification snapshot. General syntax references: [RFC 3986](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986) and [RFC 3987](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3987). The pinned function draft also specifies convenient handling for some URI-adjacent strings. ## 2. Intent Construct an invoice API route from a configured endpoint, an invoice identifier and a search value. Preserve a slash inside the identifier as data in one path segment and distinguish a literal plus from a query-parameter space. ## 3. Also Known As URI decomposition, component assembly and percent decoding are descriptive terms. No aliases are registered. Form decoding is a distinct convention used for query parameters, not a synonym for generic URI decoding. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 can assemble a fixed route with `concat` and `encode-for-uri` on each identifier/query value. The complete comparison below constructs the same URI for this configured HTTPS `/v1` endpoint. Its explicit removal of port 443 is scoped to that fixture, not a general-purpose URI parser. XPath 3.1 has no direct standard counterpart to the complete component-record parser or UTF-8 percent decoder; a host implementation or dedicated helper is needed for general decoding. ## 5. Motivation An invoice ID such as INV/2048 may contain a slash as part of its business key. Concatenating it into the route without segment encoding creates two route segments. Likewise, a plus in a search value must not turn into a space when the server form-decodes query parameters. Component-based assembly makes those boundaries explicit before the host uses the resulting address. ## 6. Language Alignment `parse-uri` returns an optional map with raw and derived fields, including scheme, host, integer port, path, decoded path-segments, query, decoded query-parameters and fragment. Repeated query keys collect a sequence of values. Parsing query parameters applies form decoding: plus becomes space before percent decoding. An encoded `%2B` becomes a literal plus. Empty input returns empty. `build-uri` takes a component map. Nonempty path-segments take precedence over path in the demonstrated cases; a nonempty query-parameters map takes precedence over query. A leading empty segment supplies the initial slash. Each hierarchical segment is encoded independently, so a slash inside a segment becomes `%2F`. Query values use their own delimiter-encoding rules. Non-hierarchical schemes such as mailto have different assembly rules; this entry's business route is HTTPS. `decode-from-uri` percent-decodes UTF-8 and leaves ordinary plus signs unchanged. Empty input becomes a zero-length string, unlike parse-uri's empty result. Malformed escapes, invalid UTF-8 and XML-invalid characters become U+FFFD replacement characters in the specified cases, rather than throwing a strict validation error. Do not decode the entire address before identifying its boundaries. The functions have optional options maps for parsing/building. This case uses `omit-default-ports` to omit HTTPS port 443; a nondefault port is preserved. The entry verifies that option and default behavior, not every option/signature. ## 7. Applicability Use for component-aware integration addresses and decoded values. The fixture assumes a validated HTTPS endpoint with the known `/v1` route, a nonempty invoice ID, and a supplied search value. The parser accepts relative references and URI-adjacent strings; successful parsing is not proof that an address is an approved API endpoint or a valid network destination. The host owns endpoint validation, relative-reference resolution and actual network requests. Do not infer a canonical signed-request spelling from a parse/build roundtrip. Keep original wire text when a protocol requires its exact bytes or query order. Generic decoding is permissive and may lose malformed input through replacement. ## 8. Structure Read the request, parse its base endpoint with default-port omission, then build scheme/host/port, separate route segments and a one-key query map. Parse the built URI to verify that invoice ID and search text still have their original values. No HTTP operation is performed. ## 9. Participants The request supplies endpoint and business values. The parser exposes endpoint components. The builder escapes component data and joins delimiters. The parsed result and report demonstrate the roundtrip of the business values. ## 10. Collaborations Pass raw component values to path-segments/query-parameters; do not pre-escape them and then ask the builder to escape again. The fixed 3.1 comparison instead calls `encode-for-uri` before concatenating delimiters. The decoder is useful for a component already isolated from its address; query form handling requires the plus-to-space step first. The form-decoding fixture illustrates that order. ## 11. Consequences Slash, space, question mark, hash and plus are preserved as component data in the verified cases. Parsing/building may change spelling: spaces become escaped, query plus may rebuild as `%20`, and configured default ports may disappear. Repeated query values remain sequences; map iteration does not promise a portable query-key order. The exact builder fixtures use one query key so they do not imply such an ordering contract. Semantic value preservation differs from byte-for-byte roundtripping. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Raw and decoded URI fields, repeated query keys and plus/percent behavior; Structured segment/query precedence and non-byte-preserving roundtrip; One-pass UTF-8 decoding, absence and malformed syntax. **Boundaries:** Use validated typed Boolean options and remove raw query when deliberately supplying an empty query map. Follow-up groups: F01, F04. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Use `CompileOptions.Compatibility40` for the new functions. The default XPath 3.1 profile rejects them. The fixed route comparison uses `Compatibility31`. The existing [catalog harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) checks exact results/errors and default-profile refusal for successful 4.0 cases. All inputs are inline, and the example hostname is illustrative. No external context item, variables, files or HTTP request are required. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** [URI/import utility review](../URI-UTILITY-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md), pinned to F&O e7ee4ab8, and [detailed import/link README](../examples/utility-contracts/README.md) supply 105 checks across five families: keyword modes, component/options/escaping, one-pass UTF-8 decoding, collation availability, identity, NaN and type/cardinality boundaries, plus complete XPath 3.1/4.0 reports. Keywords remain unavailable. Boolean-option/record tolerance and empty query-map precedence remain follow-ups. All 37 absent-keyword families now have first targeted review, with metadata still absent; this does not close D2. Source/public version is 1.1.3; original delivery/unit/gate and historical adopted-pin limits remain. ## 13. Sample Code Complete synthetic input: ```xml ``` [Complete XPath 4.0 expression](../examples/invoice-api-uris/main.xpath): ```xpath let $request := parse-xml('')/request let $base := parse-uri(string($request/@endpoint), map {'omit-default-ports': true()}) let $uri := build-uri(map {'scheme': $base?scheme, 'host': $base?host, 'port': $base?port, 'path-segments': ('', 'v1', 'invoices', string($request/@invoice)), 'query-parameters': map {'q': string($request/@query)}}) let $parsed := parse-uri($uri) return concat('uri=', $uri, '; invoice=', $parsed?path-segments[4], '; query=', $parsed?query-parameters?q) ``` Exact output: ```text uri=https://api.example.test/v1/invoices/INV%2F2048?q=Ada%20Lovelace%20%2B%20VAT; invoice=INV/2048; query=Ada Lovelace + VAT ``` [Complete XPath 3.1 construction comparison](../examples/invoice-api-uris/baseline.xpath): ```xpath let $request := parse-xml('')/request return let $origin := replace(substring-before(string($request/@endpoint), '/v1'), ':443$', '') return let $uri := concat($origin, '/v1/invoices/', encode-for-uri(string($request/@invoice)), '?q=', encode-for-uri(string($request/@query))) return $uri ``` Exact output (URI construction only): ```text https://api.example.test/v1/invoices/INV%2F2048?q=Ada%20Lovelace%20%2B%20VAT ``` ### Delimiters inside the identifier Full input contains both a question mark and a hash in the invoice ID: ```xml ``` The [delimiter fixture](../examples/invoice-api-uris/delimiter-in-id.xpath) reports: ```text uri=https://api.example.test/v1/invoices/INV%3F2048%23A?q=Ada%20Lovelace%20%2B%20VAT; invoice=INV?2048#A; query=Ada Lovelace + VAT ``` ### Complete fixture inventory Each file embeds its full input and exact result or diagnostic marker. `�` below is the literal Unicode replacement character U+FFFD. | Runnable case | Exact result or diagnostic marker | |---|---| | [main](../examples/invoice-api-uris/main.xpath) | `uri=https://api.example.test/v1/invoices/INV%2F2048?q=Ada%20Lovelace%20%2B%20VAT; invoice=INV/2048; query=Ada Lovelace + VAT` | | [baseline](../examples/invoice-api-uris/baseline.xpath) | `https://api.example.test/v1/invoices/INV%2F2048?q=Ada%20Lovelace%20%2B%20VAT` | | [space-in-id](../examples/invoice-api-uris/space-in-id.xpath) | `uri=https://api.example.test/v1/invoices/INV%202048?q=Ada%20Lovelace%20%2B%20VAT; invoice=INV 2048; query=Ada Lovelace + VAT` | | [delimiter-in-id](../examples/invoice-api-uris/delimiter-in-id.xpath) | `uri=https://api.example.test/v1/invoices/INV%3F2048%23A?q=Ada%20Lovelace%20%2B%20VAT; path=../invoices/INV2048; query=ready` | | [fragment-only](../examples/invoice-api-uris/fragment-only.xpath) | `pathCount=0; fragment=summary view` | | [ipv6-host](../examples/invoice-api-uris/ipv6-host.xpath) | `[2001:db8::7]` | | [normalized-roundtrip](../examples/invoice-api-uris/normalized-roundtrip.xpath) | `https://api.example.test/p%20x?q=Ada%20Lovelace#summary%20view` | | [segment-precedence](../examples/invoice-api-uris/segment-precedence.xpath) | `https://api.example.test/invoices/INV%2F2048` | | [query-precedence](../examples/invoice-api-uris/query-precedence.xpath) | `https://api.example.test?q=ready` | | [nonhierarchical](../examples/invoice-api-uris/nonhierarchical.xpath) | `mailto:accounts@example.test` | | [unmatched-ipv6](../examples/invoice-api-uris/unmatched-ipv6.xpath) | `FOUR0001` | | [build-nonmap](../examples/invoice-api-uris/build-nonmap.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | The duplicate-key fixtures parse and rebuild ready/review tags in one key's value sequence. ```xpath

```xpath
let $base := parse-uri(string($request/@endpoint), map {'omit-default-ports': true()})
let $uri := build-uri(map {'scheme': $base?scheme, 'host': $base?host, 'port': $base?port, 'path-segments': ('', 'v1', 'invoices', string($request/@invoice)), 'query-parameters': map {'q': string($request/@query)}})
let $parsed := parse-uri($uri)
return concat('uri=', $uri, '; invoice=', $parsed?path-segments[4], '; query=', $parsed?query-parameters?q)
```

Exact output:

```text
uri=https://api.example.test/v1/invoices/INV%2F2048?q=Ada%20Lovelace%20%2B%20VAT; invoice=INV/2048; query=Ada Lovelace + VAT
```

[Complete XPath 3.1 construction comparison](../examples/invoice-api-uris/baseline.xpath):

```xpath
let $request := parse-xml('<request endpoint="https://api.example.test:443/v1" invoice="INV/2048" query="Ada Lovelace + VAT"/>')/request
return let $origin := replace(substring-before(string($request/@endpoint), '/v1'), ':443$', '')
return let $uri := concat($origin, '/v1/invoices/', encode-for-uri(string($request/@invoice)), '?q=', encode-for-uri(string($request/@query)))
return $uri
```

Exact output (URI construction only):

```text
https://api.example.test/v1/invoices/INV%2F2048?q=Ada%20Lovelace%20%2B%20VAT
```

### Delimiters inside the identifier

Full input contains both a question mark and a hash in the invoice ID:

```xml
<request endpoint="https://api.example.test:443/v1" invoice="INV?2048#A" query="Ada Lovelace + VAT"/>
```

The [delimiter fixture](../examples/invoice-api-uris/delimiter-in-id.xpath) reports:

```text
uri=https://api.example.test/v1/invoices/INV%3F2048%23A?q=Ada%20Lovelace%20%2B%20VAT; invoice=INV?2048#A; query=Ada Lovelace + VAT
```

Map-to-element conversion

Practical reference: Frozen 4.0

**C10 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-2.md) records 2 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited verified frozen contract**. The reduced example does not certify the whole conversion-plan/record/namespaces space; supplementary provider Unicode limits belong to the deferred skip queue. Current-draft escape-names encoding is unsupported; use XML-compatible field names and verified conversion options. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Map-to-element conversion** - **Frozen 4.0**. Delivery family: [REQ-118](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) / [REQ-123 registry](../../FEATURE_REQUESTS.md). Section provenance: See the linked REQ dossiers and implementation evidence. [Primary implementation evidence](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/ElementMapTests.cs) records the shipped behavior; this entry adds executable user-facing examples under REQ-126, rather than announcing a new engine feature. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [fn:map-to-element](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-map-to-element). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #106](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/106), [immutable mainline revision `1bb73147`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/1bb731474c6ba48dded66441183c676a0ebf9761) (2026-10-09). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Convert an agreed map shape back into XML and inspect its text value. ## 3. Also Known As Use the name and spelling in this entry and its executable files. Related functions or instruction forms are described in the primary test evidence; no additional alias is adopted here. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1, an XSLT template or XQuery constructor builds the target XML explicitly. Compare the [complete earlier-version baseline](../examples/map-to-element/before.xsl) with the [complete expression](../examples/map-to-element/main.xpath). Both yield `FILTER-A` for this synthetic input. They demonstrate this task, not universal equivalence of the two mechanisms. ## 5. Motivation A map-based integration step must deliver a small XML product element. Convert an agreed map shape back into XML and inspect its text value. Keeping this task explicit makes it possible to choose the feature for a practical reason and verify what the receiving application will see. ## 6. Language Alignment Read the behavior as XPath/XSLT semantics. Similar vocabulary in another programming language is not a compatibility promise. A conversion is not automatically a lossless round trip for arbitrary mixed-content XML; agree on namespaces and layout. ## 7. Applicability Use this form when solving the stated task and the consumer permits the declared compatibility level. Keep the earlier baseline when the application requires 3.1 expressions or portable 3.0 stylesheets. A conversion is not automatically a lossless round trip for arbitrary mixed-content XML; agree on namespaces and layout. ## 8. Structure ```xquery string(fn:map-to-element(map { 'sku': 'FILTER-A' })) ``` This is the worked case's syntax, not a replacement for the full language grammar. Required namespaces and surrounding context are supplied in the linked complete files. ## 9. Participants XPath31Expression, CompileOptions, the parser/compiler, and the shared runtime/function library provide the public execution path. [Primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/ElementMapTests.cs) identify the feature's implementation contract. The examples use public APIs only. ## 10. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Single tested map-to-XML conversion shape; QName/name/layout, nested content and option boundaries are distinct. **Boundaries:** The reduced example does not certify the whole conversion-plan/record/namespaces space; supplementary provider Unicode limits belong to the deferred skip queue. This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Compile the after/edge expressions at XPathCompatibility.XPath40. The baseline uses XPath31. The example harness checks default-mode refusal for successful 4.0 cases; negative cases pin the declared error. See [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs): it executes the published files from the [case manifest](../examples/cases.json). This documentation slice changes no engine source. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** Keyword drift: implemented input differs from pinned map; the [signature audit](../SIGNATURE-CONTRACT-AUDIT.md) publishes paired success/refusal files. Positional conversion remains separate evidence. ## 13. Sample Code Input is synthetic and declared directly in the complete expression. The [complete expression](../examples/map-to-element/main.xpath) yields `FILTER-A`. The [edge case](../examples/map-to-element/edge.xpath) yields `0`. No external resources or application variables are required. See the [example runner](../examples/README.md) for commands and host context. ## 14. Performance Notes Expected class: output-size dependent construction. The resulting element tree occupies memory in addition to its source map. These are implementation expectations, not measured deltas. No benchmark is claimed; use the repository benchmark harness before making workload-specific speed or memory claims. ## 15. Known Uses Executable example IDs: `map-to-element-main`, `map-to-element-edge`, `map-to-element-before` in `CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome`. Existing unit evidence: [primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/ElementMapTests.cs). Chapter-level evidence does not promote a qt4tests set into GatedSets; conformance status remains owned by the harness and delivery records. **Named implementation evidence:** [`MapToElement_SingleEntryMap_BuildsElement`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/ElementMapTests.cs), [`MapToElement_EmptySequence_ReturnsEmpty`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/ElementMapTests.cs), [`MapToElement_NonMapInput_Xpty0004`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/ElementMapTests.cs). Named frozen gate: `fn-map-to-element`, enforced after the [gate-name repair](../MAP-TO-ELEMENT-GATE-REPAIR.md). The native set contributes156 passed /0 failed /2 skipped; the complete expanded gate passes8,434/0/1,896. Synthetic controls verify that a failing assertion now causes exit2. This is bounded frozen-revision evidence; current-upstream map/element contract changes remain separate. ## 16. Related Features See the [catalog index](../README.md), [worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md), and the alternatives in section 4. The case may be used independently of the larger chapters. *Created 2026-10-11: verified practical catalog example and earlier-version baseline.*

functions/measurement-comparison.md.text:
Typed Measurement Comparison

Frozen 4.0 — a changed existing-function contract

**C10 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-2.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Exact positional comparison; keyword mismatch remains**. Do not substitute this comparator for engineering tolerance, generalized numeric conversion or automatic unit normalization. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. **Related current review:** [Equality/collation contracts](../EQUALITY-COLLATION-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md) refresh the five-family declarations, complete customer example, keyword boundaries and explicitly separate engine findings without replacing the historical evidence below. ## 1. Name and Classification [fn:compare](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-compare) is an existing XPath 3.1 function with expanded 4.0 comparison semantics. It is therefore absent from the 117-name inventory of **4.0-only** functions. Bosak delivery: [PR #112](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/112), [89c90b4d](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/89c90b4d5b6a216a4a37223e169d36e3a1a832bd). Reviewed 2026-10-12 against immutable [QT4CG F&O source e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This is a current review, not recovery of a historical adoption pin. ## 2. Intent Classify imported measurements relative to declared decimal limits while keeping their supplied numeric types. Show why a binary floating-point reading written as `3.1` can compare above or below the decimal value `3.1`. ## 3. Also Known As Three-way comparison, atomic ordering and mixed numeric comparison describe the operation. There is no new registered function name or alias. ## 4. History / Supersedes [F&O 3.1 fn:compare](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions-31/#func-compare) compares optional strings. The reviewed 4.0 draft expands the comparands to optional atomic values. Numeric ordering compares their mathematical values without the usual mixed-type promotion rounding; NaN orders below other numbers and compares equal to NaN. This does not change the meaning of ordinary `eq` or `lt` expressions. The earlier-version report below deliberately normalizes to double and therefore gives a different boundary classification for row B. ## 5. Motivation A measurement feed may combine decimal instrument exports with binary float or double readings. Converting every value to double hides some differences at a decimal threshold. A deterministic comparison can expose those differences for reconciliation. It cannot decide the engineering tolerance: the application must define acceptable deviation and rounding separately. ## 6. Language Alignment Bosak registers `compare#2` and `compare#3`. The result is `-1`, `0` or `1`, or an empty sequence if either comparand is absent. Two numeric values use 4.0 atomic ordering; unrelated type families such as number and string raise `XPTY0004`. Multiple comparands are not a supported singleton contract. The third argument selects string collation. The 4.0 empty-collation form uses the default collation; the fixture's default is codepoint. Explicit ASCII-insensitive and codepoint tests show two distinct label policies. Collation is not a numeric tolerance or a conversion instruction. **Keyword drift:** Bosak accepts `comparand1` and `comparand2`; the pinned draft declares `value1` and `value2`. Current-draft keyword calls are refused with `XPST0017`. Positional calls avoid this spelling mismatch. Keep the observed engine form distinct from the reviewed draft rather than claiming full signature conformance. The earlier-version keyword form is refused with `XPST0003`. ## 7. Applicability Use this report to reconcile typed readings against decimal limits. Input IDs, kind labels and decimal limits are assumed present and valid; kinds are restricted to `decimal`, `float` and `double`. The fixture omits unit conversion, calibration, measurement uncertainty, schema validation and real device acquisition. Missing text and numeric NaN become `missing`; malformed nonempty numeric text still raises a constructor error. This is not a general import validator. ## 8. Structure Parse the synthetic XML, convert each supplied reading according to its declared kind, read its decimal limit, screen absent/NaN values, and classify the sign of the comparison. Emit IDs in input order as a compact reconciliation report. ## 9. Participants The XML carries lexical values and numeric kinds. Constructors create typed atomic values. The guard implements the application's missing-data policy. `compare` returns ordering; the report maps it to `below`, `at-limit` or `above`. ## 10. Collaborations `empty($value)` handles absent data, while `not($value eq $value)` identifies numeric NaN using ordinary equality. sections.1:
[fn:compare](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-compare)
is an existing XPath 3.1 function with expanded 4.0 comparison semantics. It is
therefore absent from the 117-name inventory of **4.0-only** functions.
Bosak delivery: [PR #112](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/112),
[89c90b4d](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/89c90b4d5b6a216a4a37223e169d36e3a1a832bd).
Reviewed 2026-10-12 against immutable
[QT4CG F&O source e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml).
This is a current review, not recovery of a historical adoption pin.
sections.2:
Classify imported measurements relative to declared decimal limits while keeping
their supplied numeric types. Show why a binary floating-point reading written
as `3.1` can compare above or below the decimal value `3.1`.
sections.3:
Three-way comparison, atomic ordering and mixed numeric comparison describe the
operation. There is no new registered function name or alias.
sections.4:
[F&O 3.1 fn:compare](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions-31/#func-compare)
compares optional strings. The reviewed 4.0 draft expands the comparands to
optional atomic values. Numeric ordering compares their mathematical values
without the usual mixed-type promotion rounding; NaN orders below other numbers
and compares equal to NaN. This does not change the meaning of ordinary `eq` or
`lt` expressions. The earlier-version report below deliberately normalizes to
double and therefore gives a different boundary classification for row B.
sections.5:
A measurement feed may combine decimal instrument exports with binary float or
double readings. Converting every value to double hides some differences at a
decimal threshold. A deterministic comparison can expose those differences for
reconciliation. It cannot decide the engineering tolerance: the application must
define acceptable deviation and rounding separately.
sections.6:
Bosak registers `compare#2` and `compare#3`. The result is `-1`, `0` or `1`, or an
empty sequence if either comparand is absent. Two numeric values use 4.0 atomic
ordering; unrelated type families such as number and string raise `XPTY0004`.
Multiple comparands are not a supported singleton contract.

The third argument selects string collation. The 4.0 empty-collation form uses the
default collation; the fixture's default is codepoint. Explicit ASCII-insensitive
and codepoint tests show two distinct label policies. Collation is not a numeric
tolerance or a conversion instruction.

**Keyword drift:** Bosak accepts `comparand1` and `comparand2`; the pinned draft
declares `value1` and `value2`. Current-draft keyword calls are refused with
`XPST0017`. Positional calls avoid this spelling mismatch. Keep the observed
engine form distinct from the reviewed draft rather than claiming full signature
conformance. The earlier-version keyword form is refused with `XPST0003`.
sections.7:
Use this report to reconcile typed readings against decimal limits. Input IDs,
kind labels and decimal limits are assumed present and valid; kinds are restricted
to `decimal`, `float` and `double`. The fixture omits unit conversion, calibration,
measurement uncertainty, schema validation and real device acquisition. Missing
text and numeric NaN become `missing`; malformed nonempty numeric text still
raises a constructor error. This is not a general import validator.
sections.8:
Parse the synthetic XML, convert each supplied reading according to its declared
kind, read its decimal limit, screen absent/NaN values, and classify the sign of
the comparison. Emit IDs in input order as a compact reconciliation report.
sections.9:
The XML carries lexical values and numeric kinds. Constructors create typed
atomic values. The guard implements the application's missing-data policy.
`compare` returns ordering; the report maps it to `below`, `at-limit` or `above`.
sections.10:
`empty($value)` handles absent data, while `not($value eq $value)` identifies
numeric NaN using ordinary equality. The policy screens NaN before ordering it;
otherwise the function would place NaN below the limit. `string-join` preserves
the row classifications. No implicit number/string conversion is requested.

policy. Do not replace the explicit comparator with `eq`/`lt` and expect identical
mixed numeric boundary results. NaN's equality inside this function also does not

sections.13:
Complete synthetic input:

```xml
<readings><reading id="A" kind="decimal" value="2" limit="2"/><reading id="B" kind="double" value="3.1" limit="3.1"/><reading id="C" kind="float" value="3.1" limit="3.1"/><reading id="D" kind="double" value="NaN" limit="3.1"/><reading id="E" kind="double" value="" limit="3.1"/></readings>
```

### XPath 4.0 report

[Runnable file](../examples/measurement-comparison/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $rows := parse-xml('<readings><reading id="A" kind="decimal" value="2" limit="2"/><reading id="B" kind="double" value="3.1" limit="3.1"/><reading id="C" kind="float" value="3.1" limit="3.1"/><reading id="D" kind="double" value="NaN" limit="3.1"/><reading id="E" kind="double" value="" limit="3.1"/></readings>')/readings/reading
return string-join(for $row in $rows return
  let $value := if (string($row/@value) = '') then () else
    if ($row/@kind = 'decimal') then xs:decimal($row/@value) else
    if ($row/@kind = 'float') then xs:float($row/@value) else xs:double($row/@value)
  return let $limit := xs:decimal($row/@limit)
  return let $status := if (empty($value) or not($value eq $value)) then 'missing' else
    let $order := compare($value, $limit)
    return if ($order lt 0) then 'below' else if ($order eq 0) then 'at-limit' else 'above'
  return concat($row/@id, '=', $status), ';')
```

Exact output:

```text
A=at-limit;B=above;C=below;D=missing;E=missing
```

A is decimal 2 against decimal 2. B and C share the decimal limit 3.1 but retain
their distinct binary representations. D contains numeric NaN and E has no value;
both are reported as missing instead of being silently ranked below the limit.

### XPath 3.1 comparison with explicit normalization

[Runnable file](../examples/measurement-comparison/baseline.xpath):

```xpath
let $rows := parse-xml('<readings><reading id="A" kind="decimal" value="2" limit="2"/><reading id="B" kind="double" value="3.1" limit="3.1"/><reading id="C" kind="float" value="3.1" limit="3.1"/><reading id="D" kind="double" value="NaN" limit="3.1"/><reading id="E" kind="double" value="" limit="3.1"/></readings>')/readings/reading
return string-join(for $row in $rows return
  let $value := if (string($row/@value) = '') then () else
    if ($row/@kind = 'decimal') then xs:decimal($row/@value) else
    if ($row/@kind = 'float') then xs:float($row/@value) else xs:double($row/@value)
  return let $limit := xs:decimal($row/@limit)
  return let $status := if (empty($value) or not($value eq $value)) then 'missing' else
    let $normalized := xs:double($value)
    return let $boundary := xs:double($limit)
    return if ($normalized lt $boundary) then 'below' else if ($normalized eq $boundary) then 'at-limit' else 'above'
  return concat($row/@id, '=', $status), ';')
```

Exact output:

```text
A=at-limit;B=at-limit;C=below;D=missing;E=missing
```

This is a different numeric policy, not an exact 3.1 implementation of the 4.0
atomic-ordering function. Stringifying the numbers and calling 3.1 `compare`
would instead compare their text and would be unsuitable for numeric limits.

functions/month-end-cutoffs.md.text:
Month-end Cutoffs

Frozen 4.0 — Gregorian components and explicit timezone offsets

**C10 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-2.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited Gregorian construction; fractional precision gap**. Millisecond precision loss, permissive malformed/multi-item input and interop calendar bounds remain explicit; arbitrary extended-year operations are not certified. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Month-end cutoffs — Frozen 4.0.** [fn:build-dateTime](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-build-dateTime) and [fn:days-in-month](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-days-in-month). Initial engine delivery: [PR #84](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/84), [revision f7f55b4e](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/f7f55b4e3a6e92da26ac607e34f46aede695cb19), REQ-118 4.0-S2. Definitions reviewed **2026-10-11** against immutable [QT4CG function source a014e1b4](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This review pin does not recover the unavailable historical adopted specification snapshot. ## 2. Intent Construct the final-day invoice submission cutoff for a given month, local clock time and explicit offset. Show both the local cutoff and its equivalent UTC instant. ## 3. Also Known As Calendar construction and month-length lookup are descriptive terms; no aliases are registered. The case is a calendar-month cutoff, not a last-business-day rule. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 can find the final date by adding a year-month duration to the first of the month, then subtracting one day. The complete comparison uses `dateTime` to combine that date and a time, then attaches the supplied offset and converts to UTC. Its report matches the 4.0 case; the constructor's result type is not thereby claimed to match the new function's `xs:dateTimeStamp` subtype. ## 5. Motivation Invoice submission calendars may specify a fixed local cutoff on the final day of each month. Hardcoding day 31 fails in shorter months, and February requires the Gregorian century rule. Reporting the UTC instant helps a scheduler consume the local business rule without guessing the offset. ## 6. Language Alignment `days-in-month` accepts an optional `xs:dateTime`, `xs:date` or `xs:gYearMonth`, returning 28, 29, 30 or 31 for its **local** year/month. A value whose UTC instant falls in February may still have a March local month. Leap years are divisible by four, except centuries not divisible by 400. Empty input returns empty. `build-dateTime` constructs a Gregorian value from a component map. Full date and clock components plus timezone produce `xs:dateTimeStamp`; omitting timezone produces `xs:dateTime` without inventing an offset. Date-only fields produce `xs:date`, and clock-only fields produce `xs:time`. Empty input returns empty. Unused components can be absent or empty; arbitrary incomplete field combinations raise FODT0005. Invalid calendar/clock values raise FORG0001; an offset outside ±14 hours raises FODT0003. Midnight uses hour zero, not 24. ## 7. Applicability Use when a rule supplies a calendar month, a local clock time and a numeric UTC offset. This fixture assumes present, valid numeric fields and an explicit whole-minute offset. It does not handle weekends, holidays or business calendars. An offset such as +02:00 is not an IANA timezone and carries no daylight-saving rules; the host must resolve a named zone for the scheduled date before supplying its offset. No implicit timezone or current clock is used here. The subsequent 1.1.3 contract review verifies year-zero date/dateTime and year-10000 date construction, as well as year-zero month-length lookup. These observed forms supersede the earlier blanket construction-limit statement; not every extended-year operation or range is certified. ## 8. Structure Read the schedule, build the first local date, ask for its month length, and build a cutoff on that final day. Convert the already offset-bearing cutoff to UTC with `adjust-dateTime-to-timezone`, preserving its instant. ## 9. Participants Schedule attributes provide year, month, clock and offset. Month-length lookup selects a valid final day. The component constructor creates the cutoff. The UTC projection and report expose the resulting scheduling decision. ## 10. Collaborations The first date has day one so month-length lookup can run before constructing the last date. In the 3.1 comparison, attaching an offset to an unzoned local value establishes its instant; the subsequent UTC conversion preserves that instant. These are two distinct uses of timezone adjustment. ## 11. Consequences The report remains correct for common and leap February and 30-day months. Explicit offsets make both displayed instants deterministic. The function does not silently repair invalid input, derive a timezone from geography, or decide whether the configured cutoff is a working day. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Local Gregorian month/leap rules and supported partial Gregorian values; Timezone presence, field-set, calendar and offset errors; Fractional components and declared singleton/type boundaries. **Boundaries:** Millisecond precision loss, permissive malformed/multi-item input and interop calendar bounds remain explicit; arbitrary extended-year operations are not certified. cutoff=', $cutoff, '; utc=', adjust-dateTime-to-timezone($cutoff, xs:dayTimeDuration('PT0S'))) ``` Exact output: ```text days=29; cutoff=2024-02-29T17:30:00+02:00; utc=2024-02-29T15:30:00Z ``` [Complete XPath 3.1 comparison](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/baseline.xpath): ```xpath let $schedule := parse-xml('')/schedule return let $year := xs:integer($schedule/@year) return let $month := xs:integer($schedule/@month) return let $first := xs:date(concat(format-integer($year, '0000'), '-', format-integer($month, '00'), '-01')) return let $last := $first + xs:yearMonthDuration('P1M') - xs:dayTimeDuration('P1D') return let $local := dateTime($last, xs:time(concat(format-integer(xs:integer($schedule/@hours), '00'), ':', format-integer(xs:integer($schedule/@minutes), '00'), ':00'))) return let $cutoff := adjust-dateTime-to-timezone($local, xs:dayTimeDuration($schedule/@timezone)) return concat('days=', day-from-date($last), '; sections.13:
Complete synthetic schedule input:

```xml
<schedule year="2024" month="2" hours="17" minutes="30" timezone="PT2H"/>
```

[Complete XPath 4.0 expression](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $schedule := parse-xml('<schedule year="2024" month="2" hours="17" minutes="30" timezone="PT2H"/>')/schedule
let $year := xs:integer($schedule/@year)
let $month := xs:integer($schedule/@month)
let $days := days-in-month(build-dateTime(map {'year': $year, 'month': $month, 'day': 1}))
let $cutoff := build-dateTime(map {'year': $year, 'month': $month, 'day': $days, 'hours': xs:integer($schedule/@hours), 'minutes': xs:integer($schedule/@minutes), 'seconds': 0, 'timezone': xs:dayTimeDuration($schedule/@timezone)})
return concat('days=', $days, '; cutoff=', $cutoff, '; utc=', adjust-dateTime-to-timezone($cutoff, xs:dayTimeDuration('PT0S')))
```

Exact output:

```text
days=29; cutoff=2024-02-29T17:30:00+02:00; utc=2024-02-29T15:30:00Z
```

[Complete XPath 3.1 comparison](../examples/month-end-cutoffs/baseline.xpath):

```xpath
let $schedule := parse-xml('<schedule year="2024" month="2" hours="17" minutes="30" timezone="PT2H"/>')/schedule
return let $year := xs:integer($schedule/@year)
return let $month := xs:integer($schedule/@month)
return let $first := xs:date(concat(format-integer($year, '0000'), '-', format-integer($month, '00'), '-01'))
return let $last := $first + xs:yearMonthDuration('P1M') - xs:dayTimeDuration('P1D')
return let $local := dateTime($last, xs:time(concat(format-integer(xs:integer($schedule/@hours), '00'), ':', format-integer(xs:integer($schedule/@minutes), '00'), ':00')))
return let $cutoff := adjust-dateTime-to-timezone($local, xs:dayTimeDuration($schedule/@timezone))
return concat('days=', day-from-date($last), '; cutoff=', $cutoff, '; utc=', adjust-dateTime-to-timezone($cutoff, xs:dayTimeDuration('PT0S')))
```

Exact output:

```text
days=29; cutoff=2024-02-29T17:30:00+02:00; utc=2024-02-29T15:30:00Z
```


Numeric Import Diagnostics

Frozen 4.0 — verified integration contracts and limitations

**C10 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-2.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Blocked empty-annotation contract**. No complete derived-type reflection/function-conversion audit; C03 owns constructor/type/coercion coverage. atomic-type-annotation(()) incorrectly returns a type record in both 4.0 profiles. Required empty-input refusal is explicitly unsupported; bounded correction F08-atomic-annotation-empty retains the independent XPTY0004 expectation. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification Functions: [fn:is-NaN](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-is-NaN), [fn:atomic-type-annotation](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-atomic-type-annotation), [fn:op](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-op). Frozen 4.0. Type/NaN delivery [PR #112](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/112), [89c90b4d](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/89c90b4d5b6a216a4a37223e169d36e3a1a832bd); operator accessor [PR #102](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/102), [2c71d1ea](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/2c71d1ea544ec2d5ab94c40c7bfabb0bc94e63c5). Reviewed 2026-10-12 against immutable [QT4CG function source e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This is a current review pin, not recovery of the unavailable historical adopted snapshot. ## 2. Intent Report accepted and rejected measurement rows, total their numeric values with an addition callback, and inspect the aggregate atomic type for diagnostics. ## 3. Also Known As NaN detection, type reflection and operator callbacks are descriptive terms; no aliases are registered. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 detects a numeric NaN because it is not equal to itself, and uses function($x,$y){$x+$y} as an addition callback. The comparison tests instance of xs:double rather than reproducing the full type-annotation record, for which standard 3.1 has no direct equivalent. ## 5. Motivation A measurement import can contain malformed numeric text. Silently adding NaN would spoil the total, while losing rejected identifiers would make correction difficult. This report keeps row classification and aggregate type visible. ## 6. Language Alignment is-NaN atomizes a single supplied value and tests whether it is numeric NaN. The string 'NaN' itself is not numeric NaN; number('invalid') is. functions/order-sequence-selection.md.text:
Order-export sequence selection

Frozen 4.0 — verified reference contracts

**C10 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-2.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited verified frozen contract**. Integral-decimal tolerance is not the declared integer-position contract; repeat counts must remain bounded. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Order-export sequence selection — Frozen 4.0.** Shipped in [Bosak PR #82](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/82) at immutable revision [`40ebaa79`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/40ebaa79032b17fc45d6d3bb3e58cb00e2fda742). Functions: [fn:replicate](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-replicate), [fn:slice](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-slice), [fn:items-at](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-items-at), [fn:foot](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-foot), [fn:trunk](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-trunk), [fn:insert-separator](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-insert-separator). Definitions reviewed 2026-10-11 against immutable [QT4CG function source `a014e1b4`](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This is a review pin, not evidence of the historical adopted snapshot, which remains unavailable. ## 2. Intent Export an inclusive page from an ordered dispatch queue, retain its final record as a boundary marker, and generate one label run for each of two packing stations. A separate selection probe follows an operator’s requested positions, including repeated positions. ## 3. Also Known As Exact spellings are `fn:replicate`, `fn:slice`, `fn:items-at`, `fn:foot`, `fn:trunk` and `fn:insert-separator`. Unprefixed names in the examples use the default function namespace. No aliases are introduced. ## 4. History / Supersedes The main XPath 3.1 comparison uses `subsequence($queue,2,3)`, predicates with `last()`, a repeated `for` result and `string-join`. The requested-position comparison iterates positions and selects `$queue[$p]`. These are equivalents for the illustrated data; `subsequence` takes a length, while `slice` takes an inclusive end and can reverse or stride. ## 5. Motivation Queue pagination, final-record checkpoints and requested label order are different operations. `items-at` retains requested-position order and duplicates; a filter such as `$queue[position()=(5,2,2)]` would instead retain queue order and omit the repeated selection. ## 6. Language Alignment XPath uses one-based positions and inclusive slice ends. Empty/zero bounds mean defaults, not JavaScript’s zero-based origin. Negative bounds count from the end. An omitted/zero step infers direction: `slice($queue,4,2)` reverses those positions. `replicate` repeats the entire input sequence, not each item in turn. `insert-separator` inserts an arbitrary sequence between adjacent items; it is not itself a string serializer. ## 7. Applicability Use after a stable business ordering is established. Positional offsets are not durable pagination cursors if concurrent inserts can change the queue. `replicate` creates repeated references for nodes rather than copying trees; prevent duplicate shipment execution when repeated labels are only presentation data. ## 8. Structure ```xquery slice($queue, $start, $end, $step) items-at($queue, $positions) foot($page) trunk($page) replicate($page, $count) insert-separator($labels, $separator) ``` Positional and shorter callback forms are exercised by the exact files below. This entry covers the illustrated contracts rather than every arity or option. ## 9. Participants Existing `FunctionLibrary` frozen registrations select these names only at `XPathCompatibility.XPath40` or higher. The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) compiles each file at its declared mode and checks default XPath31 refusal for successful 4.0 forms. ## 10. Collaborations The [routing chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md) preserves dispatch arrival order and splits it into consecutive route/capacity partitions. Selection is not partitioning: it chooses positions without assigning all records to batches. ## 11. Consequences Out-of-range `items-at` positions are ignored; duplicate requested positions remain duplicated. Fractional positions fail XPTY0004. `foot(())` and `trunk` of an empty/singleton sequence are empty. `replicate` of empty input or with count zero is empty; negative count fails XPTY0004. A separator can contain several items, and no separator is inserted for empty or singleton input. Negative-step slices reverse traversal, while a mismatched explicit direction yields no items. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Whole-sequence repetition and separator insertion; One-based positions, duplicates, inclusive/negative/default slice bounds; Empty/singleton input, negative counts and invalid positions. **Boundaries:** Integral-decimal tolerance is not the declared integer-position contract; repeat counts must remain bounded. Follow-up groups: F01, F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Implementation: [FunctionLibrary.cs](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs); [named unit tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs); [manifest](../examples/cases.json). Names refuse XPST0017 in default XPath31; the comparisons remain valid at XPath31. Source/package version stays 1.1.2. This reference work changes no engine code. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** [Six-family review](../SEQUENCE-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md) against F&O e7ee4ab8 and [detailed dispatch-batch README](../examples/sequence-contracts/README.md) supply 65 checks, explicit keyword modes, defaults/empty/direction/types, node identity and complete normal/empty/reordered reports in 3.1/4.0. Five keyword families remain absent; slice keywords work in the tested forms. items-at tolerates integral decimal positions; replicate/slice reject them. Untyped-node positions refuse; precise coercion remains an explicit follow-up, not a conformance claim. Historical delivery/adopted-pin limits are unchanged. ## 13. Sample Code Input is declared inside each expression: reduced order/product records, no document focus, external variables or resource access. Namespace prefixes `map` and `array` use the standard public API bindings. Outputs are exact text projections of XDM results, not serialized supplier or ERP formats. **Main — mode 40:** [main.xpath](../examples/order-sequence-selection/main.xpath) ```xquery (: Export positions 2 through 4; repeat the label set for two packing stations. :) let $queue := ('ORD-101','ORD-102','ORD-103','ORD-104','ORD-105'), $page := slice($queue, 2, 4), $labels := replicate($page, 2) return concat('page=', string-join($page, ','), ';last=', foot($page), ';body=', string-join(trunk($page), ','), ';labels=', string-join(insert-separator($labels, '|'), '')) ``` Expected text: ```text page=ORD-102,ORD-103,ORD-104;last=ORD-104;body=ORD-102,ORD-103;labels=ORD-102|ORD-103|ORD-104|ORD-102|ORD-103|ORD-104 ``` **Baseline — mode 31:** [baseline.xpath](../examples/order-sequence-selection/baseline.xpath) ```xquery let $queue := ('ORD-101','ORD-102','ORD-103','ORD-104','ORD-105'), $page := subsequence($queue, 2, 3), $labels := for $station in 1 to 2 return $page return concat('page=', string-join($page, ','), ';last=', $page[last()], ';body=', string-join($page[position() lt last()], ','), ';labels=', string-join($labels, '|')) ``` Expected text: ```text page=ORD-102,ORD-103,ORD-104;last=ORD-104;body=ORD-102,ORD-103;labels=ORD-102|ORD-103|ORD-104|ORD-102|ORD-103|ORD-104 ``` **Edge — mode 40:** [edge.xpath](../examples/order-sequence-selection/edge.xpath) ```xquery concat(count(slice((),2,4)), '/', count(replicate((),2)), '/', count(foot(())), '/', count(trunk(())), '/', count(insert-separator((), '|')), '/', count(items-at((),1))) ``` Expected text: ```text 0/0/0/0/0/0 ``` **Additional executable contracts:** | Case | Mode | Expected text or error | |---|---|---| | [requested-positions](../examples/order-sequence-selection/requested-positions.xpath) | 40 | `ORD-105,ORD-102,ORD-102` | | [requested-baseline](../examples/order-sequence-selection/requested-baseline.xpath) | 31 | `ORD-105,ORD-102,ORD-102` | | [negative-bounds](../examples/order-sequence-selection/negative-bounds.xpath) | 40 | `ORD-104,ORD-105` | | [reverse](../examples/order-sequence-selection/reverse.xpath) | 40 | `ORD-105,ORD-104,ORD-103,ORD-102,ORD-101` | | [automatic-direction](../examples/order-sequence-selection/automatic-direction.xpath) | 40 | `ORD-104,ORD-103,ORD-102` | | [step](../examples/order-sequence-selection/step.xpath) | 40 | 40 | `0` | | [negative-repeat](../examples/order-sequence-selection/negative-repeat.xpath) | 40 | `XPTY0004` | | [fractional-position](../examples/order-sequence-selection/fractional-position.xpath) | Definitions reviewed 2026-10-11 against immutable [QT4CG function source `a014e1b4`](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This is a review pin, not evidence of the historical adopted snapshot, which remains unavailable.
sections.2: Export an inclusive page from an ordered dispatch queue, retain its final record as a boundary marker, and generate one label run for each of two packing stations. A separate selection probe follows an operator’s requested positions, including repeated positions.
sections.3: Exact spellings are `fn:replicate`, `fn:slice`, `fn:items-at`, `fn:foot`, `fn:trunk` and `fn:insert-separator`. Unprefixed names in the examples use the default function namespace. No aliases are introduced.
sections.4: The main XPath 3.1 comparison uses `subsequence($queue,2,3)`, predicates with `last()`, a repeated `for` result and `string-join`. The requested-position comparison iterates positions and selects `$queue[$p]`. These are equivalents for the illustrated data; `subsequence` takes a length, while `slice` takes an inclusive end and can reverse or stride.
sections.5: Queue pagination, final-record checkpoints and requested label order are different operations. `items-at` retains requested-position order and duplicates; a filter such as `$queue[position()=(5,2,2)]` would instead retain queue order and omit the repeated selection.
sections.6: XPath uses one-based positions and inclusive slice ends. Empty/zero bounds mean defaults, not JavaScript’s zero-based origin. Negative bounds count from the end. An omitted/zero step infers direction: `slice($queue,4,2)` reverses those positions. `replicate` repeats the entire input sequence, not each item in turn. `insert-separator` inserts an arbitrary sequence between adjacent items; it is not itself a string serializer.
sections.7: Use after a stable business ordering is established. Positional offsets are not durable pagination cursors if concurrent inserts can change the queue. `replicate` creates repeated references for nodes rather than copying trees; prevent duplicate shipment execution when repeated labels are only presentation data.
sections.8:
```xquery
slice($queue, $start, $end, $step)
items-at($queue, $positions)
foot($page)
trunk($page)
replicate($page, $count)
insert-separator($labels, $separator)
```

Positional and shorter callback forms are exercised by the exact files below. This entry covers the illustrated contracts rather than every arity or option.
sections.9: Existing `FunctionLibrary` frozen registrations select these names only at `XPathCompatibility.XPath40` or higher. The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) compiles each file at its declared mode and checks default XPath31 refusal for successful 4.0 forms.
sections.10: The [routing chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md) preserves dispatch arrival order and splits it into consecutive route/capacity partitions. Selection is not partitioning: it chooses positions without assigning all records to batches.
sections.11: Out-of-range `items-at` positions are ignored; duplicate requested positions remain duplicated. Fractional positions fail XPTY0004. `foot(())` and `trunk` of an empty/singleton sequence are empty. `replicate` of empty input or with count zero is empty; negative count fails XPTY0004. A separator can contain several items, and no separator is inserted for empty or singleton input. Negative-step slices reverse traversal, while a mismatched explicit direction yields no items.

```xquery
return concat('page=', string-join($page, ','), ';last=', foot($page), ';body=', string-join(trunk($page), ','), ';labels=', string-join(insert-separator($labels, '|'), ''))
```

functions/ordered-queue-prefix.md.text:
Ordered Queue Prefix

Frozen 4.0 — dispatch the ready prefix and retain the remainder

**C10 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-2.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited verified frozen contract**. Not an arbitrary filter or partition; no operational side effects or general callable-subtyping promise. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Ordered queue prefix — Frozen 4.0.** [fn:take-while](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-take-while) and [fn:drop-while](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-drop-while). Initial engine delivery: [PR #88](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/88), [revision 0a928bb8](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/0a928bb81b81d0631cc681f86bba83259c0ed790), REQ-118 4.0-S5. Definitions reviewed 2026-10-11 against the immutable [QT4CG function source a014e1b4](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This review pin does not recover the unavailable historical adopted specification snapshot. ## 2. Intent Split an ordered dispatch queue at its first non-ready order. Dispatch the ready prefix and retain the blocking order together with every later order for investigation. ## 3. Also Known As Prefix selection and prefix removal. These descriptive terms introduce no function aliases. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 can locate the first failing position and use `subsequence` for both parts. The complete comparison below uses explicit nested `let … return` expressions and the same status rule. Filtering ready orders throughout the queue implements a different business policy: it lets later orders overtake a blocker. ## 5. Motivation A warehouse may preserve acceptance order because orders share a shipment, reservation or review process. A held order blocks later dispatch even when a later order is individually ready. The example makes that policy visible in its report. ## 6. Language Alignment Both functions accept an `item()*` input and a predicate receiving the item and its one-based input position, returning `xs:boolean?`. `false()` or `()` marks the boundary. `take-while` excludes that item; `drop-while` includes it and all later items. Empty input gives empty results; all matching input is returned by `take-while` and removed by `drop-while`. A string such as `'ready'` is not a boolean predicate result and raises XPTY0004. Bosak also accepts a map as a one-argument callable predicate; a missing key returns empty and stops selection. The fixtures use ordinary two-argument inline functions for the business rule. ## 7. Applicability Use when input order is authoritative and the first failed condition blocks subsequent work. If independent ready orders may proceed, use a filter instead. The sample assumes nonempty, unique order identifiers supplied by upstream validation. It does not validate identities, sort timestamps, persist a queue, reserve inventory or send a shipment. Missing status is treated as non-ready. ## 8. Structure `input → readiness predicate → ready prefix + retained remainder`. The order sequence consists of XML element nodes, not their identifier strings. The report projects identifiers only after the split. ## 9. Participants The queue preserves arrival order. Each order supplies an identifier and status. The predicate defines readiness. The two functions select nodes. The report shows dispatch and retained identifiers so the boundary is reviewable. ## 10. Collaborations Supply the same deterministic predicate to both calls. Concatenating the two results reconstructs the input with order and node identity preserved. The calls are independent and repeat predicate work; changing state between calls would invalidate the business assumption behind the split. ## 11. Consequences The first held order and every later ready order remain visible. No order is silently discarded or moved. An empty queue needs no dispatch; an entirely ready queue leaves no remainder. These are selection decisions, not operational side effects. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Prefix-only selection with first nonmatch excluded/included; Original input positions and empty/all-match queues; Boolean/empty predicates and tested callable maps. **Boundaries:** Not an arbitrary filter or partition; no operational side effects or general callable-subtyping promise. Follow-up groups: F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Compile the 4.0 expressions with `CompileOptions.Compatibility40`. The default 3.1 profile rejects the new functions. The comparison uses `Compatibility31`. The existing [catalog test harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) checks exact text/error outcomes and default-profile refusal for successful 4.0 cases. No external files, variables, services or context item are required. ## 13. Sample Code The synthetic fixture represents a warehouse queue in arrival order. ORD103 is held for investigation; ORD104 must wait behind it despite its ready status. ```xml ``` Complete XPath 4.0 expression ([runnable file](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/main.xpath)): ```xpath let $queue := parse-xml('')/queue/order let $ready := function($order, $position) { string($order/@status) eq 'ready' } let $dispatch := take-while($queue, $ready) let $retained := drop-while($queue, $ready) return concat('dispatch=', string-join($dispatch/@id, ','), '; retained=', string-join($retained/@id, ',')) ``` Exact output: ```text dispatch=ORD101,ORD102; retained=ORD103,ORD104 ``` Complete XPath 3.1 comparison ([runnable file](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/baseline.xpath)): ```xpath let $queue := parse-xml('')/queue/order return let $stop := ((for $i in 1 to count($queue) return if (string($queue[$i]/@status) eq 'ready') then () else $i)[1], count($queue) + 1)[1] return let $dispatch := subsequence($queue, 1, $stop - 1) return let $retained := subsequence($queue, $stop) return concat('dispatch=', string-join($dispatch/@id, ','), '; retained=', string-join($retained/@id, ',')) ``` Its exact output is identical. A whole-queue filter instead returns `ORD101,ORD102,ORD104`, as the [filter comparison](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/filter-comparison.xpath) verifies. It would allow ORD104 to overtake the held order. ### Boundary and callback cases Each file embeds its complete input. Empty output below means an empty string from the report's `string-join`, not a string returned by the selection function. | Runnable case | Exact result or error | Meaning | |---|---|---| | [main](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/main.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101,ORD102; retained=ORD103,ORD104` | Normal ordered split | | [baseline](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/baseline.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101,ORD102; retained=ORD103,ORD104` | Earlier-version equivalent | | [filter-comparison](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/filter-comparison.xpath) | `ORD101,ORD102,ORD104` | Independent ready-order policy | | [all-ready](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/all-ready.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101,ORD102,ORD103,ORD104; retained=` | No blocker | | [first-held](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/first-held.xpath) | `dispatch=; retained=ORD101,ORD102,ORD103,ORD104` | First order blocks all work | | [empty](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/empty.xpath) | `dispatch=; retained=` | No orders | | [missing-status](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/missing-status.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101,ORD102; retained=ORD103,ORD104` | Missing status blocks dispatch | | [position-cap](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/position-cap.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101; retained=ORD102,ORD103,ORD104` | One-based capacity boundary | | [reconstruction](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/reconstruction.xpath) | `true` | Both parts restore input | | [map-predicate](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/map-predicate.xpath) | `ready,ready` | Status map used as callable | | [take-empty-decision](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/take-empty-decision.xpath) | `(empty string)` | Empty decision stops immediately | | [take-nonboolean](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/take-nonboolean.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | Strict boolean result | | [take-noncallable](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/take-noncallable.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | Predicate must be callable | | [take-early-stop](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/take-early-stop.xpath) | `ORD101` | Later predicate error is not evaluated | | [drop-empty-decision](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/drop-empty-decision.xpath) | `ORD101,ORD102` | Empty decision retains everything | | [drop-nonboolean](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/drop-nonboolean.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | Strict boolean result | | [drop-noncallable](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/drop-noncallable.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | Predicate must be callable | | [drop-early-stop](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/drop-early-stop.xpath) | `ORD102,ORD103` | Later predicate error is not evaluated | For the missing-status case the full input is the XML above with ORD103's `status="hold"` attribute removed; the exact report remains the normal report. The all-ready case changes that attribute to `status="ready"` and dispatches all four identifiers. The first-held case changes ORD101 to `hold` and retains all four. The empty fixture is `` and reports `dispatch=; retained=`. The position-cap fixture allows only position one: it reports `dispatch=ORD101; retained=ORD102,ORD103,ORD104`. ## 14. Performance Bosak stops invoking the predicate at the boundary, as the early-stop fixtures verify. `drop-while` still copies the retained items, and both implementations materialize their results. Two calls repeat the prefix scan. No streaming or benchmark claim follows from this example; for an expensive predicate, locate the boundary once and slice the queue as in the earlier-version comparison. ## 15. Known Uses The warehouse scenario is a reproducible synthetic example, not a claim about an identified production deployment. Existing named unit evidence includes [`TakeWhile_StopsAtFirstNonMatch`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`TakeWhile_MapAsPredicate_LooksUpEachItem`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`TakeWhile_EmptyPredicateResultMeansFalse`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`DropWhile_DropsPrefixUpToFirstNonMatch`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), and [`DropWhile_TakeWhile_ReconstructInput`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs). The [4.0 gate runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs) assigns exactly `fn-take-while` to GatedSets. No exact `fn-drop-while` set is assigned; its unit tests and executable examples provide separate evidence. This documentation delivery changes no gate membership. ## 16. Related Features [Order sequence selection](order-sequence-selection.md) covers general selection and positions. [Shipment-event sequence checks](shipment-event-sequences.md) covers identity and contiguous event rules. [The completeness audit](../COMPLETENESS-AUDIT.md) tracks the remaining higher-order families and reference coverage limits.

The first held order and every later ready order remain visible. No order is
silently discarded or moved. An empty queue needs no dispatch; an entirely ready
queue leaves no remainder. These are selection decisions, not operational side effects.
sections.12:
**C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Prefix-only selection with first nonmatch excluded/included; Original input positions and empty/all-match queues; Boolean/empty predicates and tested callable maps. **Boundaries:** Not an arbitrary filter or partition; no operational side effects or general callable-subtyping promise. Follow-up groups: F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance.

Compile the 4.0 expressions with `CompileOptions.Compatibility40`. The default
3.1 profile rejects the new functions. The comparison uses `Compatibility31`.
The existing [catalog test harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs)
checks exact text/error outcomes and default-profile refusal for successful 4.0 cases.
No external files, variables, services or context item are required.
sections.13:
The synthetic fixture represents a warehouse queue in arrival order. ORD103 is
held for investigation; ORD104 must wait behind it despite its ready status.

```xml
<queue>
  <order id="ORD101" status="ready"/>
  <order id="ORD102" status="ready"/>
  <order id="ORD103" status="hold"/>
  <order id="ORD104" status="ready"/>
</queue>
```

Complete XPath 4.0 expression ([runnable file](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/main.xpath)):

```xpath
let $queue := parse-xml('<queue><order id="ORD101" status="ready"/><order id="ORD102" status="ready"/><order id="ORD103" status="hold"/><order id="ORD104" status="ready"/></queue>')/queue/order
let $ready := function($order, $position) { string($order/@status) eq 'ready' }
let $dispatch := take-while($queue, $ready)
let $retained := drop-while($queue, $ready)
return concat('dispatch=', string-join($dispatch/@id, ','), '; retained=', string-join($retained/@id, ','))
```

Exact output:

```text
dispatch=ORD101,ORD102; retained=ORD103,ORD104
```

Complete XPath 3.1 comparison ([runnable file](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/baseline.xpath)):

```xpath
let $queue := parse-xml('<queue><order id="ORD101" status="ready"/><order id="ORD102" status="ready"/><order id="ORD103" status="hold"/><order id="ORD104" status="ready"/></queue>')/queue/order
return let $stop := ((for $i in 1 to count($queue) return if (string($queue[$i]/@status) eq 'ready') then () else $i)[1], count($queue) + 1)[1]
return let $dispatch := subsequence($queue, 1, $stop - 1)
return let $retained := subsequence($queue, $stop)
return concat('dispatch=', string-join($dispatch/@id, ','), '; retained=', string-join($retained/@id, ','))
```

Its exact output is identical. A whole-queue filter instead returns
`ORD101,ORD102,ORD104`, as the [filter comparison](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/filter-comparison.xpath)
verifies. It would allow ORD104 to overtake the held order.

### Boundary and callback cases

Each file embeds its complete input. Empty output below means an empty string
from the report's `string-join`, not a string returned by the selection function.

| Runnable case | Exact result or error | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| [main](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/main.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101,ORD102; retained=ORD103,ORD104` | Normal ordered split |
| [baseline](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/baseline.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101,ORD102; retained=ORD103,ORD104` | Earlier-version equivalent |
| [filter-comparison](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/filter-comparison.xpath) | `ORD101,ORD102,ORD104` | Independent ready-order policy |
| [all-ready](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/all-ready.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101,ORD102,ORD103,ORD104; retained=` | No blocker |
| [first-held](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/first-held.xpath) | `dispatch=; retained=ORD101,ORD102,ORD103,ORD104` | First order blocks all work |
| [empty](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/empty.xpath) | `dispatch=; retained=` | No orders |
| [missing-status](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/missing-status.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101,ORD102; retained=ORD103,ORD104` | Missing status blocks dispatch |
| [position-cap](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/position-cap.xpath) | `dispatch=ORD101; retained=ORD102,ORD103,ORD104` | One-based capacity boundary |
| [reconstruction](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/reconstruction.xpath) | `true` | Both parts restore input |
| [map-predicate](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/map-predicate.xpath) | `ready,ready` | Status map used as callable |
| [take-empty-decision](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/take-empty-decision.xpath) | `(empty string)` | Empty decision stops immediately |
| [take-nonboolean](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/take-nonboolean.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | Strict boolean result |
| [take-noncallable](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/take-noncallable.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | Predicate must be callable |
| [take-early-stop](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/take-early-stop.xpath) | `ORD101` | Later predicate error is not evaluated |
| [drop-empty-decision](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/drop-empty-decision.xpath) | `ORD101,ORD102` | Empty decision retains everything |
| [drop-nonboolean](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/drop-nonboolean.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | Strict boolean result |
| [drop-noncallable](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/drop-noncallable.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | Predicate must be callable |
| [drop-early-stop](../examples/ordered-queue-prefix/drop-early-stop.xpath) | `ORD102,ORD103` | Later predicate error is not evaluated |

For the missing-status case the full input is the XML above with ORD103's
`status="hold"` attribute removed; the exact report remains the normal report.
The all-ready case changes that attribute to `status="ready"` and dispatches all
four identifiers. The first-held case changes ORD101 to `hold` and retains all
four. The empty fixture is `<queue/>` and reports `dispatch=; retained=`.
The position-cap fixture allows only position one: it reports
`dispatch=ORD101; retained=ORD102,ORD103,ORD104`.
sections.14:
Bosak stops invoking the predicate at the boundary, as the early-stop fixtures
verify. `drop-while` still copies the retained items, and both implementations
materialize their results. Two calls repeat the prefix scan. No streaming or
benchmark claim follows from this example; for an expensive predicate, locate
the boundary once and slice the queue as in the earlier-version comparison.
