an identified production deployment. Existing named unit evidence includes
[`TakeWhile_StopsAtFirstNonMatch`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs),
[`TakeWhile_MapAsPredicate_LooksUpEachItem`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs),

assigned; its unit tests and executable examples provide separate evidence.

functions/payload-fingerprints.md.text:
Payload Fingerprints

Frozen 4.0 — verified integration contracts and limitations

**C10 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-2.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited verified frozen contract**. BLAKE3 and CRC-32 remain unsupported FOHA0001; opaque hash options do not establish a missing standard named parameter. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification Function: [fn:hash](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-hash). Frozen 4.0. Original delivery [PR #83](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/83), [532d04f4](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/532d04f4672df430d93752e3158fc3cdfd4c7c39). Reviewed 2026-10-12 against immutable [QT4CG function source e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This is a current review pin, not recovery of the unavailable historical adopted snapshot. ## 2. Intent Compute an explicit SHA-256 fingerprint of a supplied invoice payload string so repeated or changed payload content can be compared. ## 3. Also Known As Digest and content fingerprint describe the operation. No aliases are registered. A fingerprint is not an authenticated message signature. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 has no standard hash function. Supply a verified digest from the host or an extension instead of claiming a pure standard-3.1 equivalent. The SHA-256 report below was independently computed with Python hashlib over the same UTF-8 payload. ## 5. Motivation An import log can compare payload content across repeated receipts. Keeping the algorithm and exact input text explicit prevents a digest over normalized text from being mistaken for one over original transport bytes. ## 6. Language Alignment hash accepts an optional string, hexBinary or base64Binary and returns optional hexBinary. Strings are hashed as UTF-8; binary values supply their octets. Empty sequence returns empty, whereas an empty string has a digest. Algorithm defaults to MD5; this case explicitly chooses SHA-256. Unsupported algorithms raise FOHA0001. The examples verify selected algorithm forms and default behavior, not every algorithm/options combination. ## 7. Applicability The payload is a deliberately defined text representation INV-2048|EUR|125.00, not a serialization of arbitrary XML. The sample hashes the payload element string value, not XML markup. To fingerprint exact acquired bytes, pass those bytes as binary. Canonicalizing XML/JSON or authenticating a sender requires a separate protocol; no canonicalization or signature is performed here. ## 8. Structure Read the text payload, call hash with SHA-256, then report the hex representation, its character length and result type. ## 9. Participants The payload defines content. Algorithm selection defines the digest method. The binary result and its textual report provide comparison values. ## 10. Collaborations Use the same representation and algorithm for comparisons. Trailing whitespace and a changed amount produce different digests in the fixtures. Binary abc and UTF-8 string abc yield the same bytes/digest. ## 11. Consequences Content changes are observable without exposing a claim about sender identity. Empty versus absent payload remains distinct. The default-MD5 fixture records the API default; the business example chooses its algorithm explicitly. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles UTF-8 string versus binary octets and absent versus empty payload; Default/explicit algorithm and unsupported-algorithm errors; Keyword/default/map-shape boundaries; extension parameters are implementation-defined. **Boundaries:** BLAKE3 and CRC-32 remain unsupported FOHA0001; opaque hash options do not establish a missing standard named parameter. Follow-up groups: F01, F11. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Compile new functions with CompileOptions.Compatibility40; default 3.1 rejects them. Earlier-version comparisons use Compatibility31. The [catalog harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) verifies exact text/error markers and default-profile refusal for successful 4.0 cases. All values are inline and deterministic. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** The [signature/options review](../SIGNATURE-CONTRACT-AUDIT.md) and [invoice fingerprint README](../examples/signature-contracts/README.md) add selected default/empty/invalid/map/keyword checks and a full business report. Additional hash options are implementation-defined in the pinned contract; opaque-key tolerance does not establish a missing standard option. Mandatory BLAKE3/CRC-32 remain unsupported. Tested two-let keyword calls refuse hash#0; the positional report is the verified alternative. ## 13. Sample Code Complete synthetic input: ```xml INV-2048|EUR|125.00 ``` ### XPath 4.0 expression [Runnable file](../examples/payload-fingerprints/main.xpath): ```xpath let $payload := string(parse-xml('INV-2048|EUR|125.00')/payload) let $digest := hash($payload, 'SHA-256') return concat('sha256=', $digest, '; hexCharacters=', string-length(string($digest)), '; hexBinary=', $digest instance of xs:hexBinary) ``` Exact output: ```text sha256=612D86BAC9C1A9654CA5BFF669CB9B2C4CF8F5C077FB024FF443589AD02D5BF4; hexCharacters=64; hexBinary=true ``` ### Complete fixture inventory Each file embeds its full input and exact result or diagnostic marker. | Runnable case | Exact result or diagnostic marker | |---|---| | [main](../examples/payload-fingerprints/main.xpath) | `sha256=612D86BAC9C1A9654CA5BFF669CB9B2C4CF8F5C077FB024FF443589AD02D5BF4; hexCharacters=64; hexBinary=true` | | [binary-equivalent](../examples/payload-fingerprints/binary-equivalent.xpath) | `true` | | [changed-payload](../examples/payload-fingerprints/changed-payload.xpath) | `true` | | [whitespace-matters](../examples/payload-fingerprints/whitespace-matters.xpath) | `true` | | [normalized-algorithm](../examples/payload-fingerprints/normalized-algorithm.xpath) | `true` | | [empty-string](../examples/payload-fingerprints/empty-string.xpath) | `E3B0C44298FC1C149AFBF4C8996FB92427AE41E4649B934CA495991B7852B855` | | [empty-sequence](../examples/payload-fingerprints/empty-sequence.xpath) | `0` | | [default-md5](../examples/payload-fingerprints/default-md5.xpath) | `900150983CD24FB0D6963F7D28E17F72` | | [unsupported](../examples/payload-fingerprints/unsupported.xpath) | `FOHA0001` | | [nonstring](../examples/payload-fingerprints/nonstring.xpath) | `XPTY0004` | ### Host-side comparison for a XPath 3.1 consumer ```python import hashlib print(hashlib.sha256(b"INV-2048|EUR|125.00").hexdigest().upper()) ``` Exact output: ```text 612D86BAC9C1A9654CA5BFF669CB9B2C4CF8F5C077FB024FF443589AD02D5BF4 ``` This independent comparison verifies the fingerprint bytes. It does not add a standard hashing function to XPath 3.1 or reproduce the Bosak result-type check. ## 14. Performance Digest calculation processes supplied text/octets; it does not acquire a resource. Strings require UTF-8 encoding and digest state. No benchmark or streaming acquisition claim is implied. ## 15. Known Uses Synthetic payload workflow. Named evidence: [`Hash_SpecVectors`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`Hash_AlgorithmIsNormalized`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`Hash_BinaryInputs_HashOctets`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`Hash_EmptySequence_ReturnsEmpty`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`Hash_UnsupportedAlgorithm_RaisesFoha0001`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs). The [runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs) has no exact fn-hash GatedSets assignment. These ten fixtures and the independent hashlib comparison provide separate evidence. No promotion is included. ## 16. Related Features [Invoice API URIs](invoice-api-uris.md) distinguishes semantic values from original wire spelling. [Numeric import diagnostics](numeric-import-diagnostics.md) reports rejected input data. [The audit](../COMPLETENESS-AUDIT.md) retains algorithm/options coverage limits.

functions/product-dependency-closure.md.text:
Product Dependency Closure

Frozen 4.0 — reachable components, shared dependencies and cycles

**C10 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-2.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited verified frozen contract**. Only XML nodes in one document are covered; no JNode/cross-document ordering, topological installation order or quantity explosion. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Product dependency closure — Frozen 4.0.** [fn:transitive-closure](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-transitive-closure). Initial engine delivery: [PR #88](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/88), [revision 0a928bb8](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/0a928bb81b81d0631cc681f86bba83259c0ed790), REQ-118 4.0-S5. Definitions reviewed **2026-10-11** against immutable [QT4CG function source a014e1b4](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This review pin does not recover the unavailable historical adopted specification snapshot. ## 2. Intent Find every component reachable from a product kit through its component references. Return each component node once, including shared dependencies reached through multiple paths, and terminate even when references form a cycle. ## 3. Also Known As Reachability and dependency closure are descriptive terms. No alias is registered. This is a set of reachable nodes, not a build-order or shortest-path algorithm. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 can accumulate node unions through a bounded `fold-left`. The complete comparison below uses at most the number of catalog parts as expansion rounds, which suffices for this finite, stable-node graph. Unlike transitive-closure it still visits the fixed range after reaching a stable set. A recursive helper in a host language supporting function declarations is another earlier idiom. ## 5. Motivation A kit's frame and motor may both require the same bolt. A component report should list that bolt once, including indirect requirements. Naively following references without tracking node identity can duplicate shared parts or loop on a cycle. This report makes the required component set explicit for review. ## 6. Language Alignment The signature takes a `node()?` start and a step callback returning `node()*`. It finds nodes reachable in **one or more steps**, removes duplicates by node identity, and delivers the result in document order. Empty start returns empty. The start is absent unless a step path reaches it again; cycles can therefore put the start in the result. Use node union to include it unconditionally. Non-node input, multiple start nodes or non-node step results raise XPTY0004. The pinned evolving specification also discusses JNodes. This entry verifies XML nodes in one document and does not assert JSON-node or cross-document ordering support. Node identity differs from equality of `@id` strings. ## 7. Applicability Use for reachability in a finite graph of existing nodes. The fixture assumes unique, nonempty part IDs and resolved references. References point into the same catalog document; the callback returns those existing nodes, never freshly parsed copies. A callback that continually constructs new node identities need not terminate. The function does not validate missing references or detect a cycle as a business error. The missing-reference examples show a separate check. ## 8. Structure The start selects KIT. The step resolves each `needs/@ref` against catalog `part/@id`. KIT reaches FRAME and MOTOR; both reach BOLT. The closure contains BOLT, FRAME and MOTOR in catalog document order, regardless of traversal order. ## 9. Participants The catalog defines stable part nodes. Reference elements define directed edges. The resolver callback returns adjacent nodes. The closure performs reachability. sections.2:
Find every component reachable from a product kit through its component references.
Return each component node once, including shared dependencies reached through
multiple paths, and terminate even when references form a cycle.
sections.3:
Reachability and dependency closure are descriptive terms. No alias is registered.
This is a set of reachable nodes, not a build-order or shortest-path algorithm.
sections.4:
XPath 3.1 can accumulate node unions through a bounded `fold-left`. The complete
comparison below uses at most the number of catalog parts as expansion rounds,
which suffices for this finite, stable-node graph. Unlike transitive-closure it
still visits the fixed range after reaching a stable set. A recursive helper
in a host language supporting function declarations is another earlier idiom.
sections.5:
A kit's frame and motor may both require the same bolt. A component report should
list that bolt once, including indirect requirements. Naively following references
without tracking node identity can duplicate shared parts or loop on a cycle.
This report makes the required component set explicit for review.
sections.6:
The signature takes a `node()?` start and a step callback returning `node()*`.
It finds nodes reachable in **one or more steps**, removes duplicates by node
identity, and delivers the result in document order. Empty start returns empty.
The start is absent unless a step path reaches it again; cycles can therefore
put the start in the result. Use node union to include it unconditionally.
Non-node input, multiple start nodes or non-node step results raise XPTY0004.

The pinned evolving specification also discusses JNodes. This entry verifies
XML nodes in one document and does not assert JSON-node or cross-document
ordering support. Node identity differs from equality of `@id` strings.
sections.7:

unique, nonempty part IDs and resolved references. References point into the
same catalog document; the callback returns those existing nodes, never freshly
parsed copies. A callback that continually constructs new node identities need
not terminate. The function does not validate missing references or detect a
cycle as a business error. The missing-reference examples show a separate check.

functions/product-map-index.md.text:
Product indexing with maps

Frozen 4.0 — verified reference contracts

**C10 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-2.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Blocked strict filter-predicate contract**. map:filter currently accepts nonboolean truthy predicate results; do not use them. Map enumeration is not portable business order. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Product indexing with maps — Frozen 4.0.** Shipped in [Bosak PR #84](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/84) at immutable revision [`f7f55b4e`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/f7f55b4e3a6e92da26ac607e34f46aede695cb19). Functions: [map:build](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-map-build), [map:entries](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-map-entries), [map:filter](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-map-filter), [map:items](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-map-items). Definitions reviewed 2026-10-11 against immutable [QT4CG function source `a014e1b4`](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This is a review pin, not evidence of the historical adopted snapshot, which remains unavailable. ## 2. Intent Turn a supplier stock snapshot into a SKU index, apply an explicit duplicate policy, and retain available products. The input deliberately contains a later correction for FILTER-A. ## 3. Also Known As Exact spellings are `map:build`, `map:entries`, `map:filter` and `map:items`. No aliases are introduced. `map:entries` is a function; map-entry iteration syntax is a separate feature. ## 4. History / Supersedes The XPath 3.1 comparison uses `map:merge` over single-entry maps and explicitly requests `use-last`. It sorts keys for presentation because a portable 3.1 map does not promise entry order. This agrees on the one surviving SKU, not on every 4.0 ordering contract. ## 5. Motivation A duplicate SKU can mean a corrected snapshot, an additive delivery, or invalid input. Those meanings require different policies. The main case chooses the last snapshot value (8), while the combiner probe totals two deliveries (20). Neither policy is a substitute for business validation. ## 6. Language Alignment Do not assume JavaScript Map overwrite semantics or SQL grouping: `map:build` defaults to sequence concatenation (`combine`), not use-last. Keys use XPath same-key rules. A key callback may return several keys or no keys. Callbacks receive the item and one-based input position; `map:filter` receives key, value and one-based entry position. Lower-arity callbacks can ignore surplus arguments. ## 7. Applicability Use for deterministic indexing of already parsed records. Reject duplicates when identities must be unique. Do not use a sum combiner for a snapshot feed, or silently drop missing SKU keys when the application must report them. These fixtures simplify the vocabulary and do not implement supplier-feed validation. ## 8. Structure ```xquery map:build($rows, $key, $value, $options) map:filter($index, function($key,$value,$position){...}) map:entries($index) map:items($index) ``` Positional and shorter callback forms are exercised by the exact files below. This entry covers the illustrated contracts rather than every arity or option. ## 9. Participants Existing `FunctionLibrary` frozen registrations select these names only at `XPathCompatibility.XPath40` or higher. The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) compiles each file at its declared mode and checks default XPath31 refusal for successful 4.0 forms. ## 10. Collaborations Maps can be supplied as stylesheet parameters; see the [order-routing chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md). Preserve source rows separately if discarded corrections or zero-stock items must appear in an exception report. ## 11. Consequences **Published 1.1.2 correction:** `map:entries` now returns a sequence of single-entry maps in entry order. Empty input returns the empty sequence; a multi-item value remains whole inside its single-entry map. `map:items` concatenates the item sequences associated with entries, omitting empty values and retaining nested maps/arrays as items rather than recursively flattening them. The `entries-boundary` result is `false/2`; `items-sequence-boundary` is `3`, matching the portable comparisons. No `?*` adapter is needed for `map:entries`. **Migration from published 1.1.1:** that version returned an array from `map:entries` and retained grouped sequence values from `map:items`. Replace `map:entries($map)?*` with `map:entries($map)`, and array indexing of the entry result with sequence predicates such as `[2]`. Item counts now reflect the concatenated values. Review code that relied on the old grouped cardinality; portable `map:for-each` alternatives remain valid. This is a correction of the supported 4.0 draft contracts; default XPath31 still rejects these new names. Version 1.1.2 is published with the corrected contracts. See the [correction dossier](../../REQ-118-MAP-RESULT-SHAPES.md). `use-any` leaves the choice implementation-defined; Bosak currently retains the first value. It is unsuitable when the business requires a specific correction to win. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Duplicate combine/use-first/use-last/reject and custom combining policies; Single-entry-map sequence and concatenated item result shapes; Entry-position callbacks, empty values, nesting and node identity. **Boundaries:** map:filter currently accepts nonboolean truthy predicate results; do not use them. Map enumeration is not portable business order. Follow-up groups: F01, F07, F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Implementation: [FunctionLibrary.cs](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs); [named unit tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs); [manifest](../examples/cases.json). Names refuse XPST0017 in default XPath31; the comparisons remain valid at XPath31. The original reference delivery changed no engine code. The later result-shape correction targets source 1.1.2; see the linked correction dossier for its regressions and gates. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** [Container review](../CONTAINER-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md), pinned to F&O e7ee4ab8, and [detailed stock-feed README](../examples/container-contracts/README.md) supply 89 checks covering six families: keyword modes, empty/default/member/item shapes, nested values, node identity, callback arity/results and complete XPath 3.1/4.0 reports. Keywords remain unavailable. map:filter boolean-result enforcement remains an engine follow-up. Source/public version is 1.1.3; original delivery/unit/gate evidence and historical adopted-pin limits are unchanged. The map result-shape corrections already shipped in 1.1.2. **Existing-function review:** The [complete baseline-name inventory](../CHANGED-31-CONTRACT-INVENTORY.md) records unavailable three-argument map/array getters and empty sort-key/map:merge-option boundaries. The [stock examples](../examples/changed31-contracts/README.md) show explicit portable fallback policy. This review does not implement draft defaults or close D2. **Existing-function default review (2026-10-12):** The [ordering/default review](../ORDER-DEFAULT-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md) and [detailed supplier README](../examples/order-contracts/README.md) add 132 checks across sort/array:sort/min/max/map:merge, explicit key/options and collation/NaN/cardinality boundaries, and six full 3.1/4.0 reports. Supplier price-plus-ID keys preserve business tie-breaking under source reordering. Use simple mapping to project sorted node IDs; a path restores document order. This is targeted evidence, not an engine fix or full D2 completion. ## 13. Sample Code Input is declared inside each expression: reduced order/product records, no document focus, external variables or resource access. Namespace prefixes `map` and `array` use the standard public API bindings. This is a review pin, not evidence of the historical adopted snapshot, which remains unavailable.
sections.2: Turn a supplier stock snapshot into a SKU index, apply an explicit duplicate policy, and retain available products. The input deliberately contains a later correction for FILTER-A.
sections.3: Exact spellings are `map:build`, `map:entries`, `map:filter` and `map:items`. No aliases are introduced. `map:entries` is a function; map-entry iteration syntax is a separate feature.
sections.4: The XPath 3.1 comparison uses `map:merge` over single-entry maps and explicitly requests `use-last`. It sorts keys for presentation because a portable 3.1 map does not promise entry order. This agrees on the one surviving SKU, not on every 4.0 ordering contract.
sections.5: A duplicate SKU can mean a corrected snapshot, an additive delivery, or invalid input. Those meanings require different policies. The main case chooses the last snapshot value (8), while the combiner probe totals two deliveries (20). Neither policy is a substitute for business validation.
sections.6: Do not assume JavaScript Map overwrite semantics or SQL grouping: `map:build` defaults to sequence concatenation (`combine`), not use-last. Keys use XPath same-key rules. A key callback may return several keys or no keys. Callbacks receive the item and one-based input position; `map:filter` receives key, value and one-based entry position. Lower-arity callbacks can ignore surplus arguments.
sections.7: Use for deterministic indexing of already parsed records. Reject duplicates when identities must be unique. Do not use a sum combiner for a snapshot feed, or silently drop missing SKU keys when the application must report them. These fixtures simplify the vocabulary and do not implement supplier-feed validation.
sections.8:
```xquery
map:build($rows, $key, $value, $options)
map:filter($index, function($key,$value,$position){...})
map:entries($index)
map:items($index)
```

sections.11:
**Published 1.1.2 correction:** `map:entries` now returns a sequence of
single-entry maps in entry order. Empty input returns the empty sequence; a
multi-item value remains whole inside its single-entry map. `map:items`
concatenates the item sequences associated with entries, omitting empty values
and retaining nested maps/arrays as items rather than recursively flattening them.
The `entries-boundary` result is `false/2`; `items-sequence-boundary` is `3`,
matching the portable comparisons. No `?*` adapter is needed for `map:entries`.

**Migration from published 1.1.1:** that version returned an array from
`map:entries` and retained grouped sequence values from `map:items`. Replace
`map:entries($map)?*` with `map:entries($map)`, and array indexing of the entry
result with sequence predicates such as `[2]`. Item counts now reflect the
concatenated values. Review code that relied on the old grouped cardinality;
portable `map:for-each` alternatives remain valid. This is a correction of the
supported 4.0 draft contracts; default XPath31 still rejects these new names.
Version 1.1.2 is published with the corrected contracts. See the
[correction dossier](../../REQ-118-MAP-RESULT-SHAPES.md).

`use-any` leaves the choice implementation-defined; Bosak currently retains the first value. It is unsuitable when the business requires a specific correction to win.

functions/sequence-distinctness.md.text:
Sequence identity checks

Frozen 4.0

**C10 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-2.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited verified frozen contract**. Maps do not satisfy the declared atomic input contract despite current tolerance; no implicit case folding or normalization. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. **Related current review:** [Equality/collation contracts](../EQUALITY-COLLATION-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md) refresh the five-family declarations, complete customer example, keyword boundaries and explicitly separate engine findings without replacing the historical evidence below. ## 1. Name and Classification **Sequence identity checks — Frozen 4.0.** [Bosak PR #83](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/83) / [immutable revision `532d04f4`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/532d04f4672df430d93752e3158fc3cdfd4c7c39). This is the shipped engine delivery. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [fn:all-different](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-all-different), [fn:duplicate-values](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-duplicate-values). Historical adopted specification source revision was not retained; this remains an explicit provenance gap. ## 2. Intent Refuse ambiguous order identities and identify duplicates for repair. ## 3. Also Known As Use the exact spellings in the linked examples; no undocumented aliases are adopted. ## 4. History / Supersedes For this string-ID contract, XPath 3.1 can compare `count(distinct-values($ids))` with `count($ids)`, as the published baseline demonstrates. That detects existence of duplicates but does not return their second-appearance order. Broader atomic inputs need a separately reviewed equality policy. all-different reports whether atomic values are pairwise distinct. duplicate-values reports each duplicated value once, in second-appearance order. Equality follows the function collation and atomic comparison rules; this chapter restricts identity to strings and the default codepoint collation. Both empty and singleton inputs are all-different. Blankness is a separate business rule. ## 5. Motivation Refuse ambiguous order identities and identify duplicates for repair. The order-routing chapter places validation before dispatch so rejected records stay available for repair. ## 6. Language Alignment Duplicate detection is not document identity, structural map equality or automatic Unicode normalization. Do not trim or case-fold identifiers implicitly; choose that policy before checking uniqueness. ## 7. Applicability Use when the consumer opts into XPath40 and needs the exact validation or ordering contract described here. Keep the XPath 3.1 baseline when that opt-in is unavailable. ## 8. Structure ```xquery string(all-different(('R1','R2','R1'))) || '/' || string-join(duplicate-values(('R1','R2','R1','R2')), ',') ``` This complete expression demonstrates the stated contract, not the full grammar. ## 9. Participants The public XPath API compiles at the manifest mode and evaluates without application variables. The routing chapter additionally supplies an XML document context. ## 10. Collaborations The routing planner passes an XDM map to portable XSLT through a required parameter. See [the full chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md). ## 11. Consequences all-different reports whether atomic values are pairwise distinct. duplicate-values reports each duplicated value once, in second-appearance order. Equality follows the function collation and atomic comparison rules; this chapter restricts identity to strings and the default codepoint collation. Both empty and singleton inputs are all-different. Blankness is a separate business rule. Duplicate detection is not document identity, structural map equality or automatic Unicode normalization. Do not trim or case-fold identifiers implicitly; choose that policy before checking uniqueness. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Atomic duplicate classes, second-occurrence representatives and order; Empty/singleton input, NaN grouping and explicit collations; Typed/atomized source and unknown-collation boundaries. **Boundaries:** Maps do not satisfy the declared atomic input contract despite current tolerance; no implicit case folding or normalization. Follow-up groups: F01, F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) runs the exact files, asserts declared results/errors, and checks default-3.1 refusal for successful 4.0 forms. No engine code changes or conformance promotions are included. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** [Five-family predicate review](../PREDICATE-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md), pinned to F&O e7ee4ab8, and [detailed shipment acceptance README](../examples/predicate-contracts/README.md) add 102 exact checks. They cover explicit keyword modes, collation/defaults, numeric/NaN/node/map boundaries, callback direction/result conversion and eight complete 3.1/4.0 reports. All five keyword families remain unavailable. Equality functions tolerate the tested singleton map despite atomic signatures; numeric and empty-string collation processing remain explicit engine follow-ups. The string-valued workflow uses supported positional forms. Initial delivery/unit/gate evidence and historical adopted-pin limits are unchanged. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** [Comparison/selection review](../SELECTION-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md), pinned to F&O e7ee4ab8, and [detailed warehouse README](../examples/selection-contracts/README.md) supply 68 checks: keyword modes, collation/default/key/predicate, atomization, result/cardinality boundaries and complete 3.1/4.0 reports. duplicate-values/highest/lowest keywords remain unavailable; index-where keywords work. Map tolerance and tested extrema NaN results remain explicit engine follow-ups. Extrema return boundary-equal items, not all distinct records sharing its key. Initial delivery/unit/gate and historical adopted-pin limits are unchanged. ## 13. Sample Code [main.xpath](../examples/sequence-distinctness/main.xpath): returns `false/R1,R2` at mode 40. [edge.xpath](../examples/sequence-distinctness/edge.xpath): returns `true/0` at mode 40. [before.xpath](../examples/sequence-distinctness/before.xpath): returns `false` at mode 31. ## 14. Performance Notes Duplicate checks and index selection may traverse the input; some/every may finish early. Partitioning creates arrays and retains input items. These are qualitative expectations, not benchmark results. Stateful or expensive callbacks change workload costs. ## 15. Known Uses Executable IDs: `sequence-distinctness-main`, `sequence-distinctness-edge`, `sequence-distinctness-before`. [`AllDifferent_SpecSemantics`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`DuplicateValues_ResultInSecondAppearanceOrder`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs), [`DuplicateValues_NoDuplicates_ReturnsEmpty`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs) Neither exact-name set is currently listed in GatedSets; named unit tests and published examples are the evidence here. [Gate runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs). ## 16. functions/shipment-event-sequences.md.text:
Shipment-event Sequence Checks

Frozen 4.0 — identities, adjacent processing steps and event boundaries

**C10 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-2.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited verified frozen contract**. Use explicit presence/count guards for missing IDs; no complete carrier-state machine or unverified coercion contract. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. **C07 lifecycle review — 26 October 2026:** [Current disposition and correction receipts](../LIFECYCLE-RECONCILIATION.md) distinguish delivered scope, retained history and pending acceptance. Six closure workpackages remain; no feature or profile promotion. **Related current review:** [Equality/collation contracts](../EQUALITY-COLLATION-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md) refresh the five-family declarations, complete customer example, keyword boundaries and explicitly separate engine findings without replacing the historical evidence below. ## 1. Name and Classification **Shipment-event sequence checks — Frozen 4.0.** Functions: [fn:all-equal](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-all-equal), [fn:contains-subsequence](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-contains-subsequence), [fn:starts-with-subsequence](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-starts-with-subsequence), [fn:ends-with-subsequence](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-ends-with-subsequence). Initial engine delivery: [Bosak PR #83](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/83), immutable revision [`532d04f4`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/532d04f4672df430d93752e3158fc3cdfd4c7c39), REQ-118 4.0-S1 part 2. Definitions reviewed **2026-10-11** against immutable [QT4CG function source `a014e1b4`](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/a014e1b408baf5614a11401d3570a04498ab76be/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This review pin does not recover the unavailable historical adopted specification snapshot. Reference example delivery: [`b75c0d26`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/b75c0d26), [PR #162](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/162). ## 2. Intent Check that a shipment history belongs to one shipment, starts with the required opening events, contains an adjacent dispatch pair, and ends in delivery. The report keeps each decision visible so a failed history can be investigated. ## 3. Also Known As `fn:all-equal` was originally proposed as `fn:uniform`, according to the pinned function source. Bosak exposes the adopted `all-equal` spelling; this entry introduces no former-name alias. The three subsequence functions use the exact spellings listed above. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 expresses all-equal as `count(distinct-values($values)) le 1`, a prefix/suffix check as `deep-equal` over the appropriate `subsequence`, and a contiguous segment search as `some $i ... satisfies deep-equal(...)`. The complete comparison below implements those operations for this string-valued history. It agrees on the illustrated report; a customized comparator requires an explicit equivalent comparison in the earlier idiom. ## 5. Motivation An unordered membership check can find PACKED and DISPATCHED while accepting the wrong order or an intervening event. An equal-identity check alone accepts an empty sequence and cannot reveal a missing attribute omitted by path selection. Combining presence/count guards with sequence checks makes those business conditions explicit. ## 6. Language Alignment Matching uses adjacent sequence positions, preserving order and repeated events. The mathematical term subsequence can allow gaps; these functions require a contiguous segment, prefix or suffix. Default item comparison is `deep-equal`, so maps are compared by content, including unrelated fields. The custom record comparator intentionally projects only the state code. Comparators receive `(input-item, required-item)` and must have arity two. Their direction is observable when the callback is asymmetric. A boolean or empty sequence is returned: empty means false, while the string `'yes'` fails XPTY0004 rather than being treated as a truthy JavaScript value. `all-equal` follows atomized `distinct-values` semantics, including collation, numeric comparison and NaN grouping, rather than comparing every item to the first with general `=`. ## 7. Applicability Use for adjacent event rules over a history whose order and identity contract are established. The sample assumes a nonempty header identity, supplies no timestamps and does not implement a full carrier state machine. Repeated events, retries and every allowed transition require additional business rules. A completed report flag does not itself trigger dispatch or publish output. ## 8. Structure ```xquery all-equal($ids) all-equal($ids, $collation) contains-subsequence($events, $required) starts-with-subsequence($events, $required, $compare) ends-with-subsequence($events, $required, $compare) ``` All three subsequence functions accept two-argument default-comparison and three-argument comparator forms. An empty comparator argument chooses the default. The exact record-comparator case exercises all three supplied-callback forms; callback-result and signature errors are verified separately. ## 9. Participants The existing FunctionLibrary registrations mark all four names frozen XPath40-only. [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) compiles complete files at their manifest modes, asserts text/errors, and verifies default-XPath31 refusal of successful 4.0 forms. The main expressions parse their own complete XML input and need no external context. ## 10. Collaborations Use with [sequence selection](order-sequence-selection.md) when an operator needs a window of a history, and [sequence identity checks](sequence-distinctness.md) when duplicate event identities need separate investigation. The [order-reconciliation chapter](../worked-examples/order-reconciliation/README.md) demonstrates the related distinction between document processing and business acceptance. These examples add no new worked chapter. ## 11. Consequences Empty required sequences match any input, including empty input. A nonempty requirement longer than the input fails. `all-equal` is true for empty and singleton values; the report separately requires events and one identity per event. Path selection of missing identities/codes drops values, so count guards are deliberate. The empty-history example also explains vacuous `known=true`. Callback selection can change business meaning: the record example ignores timestamps and normalizes code casing while the default compares full maps. The supplied ASCII case-insensitive collation treats SHIP-42 and ship-42 as equal; the default codepoint comparison keeps them distinct. Use that collation only when the identifier contract permits it. NaN grouping is an equality contract, not evidence that invalid measurement values are acceptable. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Contiguous segment/prefix/suffix matching with order and duplicates; Deep-equal default, asymmetric custom comparators and argument order; Empty requirements, boolean/empty callback conversion and atomic all-equal. **Boundaries:** Use explicit presence/count guards for missing IDs; no complete carrier-state machine or unverified coercion contract. Follow-up groups: F01, F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Source: [FunctionLibrary.cs](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs), `ContainsSubsequence`, `StartsWithSubsequence`, `EndsWithSubsequence` and `AllEqual`; named assertions are in [XPath40FunctionTests.cs](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs). Direct names refuse XPST0017 at default XPath31. Source/public package version remains 1.1.2. This entry changes documentation and exact fixtures only, with no engine code, API or gate membership changes. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** [Five-family predicate review](../PREDICATE-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md), pinned to F&O e7ee4ab8, and [detailed shipment acceptance README](../examples/predicate-contracts/README.md) add 102 exact checks. They cover explicit keyword modes, collation/defaults, numeric/NaN/node/map boundaries, callback direction/result conversion and eight complete 3.1/4.0 reports. All five keyword families remain unavailable. Equality functions tolerate the tested singleton map despite atomic signatures; numeric and empty-string collation processing remain explicit engine follow-ups. The string-valued workflow uses supported positional forms. Initial delivery/unit/gate evidence and historical adopted-pin limits are unchanged. ## 13. Sample Code The synthetic carrier vocabulary below has one shipment header and ordered event records. Each event supplies its shipment identity and state code. The fixtures use document order as event order; production feeds must establish that ordering before applying the checks. No timestamps, carrier standard, resource access or application variables are assumed. **Normal input:** ```xml ``` | Report field | Business check | |---|---| | `shipment`, `events` | Header identity and observed event count. | | `consistent` | There is at least one event, every event has an identity, and all identities agree with the header. | | `known` | Every event has a code and each code belongs to the declared vocabulary. | | `start` | The first two events are CREATED then PICKED. | | `dispatch` | PACKED immediately precedes DISPATCHED somewhere in the history. | | `end` | DELIVERED is the final event. | | `ready` | All five checks hold. This report flag is the demo's acceptance decision. | **Complete XPath40 report — mode 40:** [main.xpath](../examples/shipment-event-sequences/main.xpath) ```xquery (: Synthetic carrier history; document order is the agreed event order. :) let $history := parse-xml('')/history, $events := $history/event, $codes := $events/@code ! string(.), $ids := $events/@shipment ! string(.), $consistent := exists($events) and count($ids) eq count($events) and (all-equal($ids)) and $ids[1] eq string($history/@shipment), $known := count($codes) eq count($events) and (every $code in $codes satisfies $code = ('CREATED','PICKED','PACKED','DISPATCHED','IN_TRANSIT','DELIVERED')), $start := starts-with-subsequence($codes,('CREATED','PICKED')), $dispatch := contains-subsequence($codes,('PACKED','DISPATCHED')), $end := ends-with-subsequence($codes,('DELIVERED')) return concat('shipment=', $history/@shipment, ';events=', count($events), ';consistent=', $consistent, ';known=', $known, ';start=', $start, ';dispatch=', $dispatch, ';end=', $end, ';ready=', $consistent and $known and $start and $dispatch and $end) ``` Exact output: ```text shipment=SHIP-42;events=6;consistent=true;known=true;start=true;dispatch=true;end=true;ready=true ``` **XPath31 comparison — mode 31:** [baseline.xpath](../examples/shipment-event-sequences/baseline.xpath) ```xquery (: Synthetic carrier history; document order is the agreed event order. :) let $history := parse-xml('')/history, $events := $history/event, $codes := $events/@code ! string(.), $ids := $events/@shipment ! string(.), $consistent := exists($events) and count($ids) eq count($events) and (count(distinct-values($ids)) le 1) and $ids[1] eq string($history/@shipment), $known := count($codes) eq count($events) and (every $code in $codes satisfies $code = ('CREATED','PICKED','PACKED','DISPATCHED','IN_TRANSIT','DELIVERED')), $start := deep-equal(subsequence($codes,1,2),('CREATED','PICKED')), $dispatch := some $i in 1 to (count($codes)-1) satisfies deep-equal(subsequence($codes,$i,2),('PACKED','DISPATCHED')), $end := deep-equal(subsequence($codes,count($codes),1),('DELIVERED')) return concat('shipment=', $history/@shipment, ';events=', count($events), ';consistent=', $consistent, ';known=', $known, ';start=', $start, ';dispatch=', $dispatch, ';end=', $end, ';ready=', $consistent and $known and $start and $dispatch and $end) ``` Exact output: ```text shipment=SHIP-42;events=6;consistent=true;known=true;start=true;dispatch=true;end=true;ready=true ``` **Empty-history edge — mode 40:** [edge.xpath](../examples/shipment-event-sequences/edge.xpath) ```xquery (: Synthetic carrier history; document order is the agreed event order. :) let $history := parse-xml('')/history, $events := $history/event, $codes := $events/@code ! string(.), $ids := $events/@shipment ! string(.), $consistent := exists($events) and count($ids) eq count($events) and (all-equal($ids)) and $ids[1] eq string($history/@shipment), $known := count($codes) eq count($events) and (every $code in $codes satisfies $code = ('CREATED','PICKED','PACKED','DISPATCHED','IN_TRANSIT','DELIVERED')), $start := starts-with-subsequence($codes,('CREATED','PICKED')), $dispatch := contains-subsequence($codes,('PACKED','DISPATCHED')), $end := ends-with-subsequence($codes,('DELIVERED')) return concat('shipment=', $history/@shipment, ';events=', count($events), ';consistent=', $consistent, ';known=', $known, ';start=', $start, ';dispatch=', $dispatch, ';end=', $end, ';ready=', $consistent and $known and $start and $dispatch and $end) ``` Exact output: ```text shipment=SHIP-42;events=0;consistent=false;known=true;start=false;dispatch=false;end=false;ready=false ``` The edge input is ``. Its `known=true` reflects the vacuous universal check over no codes; `consistent=false` and the required nonempty prefix/segment/suffix checks keep `ready=false`. **Unexpected event input:** ```xml ``` The complete [unexpected-event expression](../examples/shipment-event-sequences/unexpected-event.xpath) uses the same report logic. CUSTOMS is outside this reduced vocabulary and breaks the required adjacent dispatch pair. Its exact output is: ```text shipment=SHIP-42;events=6;consistent=true;known=false;start=true;dispatch=false;end=true;ready=false ``` **Additional executable contracts:** | Case | Mode | Exact text or error | |---|---|---| | [unexpected-event](../examples/shipment-event-sequences/unexpected-event.xpath) | 40 | `shipment=SHIP-42;events=6;consistent=false;known=true;start=true;dispatch=true;end=true;ready=false` | | [missing-shipment](../examples/shipment-event-sequences/missing-shipment.xpath) | 40 | `shipment=SHIP-42;events=6;consistent=false;known=true;start=true;dispatch=true;end=true;ready=false` | | [missing-event-code](../examples/shipment-event-sequences/missing-event-code.xpath) | 40 | `shipment=SHIP-42;events=6;consistent=true;known=false;start=true;dispatch=false;end=true;ready=false` | | [wrong-start](../examples/shipment-event-sequences/wrong-start.xpath) | 40 | `true/true/true/true` | | [noncontiguous](../examples/shipment-event-sequences/noncontiguous.xpath) | 40 | `false` | | `false/false/false` | | [repeated-events](../examples/shipment-event-sequences/repeated-events.xpath) | 40 | `true` | | Performance Notes The shipped segment search materializes both sequences and tries candidate start positions, making up to input-length times requirement-length item comparisons. Prefix/suffix operations materialize input and compare the required positions. Comparator work and recursive deep equality add their own costs; all-equal uses the distinct-values implementation and retains distinct results. The fixtures establish no streaming or benchmark timing claims. ## 15. Named units and the 27 exact manifest cases remain separate evidence; family assignment does not certify every signature. No gate promotion or new conformance run is claimed for this documentation delivery. ## 16. sections.13:
The synthetic carrier vocabulary below has one shipment header and ordered
event records. Each event supplies its shipment identity and state code. The
fixtures use document order as event order; production feeds must establish that
ordering before applying the checks. No timestamps, carrier standard, resource
access or application variables are assumed.

**Normal input:**

```xml
<history shipment="SHIP-42">
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="CREATED"/>
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="PICKED"/>
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="PACKED"/>
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="DISPATCHED"/>
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="IN_TRANSIT"/>
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="DELIVERED"/>
</history>
```

| Report field | Business check |
|---|---|
| `shipment`, `events` | Header identity and observed event count. |
| `consistent` | There is at least one event, every event has an identity, and all identities agree with the header. |
| `known` | Every event has a code and each code belongs to the declared vocabulary. |
| `start` | The first two events are CREATED then PICKED. |
| `dispatch` | PACKED immediately precedes DISPATCHED somewhere in the history. |
| `end` | DELIVERED is the final event. |
| `ready` | All five checks hold. This report flag is the demo's acceptance decision. |

**Complete XPath40 report — mode 40:** [main.xpath](../examples/shipment-event-sequences/main.xpath)

```xquery
(: Synthetic carrier history; document order is the agreed event order. :)
let $history := parse-xml('<history shipment="SHIP-42"><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="CREATED"/><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="PICKED"/><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="PACKED"/><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="DISPATCHED"/><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="IN_TRANSIT"/><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="DELIVERED"/></history>')/history,
    $events := $history/event,
    $codes := $events/@code ! string(.),
    $ids := $events/@shipment ! string(.),
    $consistent := exists($events) and count($ids) eq count($events)
                   and (all-equal($ids)) and $ids[1] eq string($history/@shipment),
    $known := count($codes) eq count($events) and
              (every $code in $codes satisfies $code = ('CREATED','PICKED','PACKED','DISPATCHED','IN_TRANSIT','DELIVERED')),
    $start := starts-with-subsequence($codes,('CREATED','PICKED')),
    $dispatch := contains-subsequence($codes,('PACKED','DISPATCHED')),
    $end := ends-with-subsequence($codes,('DELIVERED'))
return concat('shipment=', $history/@shipment, ';events=', count($events),
              ';consistent=', $consistent, ';known=', $known, ';start=', $start,
              ';dispatch=', $dispatch, ';end=', $end,
              ';ready=', $consistent and $known and $start and $dispatch and $end)
```

Exact output:

```text
shipment=SHIP-42;events=6;consistent=true;known=true;start=true;dispatch=true;end=true;ready=true
```

**XPath31 comparison — mode 31:** [baseline.xpath](../examples/shipment-event-sequences/baseline.xpath)

```xquery
(: Synthetic carrier history; document order is the agreed event order. :)
let $history := parse-xml('<history shipment="SHIP-42"><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="CREATED"/><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="PICKED"/><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="PACKED"/><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="DISPATCHED"/><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="IN_TRANSIT"/><event shipment="SHIP-42" code="DELIVERED"/></history>')/history,
    $events := $history/event,
    $codes := $events/@code ! string(.),
    $ids := $events/@shipment ! string(.),
    $consistent := exists($events) and count($ids) eq count($events)
                   and (count(distinct-values($ids)) le 1) and $ids[1] eq string($history/@shipment),
    $known := count($codes) eq count($events) and
              (every $code in $codes satisfies $code = ('CREATED','PICKED','PACKED','DISPATCHED','IN_TRANSIT','DELIVERED')),
    $start := deep-equal(subsequence($codes,1,2),('CREATED','PICKED')),
    $dispatch := some $i in 1 to (count($codes)-1) satisfies deep-equal(subsequence($codes,$i,2),('PACKED','DISPATCHED')),
    $end := deep-equal(subsequence($codes,count($codes),1),('DELIVERED'))
return concat('shipment=', $history/@shipment, ';events=', count($events),
              ';consistent=', $consistent, ';known=', $known, ';start=', $start,
              ';dispatch=', $dispatch, ';end=', $end,
              ';ready=', $consistent and $known and $start and $dispatch and $end)
```

Exact output:

```text
shipment=SHIP-42;events=6;consistent=true;known=true;start=true;dispatch=true;end=true;ready=true
```

**Empty-history edge — mode 40:** [edge.xpath](../examples/shipment-event-sequences/edge.xpath)

```xquery
(: Synthetic carrier history; document order is the agreed event order. :)
let $history := parse-xml('<history shipment="SHIP-42"></history>')/history,
    $events := $history/event,
    $codes := $events/@code ! string(.),
    $ids := $events/@shipment ! string(.),
    $consistent := exists($events) and count($ids) eq count($events)
                   and (all-equal($ids)) and $ids[1] eq string($history/@shipment),
    $known := count($codes) eq count($events) and
              (every $code in $codes satisfies $code = ('CREATED','PICKED','PACKED','DISPATCHED','IN_TRANSIT','DELIVERED')),
    $start := starts-with-subsequence($codes,('CREATED','PICKED')),
    $dispatch := contains-subsequence($codes,('PACKED','DISPATCHED')),
    $end := ends-with-subsequence($codes,('DELIVERED'))
return concat('shipment=', $history/@shipment, ';events=', count($events),
              ';consistent=', $consistent, ';known=', $known, ';start=', $start,
              ';dispatch=', $dispatch, ';end=', $end,
              ';ready=', $consistent and $known and $start and $dispatch and $end)
```

Exact output:

```text
shipment=SHIP-42;events=0;consistent=false;known=true;start=false;dispatch=false;end=false;ready=false
```

The edge input is `<history shipment="SHIP-42"/>`. Its `known=true` reflects
the vacuous universal check over no codes; `consistent=false` and the required
nonempty prefix/segment/suffix checks keep `ready=false`.

**Unexpected event input:**

```xml
<history shipment="SHIP-42">
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="CREATED"/>
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="PICKED"/>
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="PACKED"/>
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="CUSTOMS"/>
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="DISPATCHED"/>
  <event shipment="SHIP-42" code="DELIVERED"/>
</history>
```

The complete [unexpected-event expression](../examples/shipment-event-sequences/unexpected-event.xpath)
uses the same report logic. CUSTOMS is outside this reduced vocabulary and breaks
the required adjacent dispatch pair. Its exact output is:

```text
shipment=SHIP-42;events=6;consistent=true;known=false;start=true;dispatch=false;end=true;ready=false
```

functions/sort-with.md.text:
Comparator-based sorting

Practical reference: Frozen 4.0

**C10 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-2.md) records 2 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited verified frozen contract**. Comparator consistency and arbitrary result/coercion combinations are not certified; avoid NaN/mixed-family business order. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Comparator-based sorting** - **Frozen 4.0**. Delivery family: [REQ-118](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) / [REQ-123 registry](../../FEATURE_REQUESTS.md). Section provenance: See the linked REQ dossiers and implementation evidence. [Primary implementation evidence](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) records the shipped behavior; this entry adds executable user-facing examples under REQ-126, rather than announcing a new engine feature. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [fn:sort-with](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-sort-with), [array:sort-with](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-array-sort-with). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #112](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/112), [immutable mainline revision `89c90b4d`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/89c90b4d5b6a216a4a37223e169d36e3a1a832bd) (2026-10-10). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent A comparator expresses descending priority directly; zero means equal priority. ## 3. Also Known As Use the name and spelling in this entry and its executable files. Related functions or instruction forms are described in the primary test evidence; no additional alias is adopted here. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1, sort by a transformed key such as negative priority, or use xsl:sort. Compare the [complete earlier-version baseline](../examples/sort-with/before.xpath) with the [complete expression](../examples/sort-with/main.xpath). Both yield `5,2,1` for this synthetic input. They demonstrate this task, not universal equivalence of the two mechanisms. ## 5. Motivation A dispatch queue must show highest priority first. A comparator expresses descending priority directly; zero means equal priority. Keeping this task explicit makes it possible to choose the feature for a practical reason and verify what the receiving application will see. ## 6. Language Alignment Read the behavior as XPath/XSLT semantics. Similar vocabulary in another programming language is not a compatibility promise. A comparator must return a consistent ordering. This example sorts numeric priorities and does not define a secondary order for equal records. ## 7. Applicability Use this form when solving the stated task and the consumer permits the declared compatibility level. Keep the earlier baseline when the application requires 3.1 expressions or portable 3.0 stylesheets. A comparator must return a consistent ordering. This example sorts numeric priorities and does not define a secondary order for equal records. ## 8. Structure ```xquery string-join(fn:sort-with((2, 5, 1), function($a, $b) { if ($a gt $b) then -1 else if ($a lt $b) then 1 else 0 }) ! string(.), ',') ``` This is the worked case's syntax, not a replacement for the full language grammar. Required namespaces and surrounding context are supplied in the linked complete files. ## 9. Participants XPath31Expression, CompileOptions, the parser/compiler, and the shared runtime/function library provide the public execution path. [Primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) identify the feature's implementation contract. The examples use public APIs only. ## 10. Collaborations The case combines source values, the named feature, and explicit output formatting. [Worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md) show how selection, construction, and business rejection fit into larger transformations. ## 11. Consequences Benefit: A comparator expresses descending priority directly; zero means equal priority. Tradeoff: the declared compatibility level and edge rules become part of the consumer contract. A comparator must return a consistent ordering. This example sorts numeric priorities and does not define a secondary order for equal records. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Comparator-driven numeric ordering and array member boundaries; Empty input, comparator result/arity and consistency requirements. **Boundaries:** Comparator consistency and arbitrary result/coercion combinations are not certified; avoid NaN/mixed-family business order. Follow-up groups: F06, F08. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Compile the after/edge expressions at XPathCompatibility.XPath40. The baseline uses XPath31. The example harness checks default-mode refusal for successful 4.0 cases; negative cases pin the declared error. See [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs): it executes the published files from the [case manifest](../examples/cases.json). This documentation slice changes no engine source. ## 13. Sample Code Input is synthetic and declared directly in the complete expression. The [complete expression](../examples/sort-with/main.xpath) yields `5,2,1`. The [edge case](../examples/sort-with/edge.xpath) yields `0`. No external resources or application variables are required. See the [example runner](../examples/README.md) for commands and host context. ## 14. Performance Notes Expected class: hot-path relevant sorting. Comparator callbacks may execute many times, so expensive work inside a comparator can dominate. These are implementation expectations, not measured deltas. No benchmark is claimed; use the repository benchmark harness before making workload-specific speed or memory claims. ## 15. Known Uses Executable example IDs: `sort-with-main`, `sort-with-edge`, `sort-with-before` in `CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome`. Existing unit evidence: [primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Chapter-level evidence does not promote a qt4tests set into GatedSets; conformance status remains owned by the harness and delivery records. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Compile_SortWithCluster_DefaultOptions_ThrowXpst0017`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Compile_SortWithCluster_3Point1Functions_StillWork`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_SortWithCluster_FrozenXPath40_Works`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Named promoted sets: `array-sort-with`, `fn-sort-with`. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features See the [catalog index](../README.md), [worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md), and the alternatives in section 4. The case may be used independently of the larger chapters. *Created 2026-10-11: verified practical catalog example and earlier-version baseline.*

functions/supplier-offer-ranking.md.text:
Supplier Offer Ranking

Frozen 4.0 — verified integration contracts and limitations

Equal keys do not imply all distinct records are extrema; NaN/exact mixed-number ordering and unverified record fields remain limits. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification Functions: [fn:highest](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-highest), [fn:lowest](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-lowest), [fn:sort-by](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-sort-by), [fn:collation-available](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-collation-available). Frozen 4.0. Original ranking delivery [PR #83](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/83), [532d04f4](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/532d04f4672df430d93752e3158fc3cdfd4c7c39); collation availability [PR #114](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/114), [33894747](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/33894747f04da970a1f3c0f17fa960fa1f620605). Reviewed 2026-10-12 against immutable [QT4CG function source e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This is a current review pin, not recovery of the unavailable historical adopted snapshot. ## 2. Intent Rank supplier offers by ascending price and descending quality score, report all cheapest offers, and inspect whether a requested string collation is available. ## 3. Also Known As Boundary-item selection, multi-key ranking and collation preflight are descriptive terms; no aliases are registered. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 uses min/max plus explicit filters for boundary-key matches. Stable sorting by the minor score key first, then the major price key, implements this two-key ranking. The comparison omits collation availability: standard 3.1 has no direct availability function. A host must preflight or supply a known supported collation. ## 5. Motivation Two suppliers can quote the same price but have different scores. A procurement report needs both tied cheapest quotes while ranking them by score. Selecting one boundary record alone does not implement that business rule. ## 6. Language Alignment highest/lowest sort by an optional key and return boundary-related input items. Untyped keys are treated numerically unless an explicit string key changes that rule. In Bosak, the final membership comparison is against the whole boundary item (contextual/deep equality), not just its computed key. The observed two-node price-tie case returns B, although B and C share price 8. The report therefore filters all offers by the selected boundary price explicitly. The pinned draft's input-item contextual-equality rules and its computed-key tie examples need follow-up reconciliation with this engine behavior. This reference records the observed contract, not a certification of all computed-key ties. **C10 source-consistency review ? 26 October 2026:** At review revision `b4723ff5`, `highest` sorts by the modified key and then selects input items contextually equal to the boundary item. The framework defines atomic contextual equality using `compare(A,B)=0`, while the same source's `highest(1 to 25, (), fn { . idiv 10 })` example lists `20` through `25`. Released Bosak returns only `25`. [The C10 receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-2.md) retains the example expectation and both source texts as an unresolved specification-reading issue; it does not certify all computed-key ties or diagnose an engine correction from that example alone. sort-by accepts key-definition maps in major-to-minor order, including key, order and collation fields. Equal full sort keys retain input order. collation-available reports whether a URI is recognized; it does not fetch that URI. Numeric comparisons do not require a string collation. ## 7. Applicability Use when numeric prices and scores are present, valid and comparable; the fixture uses decimal values and no NaN/missing keys. Lowest price is the primary rule and highest score the secondary. No purchasing action is taken. If every equal-price offer must be retained, use the explicit filter shown here. String ordering policy needs a deliberate collation or fallback. ## 8. Structure Read offers, define numeric price/score callbacks, select a lowest boundary, filter all equal-price records, and sort with price ascending then score descending. ## 9. Participants Offer nodes supply identifiers and metrics. Key callbacks supply comparable decimals. Boundary selection provides a reference price. Filtering retains all tied quotes. Multi-key sort orders the report. ## 10. Collaborations Use simple-map projection `! string(@id)` after sorting nodes. A path such as `$ranked/@id` normalizes node results to document order and can discard the ranking. Empty offers bypass the boundary-price callback. The fallback fixture selects codepoint collation when the requested URI is unavailable. ## 11. Consequences Ties are explicit and the report preserves computed ranking. Lowest/highest are not a substitute for an all-equal-key selection policy on arbitrary records. An invalid key or order raises the demonstrated errors. Checking collation availability does not certify every collation feature. ## 12. Sample Code Complete synthetic input: ```xml ``` ### XPath 4.0 expression [Runnable file](../examples/supplier-offer-ranking/main.xpath): ```xpath let $offers := parse-xml('')/offers/offer let $price := function($o) { xs:decimal($o/@price) } let $score := function($o) { xs:decimal($o/@score) } let $boundary := lowest($offers, (), $price) let $cheapest := if (empty($boundary)) then () else $offers[$price(.) eq $price($boundary[1])] let $collation := 'http://www.w3.org/2005/xpath-functions/collation/codepoint' return concat('cheapest=', string-join($cheapest/@id, ','), '; bestScore=', string-join(highest($offers, (), $score)/@id, ','), '; ranked=', string-join(sort-by($offers, (map {'key': $price}, map {'key': $score, 'order': 'descending'})) ! Complete synthetic input:

```xml
<offers><offer id="A" price="10" score="90"/><offer id="B" price="8" score="90"/><offer id="C" price="8" score="85"/><offer id="D" price="12" score="92"/></offers>
```

### XPath 4.0 expression

[Runnable file](../examples/supplier-offer-ranking/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $offers := parse-xml('<offers><offer id="A" price="10" score="90"/><offer id="B" price="8" score="90"/><offer id="C" price="8" score="85"/><offer id="D" price="12" score="92"/></offers>')/offers/offer
let $price := function($o) { xs:decimal($o/@price) }
let $score := function($o) { xs:decimal($o/@score) }
let $boundary := lowest($offers, (), $price)
let $cheapest := if (empty($boundary)) then () else $offers[$price(.) eq $price($boundary[1])]
let $collation := 'http://www.w3.org/2005/xpath-functions/collation/codepoint'
return concat('cheapest=', string-join($cheapest/@id, ','), '; bestScore=', string-join(highest($offers, (), $score)/@id, ','), '; ranked=', string-join(sort-by($offers, (map {'key': $price}, map {'key': $score, 'order': 'descending'})) ! string(@id), ','), '; collationAvailable=', collation-available($collation))
```

Exact output:

```text
cheapest=B,C; bestScore=D; ranked=B,C,A,D; collationAvailable=true
```

### XPath 3.1 comparison

[Runnable file](../examples/supplier-offer-ranking/baseline.xpath):

```xpath
let $offers := parse-xml('<offers><offer id="A" price="10" score="90"/><offer id="B" price="8" score="90"/><offer id="C" price="8" score="85"/><offer id="D" price="12" score="92"/></offers>')/offers/offer
return let $cheap := min($offers/@price ! xs:decimal(.))
return let $best := max($offers/@score ! xs:decimal(.))
return let $byScore := sort($offers, (), function($o) { -xs:decimal($o/@score) })
return let $ranked := sort($byScore, (), function($o) { xs:decimal($o/@price) })
return concat('cheapest=', string-join($offers[xs:decimal(@price) eq $cheap]/@id, ','), '; bestScore=', string-join($offers[xs:decimal(@score) eq $best]/@id, ','), '; ranked=', string-join($ranked ! string(@id), ','))
```

Exact output:

```text
cheapest=B,C; bestScore=D; ranked=B,C,A,D
```

Name and Classification **Timestamp deadlines — Frozen 4.0.** [fn:unix-dateTime](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-unix-dateTime), [fn:seconds](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-seconds), and [fn:duration-to-seconds](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-duration-to-seconds). Initial engine delivery: [PR #84](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/84), [revision f7f55b4e](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/f7f55b4e3a6e92da26ac607e34f46aede695cb19), REQ-118 4.0-S2.
