Explicit current negative-epoch and wide-integer diagnostics remain unresolved; source/public1.25.0. Earlier source/public1.1.3 labels below are historical. ## 2. Intent Turn a receipt's epoch timestamp and measured processing time into UTC instants, then report elapsed and remaining seconds against a configured processing budget. Keep milliseconds and seconds explicit so the deadline is not scaled incorrectly. ## 3. Also Known As Epoch conversion and elapsed-budget accounting are descriptive terms. `seconds` constructs a duration; `seconds-from-duration` extracts a component and is not an alias for the total-seconds function. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 adds a scaled `xs:dayTimeDuration` to the UTC Unix epoch. Multiplying `PT1S` by a seconds count builds a duration, and dividing by `PT1S` gets its total seconds. The complete comparison returns the same report. Its epoch addition returns a dateTime; matching report text does not prove the same stamp subtype. ## 5. Motivation A receipt log often stores epoch milliseconds while service budgets use seconds. A 1,250-millisecond processing measurement is 1.25 seconds, not 1,250 seconds. A duration containing minutes also needs total seconds; taking just its seconds component would understate elapsed time. The report exposes both unit conversions. ## 6. Language Alignment In frozen `XPath40`, `unix-dateTime` uses **nonnegative epoch milliseconds** and returns a UTC `xs:dateTimeStamp`; a negative argument raises `FOCA0002`. `XPath40Experimental` supports signed epoch milliseconds within the existing bounded calendar representation. Omitted or empty input means zero (the epoch), not the current time. Unix time assumes 86,400-second days and does not account for leap seconds. `seconds` accepts an optional decimal count, returning a day-time duration with fractional and negative values preserved. `duration-to-seconds` returns an optional decimal total for a day-time duration. Both return empty for empty input. For example PT1M30S has total 90 seconds but a seconds component of 30. Year-month durations cannot be converted to a fixed seconds count by this rule. ## 7. Applicability Use for explicit epoch-unit conversion and elapsed-budget reports from supplied measurements. The fixture assumes nonnegative integer epoch milliseconds, nonnegative elapsed milliseconds, and a nonnegative decimal seconds budget. Negative remaining time is allowed: it reports an overrun. These are measured values, not a clock read. The host owns monotonic measurement, actual cancellation and timeout enforcement; this XPath merely calculates a report. The supported Gregorian date range and decimal precision remain implementation limits. The examples do not establish unlimited timestamp or duration ranges. ## 8. Structure Convert receipt milliseconds to a received UTC instant. Divide measured milliseconds by 1,000 before building an elapsed duration. Build a budget duration directly from seconds. Add both to received time, subtract finished time from the deadline, and project total seconds for the report. ## 9. Participants The receipt supplies timestamp, elapsed measurement and budget with named units. The epoch converter creates the received instant. Duration functions normalize units. DateTime arithmetic derives finished/deadline instants. The comparison reports whether completion is within the budget. ## 10. Collaborations All instants use explicit UTC, avoiding implicit-timezone dependence. The report uses `$finished le $deadline`, so exact equality is within budget. Preserve signed remaining seconds to distinguish unused allowance from an overrun. ## 11. Consequences Fractional measurements survive the conversion. A negative remaining duration signals lateness without losing its magnitude. None of these functions sleeps, retries a request, cancels processing or checks the current wall clock. Calling `unix-dateTime()` always returns the epoch, which must not be mistaken for a receipt's missing timestamp. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Epoch milliseconds, omitted/empty zero and UTC subtype; Experimental signed epochs with frozen negative refusal; Duration total seconds, signs/fractions and bounded-calendar errors. **Boundaries:** Published wide-integer/range fixes are delivered; permissive scalar/cardinality conversion and bounded DateTimeOffset calendar remain separate. Follow-up groups: F01, F02, F08, F10. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. Use `CompileOptions.Compatibility40` for the new calls. The default 3.1 profile rejects them; the comparison uses `Compatibility31`. The existing [catalog harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) checks exact reports/errors and default-profile refusal for successful 4.0 cases. All values are inline and deterministic; no external context or clock is needed. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** [Date/time review](../DATE-TIME-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md), pinned to F&O e7ee4ab8, and [detailed receipt-retention README](../examples/date-contracts/README.md) supply 108 checks across five families: keywords, Gregorian field sets, offsets, units, empty/default, precision and type/cardinality boundaries, plus complete XPath 3.1/4.0 reports. Keywords remain unavailable. Malformed/multi-item tolerance, record conversion and fractional-component loss remain engine follow-ups. Source/public version is 1.1.3; original delivery/unit/gate and historical adopted-pin limits remain. ## 13. finished=', $finished, '; deadline=', $deadline, '; elapsedSeconds=', duration-to-seconds($elapsed), '; remainingSeconds=', duration-to-seconds($deadline - $finished), '; withinBudget=', $finished le $deadline) ``` Exact output: ```text received=2024-01-31T12:00:00Z; sections.13:
Complete synthetic receipt input:

```xml
<receipt epochMilliseconds="1706702400000" elapsedMilliseconds="1250" budgetSeconds="2.5"/>
```

[Complete XPath 4.0 expression](../examples/timestamp-deadlines/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $receipt := parse-xml('<receipt epochMilliseconds="1706702400000" elapsedMilliseconds="1250" budgetSeconds="2.5"/>')/receipt
let $received := unix-dateTime(xs:integer($receipt/@epochMilliseconds))
let $elapsed := seconds(xs:decimal($receipt/@elapsedMilliseconds) div 1000)
let $budget := seconds(xs:decimal($receipt/@budgetSeconds))
let $finished := $received + $elapsed
let $deadline := $received + $budget
return concat('received=', $received, '; finished=', $finished, '; deadline=', $deadline, '; elapsedSeconds=', duration-to-seconds($elapsed), '; remainingSeconds=', duration-to-seconds($deadline - $finished), '; withinBudget=', $finished le $deadline)
```

Exact output:

```text
received=2024-01-31T12:00:00Z; finished=2024-01-31T12:00:01.25Z; deadline=2024-01-31T12:00:02.5Z; elapsedSeconds=1.25; remainingSeconds=1.25; withinBudget=true
```

[Complete XPath 3.1 comparison](../examples/timestamp-deadlines/baseline.xpath):

```xpath
let $receipt := parse-xml('<receipt epochMilliseconds="1706702400000" elapsedMilliseconds="1250" budgetSeconds="2.5"/>')/receipt
return let $received := xs:dateTime('1970-01-01T00:00:00Z') + xs:dayTimeDuration('PT0.001S') * xs:integer($receipt/@epochMilliseconds)
return let $elapsed := xs:dayTimeDuration('PT1S') * (xs:decimal($receipt/@elapsedMilliseconds) div 1000)
return let $budget := xs:dayTimeDuration('PT1S') * xs:decimal($receipt/@budgetSeconds)
return let $finished := $received + $elapsed
return let $deadline := $received + $budget
return concat('received=', $received, '; finished=', $finished, '; deadline=', $deadline, '; elapsedSeconds=', ($elapsed div xs:dayTimeDuration('PT1S')), '; remainingSeconds=', (($deadline - $finished) div xs:dayTimeDuration('PT1S')), '; withinBudget=', $finished le $deadline)
```

Exact output:

```text
received=2024-01-31T12:00:00Z; finished=2024-01-31T12:00:01.25Z; deadline=2024-01-31T12:00:02.5Z; elapsedSeconds=1.25; remainingSeconds=1.25; withinBudget=true
```

functions/uri-option-policy.md.text:
Archive and partner URI policy

Frozen 4.0 — Boolean options and component precedence

**C11 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-3.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited URI options; query precedence gap**. C02-F04: empty structured query map falls back to raw query; unsupported string Booleans remain a type-validation limit. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **URI option policy — Frozen 4.0.** [fn:parse-uri](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-parse-uri) and [fn:build-uri](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-build-uri). Initial engine delivery: [PR #84](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/84), [revision f7f55b4e](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/f7f55b4e3a6e92da26ac607e34f46aede695cb19), REQ-118 4.0-S2. Definitions reviewed 2026-10-12 against immutable [QT4CG function source e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). This review does not recover the historical adopted specification snapshot. General syntax: [RFC 3986](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3986) and [RFC 3987](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3987). ## 2. Intent Interpret a configured network archive as a UNC path and construct an invoice route from a partner endpoint. Choose structured components deliberately when legacy raw fields coexist. ## 3. Also Known As URI component policy and UNC interpretation are descriptive terms; no aliases are registered. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath 3.1 can assemble known routes from host-validated metadata. The comparison below uses separate server/folder/leaf and host attributes; it does not implement generic parsing, percent decoding, UNC detection or password filtering. ## 5. Motivation Archive paths and HTTP endpoints need different interpretation. A leading double slash normally denotes a relative authority; enabling UNC interpretation instead preserves the server/share text as a file path. Partner configuration may retain obsolete raw authority, path and query fields while a new structured route overrides them. ## 6. Language Alignment Compile with `XPathCompatibility.XPath40`. The runner refuses successful new-function fixtures in default 3.1 mode. Both functions accept an optional options map; empty options use defaults. Bosak registers keywords `uri`/`options` for parsing and `parts`/`options` for building. The working keyword fixture verifies the parser's actual metadata. | Option | Reviewed type/default | Effect | |---|---|---| | `allow-deprecated-features` | `xs:boolean`, `false()` | Retain nonempty password-bearing structured userinfo | | `omit-default-ports` | `xs:boolean`, `false()` | Omit recognized scheme-default structured ports | | `unc-path` | `xs:boolean`, `false()` | Interpret leading slashes as UNC when parsing; select the file prefix when building | Always supply Boolean values. Bosak currently applies effective Boolean value: the nonempty string `'false'` enables the tested options. These observed fixtures record a validation gap against the Boolean contract. ## 7. Applicability Use for configured archive paths and route assembly. Parsing does not validate a destination or perform network/file I/O. The synthetic `demo:placeholder` is example data. Password filtering is not redaction: the original URI and raw authority can retain the text. ## 8. Structure Parse archive with explicit UNC policy; parse partner with default-port omission; build a fresh route from host, scheme, segments and query map. Do not copy raw authority into the structured route. ## 9. Participants The route XML supplies configuration; component maps carry parsed values; `path-segments` preserves `INV/2048` as one encoded business identifier; the options map supplies Boolean policy. ## 10. Collaborations `parse-xml`, map lookup, `exists`, `concat` and `encode-for-uri` support the complete report and portable comparison. [Invoice API URIs](invoice-api-uris.md) explains decoding, repeated query keys and textual roundtrip limits. ## 11. Consequences Structured userinfo/host/port take precedence over raw authority when any is present. Otherwise raw authority is appended unchanged: password/default-port options do not inspect it, as stated by the reviewed draft. Nonempty segment sequences override raw path; an empty sequence falls back, while one empty string is a present segment and can produce an empty path. A nonempty query map overrides raw query. **Observed draft gap:** an empty map is still a present item under the reviewed rules, but Bosak falls back to raw query. Remove the raw query field when deliberately building with an empty query map. UNC construction uses a literal `:////` prefix after `file`. The tested leading path slash therefore yields `file://///server/share`; this is verified spelling, not a claim of canonical file-URI representation. Password-free userinfo with an empty password (`demo:`) is retained. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Boolean deprecated/default-port/UNC policies; Structured versus raw authority/path/query precedence; Nonmap option and malformed authority errors. **Boundaries:** String false currently enables a Boolean option; empty query map currently falls back to raw query. Raw-authority bypass itself is draft-defined. Follow-up groups: F01, F04. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. See [FunctionLibrary](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs): `UriBooleanOption`, `ParseUri` and `BuildUri`. The empty-query-map branch and option truthiness are observed implementation limits. Public function conversion rejects non-map options with `XPTY0004`, including empty parse input; unmatched bracket authority raises `FOUR0001`. No engine changes are included here. **Supplementary contract review (2026-10-12):** Keyword drift: implemented uri differs from pinned value; the [signature audit](../SIGNATURE-CONTRACT-AUDIT.md) publishes paired success/refusal files. Existing positional option-policy examples remain valid. ## 13. Sample Code Complete synthetic input: ```xml ``` Complete [main fixture](../examples/uri-option-policy/main.xpath): ```xpath let $r := parse-xml('')/routes return let $archive := parse-uri(string($r/archive/@value), map {'unc-path': true()}) return let $api := parse-uri(string($r/partner/@value), map {'omit-default-ports': true()}) return let $target := build-uri(map {'scheme': $api?scheme, 'host': $api?host, 'port': $api?port, 'authority': 'ignored.example.test:8443', 'path': '/ignored', 'path-segments': ('', 'v2', 'invoices', 'INV/2048'), 'query': 'ignored=1', 'query-parameters': map {'status': 'ready now'}}) return concat('archive-scheme=', $archive?scheme, '; archive=', $archive?filepath, '; partner=', $target, '; userinfo=', exists($api?userinfo)) ``` Output: ```text archive-scheme=file; archive=//files.example.test/invoices/October 2026; partner=https://api.example.test/v2/invoices/INV%2F2048?status=ready%20now; userinfo=false ``` The archive has no parsed host component under UNC policy. Partner password-bearing userinfo is absent and port 443 is omitted; the freshly built route overrides deliberately conflicting raw fields. ### XPath 3.1 comparison Host-provided normalized archive metadata and validated HTTPS host allow this scoped construction: ```xpath let $r := parse-xml('')/routes return let $archive := concat('//', $r/archive/@server, '/', $r/archive/@folder, '/', $r/archive/@leaf) return let $target := concat('https://', $r/partner/@host, '/v2/invoices/', encode-for-uri('INV/2048'), '?status=', encode-for-uri('ready now')) return concat('archive=', $archive, '; partner=', $target) ``` Output: ```text archive=//files.example.test/invoices/October 2026; partner=https://api.example.test/v2/invoices/INV%2F2048?status=ready%20now ``` This comparison constructs the two addresses; it does not produce parsed scheme/userinfo evidence. It requires the separate normalized attributes and an explicit host validation policy. ### Complete fixture inventory The [manifest](../examples/cases.json) runs all 28 cases through [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs). | Fixture | Exact output or error marker | |---|---| | [main](../examples/uri-option-policy/main.xpath) | `archive-scheme=file; archive=//files.example.test/invoices/October 2026; partner=https://api.example.test/v2/invoices/INV%2F2048?status=ready%20now; userinfo=false` | | [unc-default](../examples/uri-option-policy/unc-default.xpath) | `scheme=; host=server; path=/share` | | [unc-enabled](../examples/uri-option-policy/unc-enabled.xpath) | `file\|//server/share\|false` [parse-password-default](../examples/uri-option-policy/parse-password-default.xpath) | `false` | | [parse-password-allow](../examples/uri-option-policy/parse-password-allow.xpath) | `demo:placeholder` `XPTY0004` | | [keyword-options](../examples/uri-option-policy/keyword-options.xpath) | `host` | | [nonboolean-unc-observed](../examples/uri-option-policy/nonboolean-unc-observed.xpath) | `file` | Names ending `observed` freeze current behavior rather than certify draft conformance. The empty-input/non-map case verifies argument conversion rejection. ## 14. Performance Operations process strings and maps in memory. No benchmark, destination access or universal complexity guarantee is claimed. ## 15. Known Uses This archive/partner case is synthetic integration evidence. Existing [XPath40FunctionTests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Standard.Tests/XPath40FunctionTests.cs) include `ParseUri_UserInfoPasswordDiscardedUnlessDeprecatedAllowed`, `ParseUri_OmitDefaultPorts`, `ParseUri_FileScheme_SegmentsAndFilepath`, `ParseUri_UnmatchedBracketInAuthority_RaisesFour0001`, `BuildUri_OmitDefaultPortsOption`, `BuildUri_UncPathOption_DoubleSlashPrefix`, `BuildUri_QueryParameters_EscapeAndEmptyKey` and `BuildUri_PathSegmentsEscapedOnlyWhenHierarchical`. The [4.0 runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs) has no exact fn-parse-uri or fn-build-uri GatedSets assignment. Named tests and fixtures provide separate evidence; gate membership is unchanged. ## 16. Related Features [Invoice API URIs](invoice-api-uris.md), [completeness audit](../COMPLETENESS-AUDIT.md) and [supplementary coverage audit](../SUPPLEMENTARY-COVERAGE-AUDIT.md). sections.13:
Complete synthetic input:

```xml
<routes><archive server="files.example.test" folder="invoices" leaf="October 2026" value="//files.example.test/invoices/October%202026"/><partner host="api.example.test" value="https://demo:placeholder@api.example.test:443/legacy"/></routes>
```

Complete [main fixture](../examples/uri-option-policy/main.xpath):

```xpath
let $r := parse-xml('<routes><archive server="files.example.test" folder="invoices" leaf="October 2026" value="//files.example.test/invoices/October%202026"/><partner host="api.example.test" value="https://demo:placeholder@api.example.test:443/legacy"/></routes>')/routes
return let $archive := parse-uri(string($r/archive/@value), map {'unc-path': true()})
return let $api := parse-uri(string($r/partner/@value), map {'omit-default-ports': true()})
return let $target := build-uri(map {'scheme': $api?scheme, 'host': $api?host, 'port': $api?port, 'authority': 'ignored.example.test:8443', 'path': '/ignored', 'path-segments': ('', 'v2', 'invoices', 'INV/2048'), 'query': 'ignored=1', 'query-parameters': map {'status': 'ready now'}})
return concat('archive-scheme=', $archive?scheme, '; archive=', $archive?filepath, '; partner=', $target, '; userinfo=', exists($api?userinfo))
```

Output:

```text
archive-scheme=file; archive=//files.example.test/invoices/October 2026; partner=https://api.example.test/v2/invoices/INV%2F2048?status=ready%20now; userinfo=false
```

The archive has no parsed host component under UNC policy. Partner password-bearing userinfo is absent and port 443 is omitted; the freshly built route overrides deliberately conflicting raw fields.

```xpath

return let $target := concat('https://', $r/partner/@host, '/v2/invoices/', encode-for-uri('INV/2048'), '?status=', encode-for-uri('ready now'))
return concat('archive=', $archive, '; partner=', $target)
```

Output:

```text
archive=//files.example.test/invoices/October 2026; partner=https://api.example.test/v2/invoices/INV%2F2048?status=ready%20now
```

functions/warehouse-pick-sorting.md.text:
Warehouse Pick Sorting

Retained sorting functions — portable workflow and 4.0 contract limits

**C11 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-3.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Blocked for full default-key/collation/order parity**. C02-F05/F06: explicit empty-key defaults, unknown-collation refusal and numeric ordering remain incomplete; passing one NaN input order is not complete ordering support. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification [fn:sort](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-sort) and [array:sort](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-array-sort) are existing 3.1 functions retained in the 4.0 draft. They are outside the 117-name inventory of 4.0-only functions. Implementation reviewed at Bosak [source baseline 0597047a](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/blob/0597047aed99851d10445993e2e636f3aeb437f2/src/Bosak.XPath.Standard/Functions/FunctionLibrary.cs), with the named tests below. Historical adopted draft pins remain unavailable. Current review: 2026-10-12 against immutable [QT4CG F&O source e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/function-catalog.xml). ## 2. Intent Produce a warehouse pick order by aisle and numeric bin, preserving input order for tied locations. Sort a sequence of XML lines and an array whose members contain both the original line and its quantity without separating that payload. ## 3. Also Known As Stable key sorting and lexicographic composite keys describe this workflow. There is no new function name or alias. ## 4. History / Supersedes The stable [3.1 sequence sort](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions-31/#func-sort) and [3.1 array sort](https://www.w3.org/TR/xpath-functions-31/#func-array-sort) already support a collation and a key callback. The reviewed 4.0 draft defines these compatibility functions through `sort-by`/`array:sort-by`, including the new numeric comparison rules. Retaining the function names does not make every numeric contract unchanged. The portable report below runs in both profiles. ## 5. Motivation Bin `10` should follow bin `2` within an aisle. Sorting raw bin text would put `10` before `2`. Equal-location lines must retain their original order, and quantities must travel with their corresponding lines. Explicit typed keys and member boundaries make those rules visible. ## 6. Language Alignment Both functions have one-, two- and three-argument forms. Omitted/empty collation uses the context default. An omitted key uses atomized input values. Explicit empty keys currently raise `XPTY0004` in the nonempty sequence/array probes, although the reviewed 4.0 draft defines default-on-empty. Supply `data#1` explicitly as a verified workaround; an empty key argument differs from a key callback that returns an empty sequence. A key can be a sequence: values are compared lexicographically, with the first differing position determining order. Equal complete keys preserve input order; an empty key precedes a nonempty key. The sequence callback receives one input item. The array callback receives a whole member, which can contain multiple items or be empty. Sorting rearranges members without flattening their payload. `array:append` deliberately creates one two-item member per line; an `array { ... }` constructor over a flat sequence would create different member boundaries. **Observed numeric gaps:** Bosak's retained functions use the shared `XdmValueComparer`, rather than the reviewed exact numeric ordering. Input `(3.1e0, 3.1)` remains double then decimal because promotion makes its keys tie; the reviewed 4.0 ordering puts decimal first. Both sequence and array probes record that limit. The two-item NaN probes also depend on input direction: `(NaN, 1)` produces number then NaN, while `(1, NaN)` produces NaN then number. The pinned numeric ordering places NaN below numbers. These are observed gaps, not a promised ordering policy for larger inputs. Corrected engine behavior must update the observed expectations while retaining historical migration notes. QName keys are refused in the demonstrated case. The reviewed sorting rules also exclude nonordered QName keys; broader `fn:compare` support does not authorize assuming every atomic family is a valid sort key. Bosak accepts the unknown-collation URI in both empty-input and nonempty-string probes; the latter returns codepoint-like order rather than `FOCH0002`. These results do not establish that the URI is supported. Use a known explicit collation and keep unknown-URI validation as an implementation follow-up. ## 7. Applicability This synthetic warehouse vocabulary assumes present IDs/aisles, valid integer bins and quantities, and a declared codepoint aisle policy. It omits route optimization, stock allocation, units, scheduling and locale-sensitive aisle names. Invalid bin text raises a constructor error. Production data should be validated before sorting, and NaN/mixed numeric keys need an explicit policy. ## 8. Structure Parse XML, construct an aisle/bin key, sort original lines, build an array of line/quantity members, and sort those members using the key from their first item. Render both orders for reconciliation. ## 9. Participants Lines carry locations and quantities. A key callback returns a string followed by an integer. The collation controls aisle strings. Array members bind each line to its converted quantity. Output projection preserves the sorted order. ## 10. Collaborations Use `string(@aisle)` and `xs:integer(@bin)` to state both key types. Compare corresponding key positions, not aisle strings against bin integers. Simple-map projection (`! string(@id)`) preserves the sequence's chosen order; a path over nodes can restore document order. The member callback accesses the line with `$member[1]`, and indexed output keeps its quantity alongside it. Lines C and D share a key and therefore remain in input order. ## 11. Consequences Both profiles produce C, D, B, A with quantities 3, 4, 1, 2. The workflow uses homogeneous types at each key position and avoids the observed mixed numeric and NaN gaps. Stable ties do not define a secondary business priority. An empty batch yields empty sequence/member reports, while an empty array member remains a member in the separate boundary probe. ## 12. Implementation **C02 reconciliation — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Function/options review](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.md) reconciles Stable lexicographic keys with sequence items versus whole array members; Omitted versus explicit-empty keys and explicit data#1 workaround; Known collation, mixed-type errors, NaN and exact cross-numeric order. **Boundaries:** Explicit empty keys, unknown collations, NaN and promoted mixed-number ties remain unsupported draft contracts; use validated homogeneous keys. Follow-up groups: F05, F06. Normal/empty/error evidence and unsupported remainder are recorded per function in the [review matrix](../FUNCTION-OPTIONS-RECONCILIATION.json). This is bounded documentation reconciliation, not whole-signature or AC-04 acceptance. The report runs with either `CompileOptions.Compatibility40` or `CompileOptions.Compatibility31`. Keyword calls use 4.0 syntax and match the reviewed names `input`/`array`, `collation` and `key`. The explicit `sort-by` comparison verifies the illustrated sequence-key equivalence, not every draft contract or support for the draft's entire array-sort-by surface. The [catalog harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) checks `baselineExpected` for shared default-mode outcomes and `baselineError` for keyword refusal. Error cases verify diagnostic markers. Observed-limit fixtures preserve current evidence rather than certifying conformance. No engine or gate membership changes are made by this delivery. **Existing-function default review (2026-10-12):** The [ordering/default review](../ORDER-DEFAULT-CONTRACT-REVIEW.md) and [detailed supplier README](../examples/order-contracts/README.md) add 132 checks across sort/array:sort/min/max/map:merge, explicit key/options and collation/NaN/cardinality boundaries, and six full 3.1/4.0 reports. Supplier price-plus-ID keys preserve business tie-breaking under source reordering. Use simple mapping to project sorted node IDs; a path restores document order. This is targeted evidence, not an engine fix or full D2 completion. ## 13. Sample Code Complete synthetic input: ```xml ``` [XPath 4.0 runnable file](../examples/warehouse-pick-sorting/main.xpath): ```xpath let $rows := parse-xml('')/picks/line return let $cp := 'http://www.w3.org/2005/xpath-functions/collation/codepoint' return let $key := function($line) { (string($line/@aisle), xs:integer($line/@bin)) } return let $ordered := sort($rows, $cp, $key) return let $members := fold-left($rows, [], function($a, $line) { array:append($a, ($line, xs:integer($line/@qty))) }) return let $sorted := array:sort($members, $cp, function($member) { $key($member[1]) }) return concat('sequence=', string-join($ordered ! string(@id), ','), '; members=', string-join(for $i in 1 to array:size($sorted) return concat($sorted($i)[1]/@id, ':', $sorted($i)[2]), ',')) ``` Exact output: ```text sequence=C,D,B,A; members=C:3,D:4,B:1,A:2 ``` ### XPath 3.1 comparison The [complete 3.1 runnable file](../examples/warehouse-pick-sorting/baseline.xpath) contains the same expression and input; select `Compatibility31`. Its exact output is also: ```text sequence=C,D,B,A; members=C:3,D:4,B:1,A:2 ``` No newer syntax is needed for this workflow. The distinction appears in the separate numeric-key probes, not in the intentionally portable report. ### Complete fixture inventory | Runnable case | Mode | Exact result/error marker | Default 3.1 operators-and-syntax/array-member-iterat.text:
Array member iteration

Practical reference: Frozen 4.0

**C11 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-3.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Verified bounded member binding**. No complete iteration/coercion/type grammar certification; C05 retains the remaining combinations. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Array member iteration** - **Frozen 4.0**. Delivery family: [REQ-118](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) / [REQ-123 registry](../../FEATURE_REQUESTS.md). Section provenance: See the linked REQ dossiers and implementation evidence. [Primary implementation evidence](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) records the shipped behavior; this entry adds executable user-facing examples under REQ-126, rather than announcing a new engine feature. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [XPath 4.0: for expressions](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-for-expressions). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #87](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/87), [immutable mainline revision `ec793559`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/ec79355936a29ac70eeea3ae47e4c4e2ee00d813) (2026-10-08). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Iterate members while preserving each member as one sequence binding. ## 3. Also Known As Use the name and spelling in this entry and its executable files. Related functions or instruction forms are described in the primary test evidence; no additional alias is adopted here. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1, iterate 1 to array:size($parcels) and call array:get. Compare the [complete earlier-version baseline](../examples/array-member-iteration/before.xpath) with the [complete expression](../examples/array-member-iteration/main.xpath). Both yield `2,1` for this synthetic input. They demonstrate this task, not universal equivalence of the two mechanisms. ## 5. Motivation A packing plan stores each parcel as an array member containing its item sequence. Iterate members while preserving each member as one sequence binding. Keeping this task explicit makes it possible to choose the feature for a practical reason and verify what the receiving application will see. ## 6. Language Alignment Read the behavior as XPath/XSLT semantics. Similar vocabulary in another programming language is not a compatibility promise. A member can contain several items; flattening the array first loses parcel boundaries. ## 7. Applicability Use this form when solving the stated task and the consumer permits the declared compatibility level. Keep the earlier baseline when the application requires 3.1 expressions or portable 3.0 stylesheets. A member can contain several items; flattening the array first loses parcel boundaries. ## 8. Structure ```xquery string-join((for member $parcel in [('FILTER-A','BOLT-M8'), 'MANUAL'] return string(count($parcel))), ',') ``` This is the worked case's syntax, not a replacement for the full language grammar. Required namespaces and surrounding context are supplied in the linked complete files. ## 9. Participants XPath31Expression, CompileOptions, the parser/compiler, and the shared runtime/function library provide the public execution path. [Primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) identify the feature's implementation contract. The examples use public APIs only. ## 10. Collaborations The case combines source values, the named feature, and explicit output formatting. [Worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md) show how selection, construction, and business rejection fit into larger transformations. ## 11. Consequences Benefit: Iterate members while preserving each member as one sequence binding. Tradeoff: the declared compatibility level and edge rules become part of the consumer contract. A member can contain several items; flattening the array first loses parcel boundaries. ## 12. Implementation **C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S4-iteration. Members and map-entry values remain whole sequences, positions continue across container sequences, empty collections bind nothing, and invalid container items refuse XPTY0141. Container iteration preserves containing focus. Do not flatten member boundaries or infer portable map entry order. Complete typed iteration combinations and host bindings remain outside bounded controls. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows. Compile the after/edge expressions at XPathCompatibility.XPath40. The baseline uses XPath31. The example harness checks default-mode refusal for successful 4.0 cases; negative cases pin the declared error. See [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs): it executes the published files from the [case manifest](../examples/cases.json). This documentation slice changes no engine source. ## 13. Sample Code Input is synthetic and declared directly in the complete expression. The [complete expression](../examples/array-member-iteration/main.xpath) yields `2,1`. The [edge case](../examples/array-member-iteration/edge.xpath) yields `0`. No external resources or application variables are required. See the [example runner](../examples/README.md) for commands and host context. ## 14. Performance Notes Expected class: per-member iteration. Member sequences retain their boundaries, and processing those contents adds its own cost. These are implementation expectations, not measured deltas. No benchmark is claimed; use the repository benchmark harness before making workload-specific speed or memory claims. ## 15. Known Uses Executable example IDs: `array-member-iteration-main`, `array-member-iteration-edge`, `array-member-iteration-before` in `CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome`. Existing unit evidence: [primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Chapter-level evidence does not promote a qt4tests set into GatedSets; conformance status remains owned by the harness and delivery records. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Compile_ForMember_31Mode_ThrowsXpst0003`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_ForMember_IteratesMembers`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_ForMember_MultiItemAndArrayMembersAreBoundWhole`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). No feature-specific qt4 set assignment recorded here; unit evidence is listed explicitly. This is not a claim of absent upstream tests. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features See the [catalog index](../README.md), [worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md), and the alternatives in section 4. The case may be used independently of the larger chapters. *Created 2026-10-11: verified practical catalog example and earlier-version baseline.*

operators-and-syntax/destructuring-let.m.text:
Destructuring let

Catalog entry — Operators & syntax · Frozen 4.0

**C11 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-3.md) records 4 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited bindings; annotated-record blocker**. C05-K03: annotated-record unknown-field destructuring incorrectly returns empty instead of XPTY0004; broader type/choice coercion limits remain. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Destructuring `let` bindings** — **Frozen 4.0** (ships at the `XPath40` level; static XPST0003 at `XPath31`). Spec: XPath 4.0 §4.14 (FLWOR expressions), [QT4CG PR #1131](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/pull/1131). Landed: REQ-123 destructuring-let cluster, [PR #129](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/129) (main `b8e4b9f`, 2026-10-10). **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [XPath 4.0: let expressions](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-let-expressions). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #129](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/129), [immutable mainline revision `b8e4b9f5`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/b8e4b9f510543c04d88a7c10ee2af28808a0fd5c) (2026-10-10). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Bind several variables at once by decomposing a sequence, an array, or a map on the right-hand side — `let $($x, $y) := (1, 2)` binds `$x` to `1` and `$y` to `2` in one clause, evaluating the right-hand side exactly once. ## 3. Also Known As "Destructuring binding" (spec), "tuple binding" (informal, from the tuple-builder relative). Not to be confused with the `for` clause's *tuple* destructuring, which is a separate (larger) construct. ## 4. History / Supersedes Supersedes three 3.1 idioms, one per container kind: | Before (3.1) | After (4.0) | |---|---| | `let $x := $seq[1] let $y := $seq[2] return …` — repeated positional indexing, RHS re-evaluated per binding if not manually cached | `let $($x, $y) := $seq return …` — one evaluation, positional bind | | `let $a := $arr(1) let $b := $arr(2) return …` | `let $[$a, $b] := $arr return …` | | `let $n := map:get($m, "name") let $a := map:get($m, "addr") return …` | `let ${$name, $addr} := $m return …` — keys are the variable local names | ## 5. Motivation The 3.1 idioms are error-prone in two ways: the RHS is visually repeated (or manually hoisted into a helper variable, cluttering scope), and positional indexing silently does the wrong thing when the sequence is shorter than expected. Destructuring makes the arity contract explicit and puts the shape of the data next to the names it feeds. ## 6. Language Alignment Prior art: ML/Haskell pattern bindings, ES6 `const {a, b} = obj` / `const [x, y] = arr`. **Semantic drift — read before relying on intuition:** - The **last variable of a sequence pattern takes all remaining items** (`let $($x, $y) := (1,2,3)` → `$y = (2,3)`); ES6 array destructuring instead discards surplus elements. Surplus *variables* (too few items) bind `()`. - The **array form discards surplus members but requires each bound index**: `let $[$a, $b] := [1,2,3]` discards member 3, but too few members for the variables is **FOAY0001**, not `undefined`-style filling. - The **ordinary map form binds by variable name** (`${$name}` looks up key `"name"`); a missing ordinary-map key binds `()`. Annotated records have a separate undeclared-field lookup rule. The current engine incorrectly binds empty for that record case; C05 K03 retains the required `XPTY0004` expectation. ## 7. Applicability Use for: unpacking fixed-shape sequences/arrays/maps at the head of a FLWOR; replacing two-or-more positional `let`s over the same value. Do **not** use for: library expressions that must still compile at `XPath31` (static XPST0003); one-item unpacks (`let $x := $seq[1]` remains clearer); hot loops where the save/restore cost (§14) matters and the 3.1 form was already hoisted. ## 8. Structure ``` LetBinding ::= SimpleLetBinding | DestructuringLetBinding DestructuringLetBinding ::= "$" ("(" | "[" | "{") VariableSpec ("," VariableSpec)* (")" | "]" | "}") TypeDeclaration? ":=" ExprSingle VariableSpec ::= "$" VarName (TypeDeclaration)? (* per-variable type, optional *) ``` Three bracket kinds select the source container: `(` sequence, `[` single array, `{` single map. ## 9. Participants - `XPathParser.ParseDestructuringLetBinding` — parses all three kinds; gated on the parser's xpath40 flag; empty pattern → XPST0003. - `XPathAstNode.LetDestructuringKind`, `DestructuringVariable` — AST model. - Opcodes `Destructure`, `SaveVariables`, `RestoreVariables` (`IrOpCode` 1.12) — binding extraction and lexical scoping, lowered by `IrLowerer` (1.54). - `VmEngine` (2.173/2.174) — `Destructure` semantics, `EnforceType` §3.4.2 coercion, `TryRelabelToDerivedNumeric` (PR 254 relabeling). - `EvaluationContext.TryGetDirectVariable` (2.36) — direct-binding probe for `SaveVariables`. ## 10. Collaborations - **Typed simple lets** (`let $v as xs:T := e`) — parsed at XP40+ as part of this slice; `EnforceType` applies XPath 4.0 §3.4.2 coercion when `IsXPath40` (untypedAtomic cast, numeric promotion, record coercion, derived-integer relabeling). - **Structural record types** — a `map(K,V)`/`record(...)` whole-pattern type validates the RHS shape (record patterns reject undeclared variables). - **Lexical scoping** — `SaveVariables`/`RestoreVariables` wrap every `LetExpression` binding group; a trailing reference to a destructured variable outside the let's body raises XPST0008. (Caveat: emitted for `LetExpression` bindings only; XQuery full-FLWOR scoping has its own machinery.) ## 11. Consequences Benefits: single RHS evaluation; arity made explicit; map unpacks name their keys at the binding site. Liabilities: three binding semantics to learn (sequence rest / array strictness / map-by-name) — the drift table in §6 is the cheat sheet. Relabeling changes the *annotation*, not the datum (`42` → `xs:short` ✓; `2.5` → `xs:integer` is XPTY0004, never truncation). Save/Restore pairs are exception-unsafe by design (abandoned evaluations discard the frame with the whole stack — intentional). ## 12. Implementation **C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers REQ123-destructuring. Sequence rest/short inputs, array member groups/surplus/short errors, map missing keys, per-variable/whole-pattern types, duplicates and lexical shadowing are mapped. Undeclared annotated-record fields incorrectly bind empty when destructured. K03 retains the required record-lookup XPTY0004 expectation. Plain-map missing-key emptiness remains a different supported contract. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows. Files: `src/Bosak.XPath.Parser/Ast/XPathParser.cs` (1.74), `src/Bosak.XPath.Parser/Ast/XPathAstNode.cs` (1.25), `src/Bosak.XPath.Compiler/Ir/IrOpCode.cs` (1.12), `src/Bosak.XPath.Compiler/Ir/IrLowerer.cs` (1.54), `src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Vm/VmEngine.cs` (2.173/2.174), `src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Vm/EvaluationContext.cs` (2.36). Version gate: XPST0003 at `XPath31`; fully legal at `XPath40`. Regression: `VersionGateTests` (0.20, +10 rows), `ParserTests` (0.11, +6 AST tests). ## 13. Sample Code Additional executable catalog cases unpack invoice metadata and explicitly test a missing currency key: [main](../examples/destructuring-let/main.xpath) produces `INV-1042 / EUR`; [edge](../examples/destructuring-let/edge.xpath) returns missing currency cardinality `0`. These run at `XPath40` and verify default-mode refusal. Start with [the invoice chapter's practical migration pair](../worked-examples/invoice-to-erp/README.md#where-xpath-40-can-improve-readability): unpack invoice ID and currency from a metadata map to build a display label. sections.2: Bind several variables at once by decomposing a sequence, an array, or a map on the right-hand side — `let $($x, $y) := (1, 2)` binds `$x` to `1` and `$y` to `2` in one clause, evaluating the right-hand side exactly once.
sections.3: "Destructuring binding" (spec), "tuple binding" (informal, from the tuple-builder relative). Not to be confused with the `for` clause's *tuple* destructuring, which is a separate (larger) construct.
sections.4:
Supersedes three 3.1 idioms, one per container kind:

| Before (3.1) | After (4.0) |
|---|---|
| `let $x := $seq[1] let $y := $seq[2] return …` — repeated positional indexing, RHS re-evaluated per binding if not manually cached | `let $($x, $y) := $seq return …` — one evaluation, positional bind |
| `let $a := $arr(1) let $b := $arr(2) return …` | `let $[$a, $b] := $arr return …` |
| `let $n := map:get($m, "name") let $a := map:get($m, "addr") return …` | `let ${$name, $addr} := $m return …` — keys are the variable local names |
sections.5: The 3.1 idioms are error-prone in two ways: the RHS is visually repeated (or manually hoisted into a helper variable, cluttering scope), and positional indexing silently does the wrong thing when the sequence is shorter than expected. Destructuring makes the arity contract explicit and puts the shape of the data next to the names it feeds.
sections.6:
Prior art: ML/Haskell pattern bindings, ES6 `const {a, b} = obj` / `const [x, y] = arr`.

**Semantic drift — read before relying on intuition:**

- The **last variable of a sequence pattern takes all remaining items** (`let $($x, $y) := (1,2,3)` → `$y = (2,3)`); ES6 array destructuring instead discards surplus elements. Surplus *variables* (too few items) bind `()`.
- The **array form discards surplus members but requires each bound index**: `let $[$a, $b] := [1,2,3]` discards member 3, but too few members for the variables is **FOAY0001**, not `undefined`-style filling.
- The **ordinary map form binds by variable name** (`${$name}` looks up key `"name"`); a missing ordinary-map key binds `()`. Annotated records have a separate undeclared-field lookup rule. The current engine incorrectly binds empty for that record case; C05 K03 retains the required `XPTY0004` expectation.
sections.7:
Use for: unpacking fixed-shape sequences/arrays/maps at the head of a FLWOR; replacing two-or-more positional `let`s over the same value.

Do **not** use for: library expressions that must still compile at `XPath31` (static XPST0003); one-item unpacks (`let $x := $seq[1]` remains clearer); hot loops where the save/restore cost (§14) matters and the 3.1 form was already hoisted.
sections.8:
```
LetBinding ::= SimpleLetBinding | DestructuringLetBinding
DestructuringLetBinding ::= "$" ("(" | "[" | "{") VariableSpec ("," VariableSpec)* (")" | "]" | "}")
                            TypeDeclaration? ":=" ExprSingle
VariableSpec ::= "$" VarName (TypeDeclaration)?        (* per-variable type, optional *)
```

Three bracket kinds select the source container: `(` sequence, `[` single array, `{` single map.
sections.9:
- `XPathParser.ParseDestructuringLetBinding` — parses all three kinds; gated on the parser's xpath40 flag; empty pattern → XPST0003.
- `XPathAstNode.LetDestructuringKind`, `DestructuringVariable` — AST model.
- Opcodes `Destructure`, `SaveVariables`, `RestoreVariables` (`IrOpCode` 1.12) — binding extraction and lexical scoping, lowered by `IrLowerer` (1.54).
- `VmEngine` (2.173/2.174) — `Destructure` semantics, `EnforceType` §3.4.2 coercion, `TryRelabelToDerivedNumeric` (PR 254 relabeling).
- `EvaluationContext.TryGetDirectVariable` (2.36) — direct-binding probe for `SaveVariables`.
sections.10:
- **Typed simple lets** (`let $v as xs:T := e`) — parsed at XP40+ as part of this slice; `EnforceType` applies XPath 4.0 §3.4.2 coercion when `IsXPath40` (untypedAtomic cast, numeric promotion, record coercion, derived-integer relabeling).
- **Structural record types** — a `map(K,V)`/`record(...)` whole-pattern type validates the RHS shape (record patterns reject undeclared variables).
- **Lexical scoping** — `SaveVariables`/`RestoreVariables` wrap every `LetExpression` binding group; a trailing reference to a destructured variable outside the let's body raises XPST0008. (Caveat: emitted for `LetExpression` bindings only; XQuery full-FLWOR scoping has its own machinery.)
sections.11:
Benefits: single RHS evaluation; arity made explicit; map unpacks name their keys at the binding site.

Liabilities: three binding semantics to learn (sequence rest / array strictness / map-by-name) — the drift table in §6 is the cheat sheet. Relabeling changes the *annotation*, not the datum (`42` → `xs:short` ✓; `2.5` → `xs:integer` is XPTY0004, never truncation). Save/Restore pairs are exception-unsafe by design (abandoned evaluations discard the frame with the whole stack — intentional).

**C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers REQ123-destructuring. Undeclared annotated-record fields incorrectly bind empty when destructured. K03 retains the required record-lookup XPTY0004 expectation. Plain-map missing-key emptiness remains a different supported contract. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows.

operators-and-syntax/focus-function-synt.text:
Focus-function syntax and pipeline focus

Frozen XPath 4.0 - bounded executable reference

**C11 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-3.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Verified bounded focus-function syntax**. No arbitrary callback/constructor/package context acceptance; C04 mapping-extra-focus and C06 host/static-mode limits remain distinct. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Focus-function syntax** - **Frozen 4.0**, REQ-118 S4. `fn { E }` and `function { E }` omit the signature and take one `item()*` argument, bound as the whole context value. `fn($x) { E }` abbreviates an ordinary explicit-signature inline function; it is not a focus function. This entry is distinct from the [zero-argument focus constructors](focus-functions.md). Delivery: [PR #87](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/87), immutable `ec79355936a29ac70eeea3ae47e4c4e2ee00d813`; that revision already contains the named focus-function tests. Current review: [immutable draft expressions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/b4723ff52fd9d4fabf2b4cd33bd44f21939c512c/specifications/xquery-40/src/expressions.xml), sections `id-inline-func`, `id-focus-functions`, `id-pipeline-operator`, and [InlineFunctionExpr grammar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/b4723ff52fd9d4fabf2b4cd33bd44f21939c512c/specifications/grammar-40/xpath-grammar.xml). Upstream master was refreshed on 22 October 2026. This is a current comparison pin, not recovery of a historically adopted specification revision. Source 1.23.5 remains unpublished; public 1.23.4 already contains this bounded syntax. ## 2. Intent Write a callback whose argument supplies its context value, and distinguish per-item processing from whole-sequence reduction. ## 3. Also Known As A focus function is an inline function without an explicit signature. Both `fn { ... }` and `function { ... }` are supplied forms. The keyword abbreviation `fn($x) { ... }` still has an explicit parameter list. A zero-argument constructor such as `xs:integer()` is a different feature. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1, write `function($line as element()) { xs:decimal($line/@qty) * xs:decimal($line/@unit) }`. The paired [3.0 stylesheet](../examples/focus-function-syntax/report-3.xsl) and [4.0 stylesheet](../examples/focus-function-syntax/report-4.xsl) produce the same order-line report. A parameterized 3.1 function does not implicitly bind its parameter as the focus; references use `$line` explicitly. ## 5. Motivation An order feed contains line quantity and unit amount. The report computes one amount per line, preserves source line order, then reports the count and total over all amounts. A focus callback keeps the attribute calculation readable; the pipeline makes the whole-sequence summary distinct from the mapping stage. [The complete task and fixtures](../examples/focus-function-syntax/README.md) state assumptions, exact input/output and failure behavior. ## 6. Language Alignment This is XPath focus, not ambient JavaScript `this` or an implicit item-by-item lambda. The callback receives a sequence as a single argument and sets position/size to 1/1, even for an empty or multiple-item argument. `=!>` calls its target per input item; `->` evaluates its right expression once with the complete left value as context. The 3.1 `=>` arrow inserts a first function argument; it does not establish the pipeline context. Similar results for a unary example do not make these operators interchangeable. ## 7. Applicability Use a focus function for an attribute-oriented callback or a whole-value operation when its context contract is clear. Use explicit parameters when argument names/types improve clarity or caller position must be passed explicitly. In the report each amount callback receives exactly one line node. Empty input makes no mapping calls; the summary pipeline still runs once with an empty value. ## 8. Structure ```xpath fn { concat(count(.), ':', position(), ':', last()) }((9,8)) ``` This returns `2:1:1`. The runnable [whole-focus probe](../examples/focus-function-syntax/probes/whole-focus.xpath) returns `2:1:1` (count:position:size), and [empty-focus probe](../examples/focus-function-syntax/probes/empty-focus.xpath) returns `0:1:1`. ## 9. Participants [XPathParser.ParseInlineFunction](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Parser/Ast/XPathParser.cs) lowers an omitted signature into a single synthetic parameter plus a PipelineExprNode. [IrLowerer](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Compiler/Ir/IrLowerer.cs) and [VmEngine](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Vm/VmEngine.cs) execute the existing function/focus path. Public callers use XPath31Expression/CompileOptions or ordinary XSLT stylesheets; no new API is introduced. ## 10. Collaborations The report's `$amount` focus function reads the supplied line; `$format` uses the explicit `fn(...)` abbreviation and typed named arguments; the per-item label callback captures those variables. Mapping creates line labels and amounts. The pipeline consumes the amounts as one value for count and sum. Caller focus is restored after inner calls/pipelines, as verified by named probes. ## 11. Consequences A callback argument containing two items is not two calls. A callback invoked from a simple map sees its own position/size 1/1, not the caller's 1/N, 2/N positions. An axis such as `@qty` requires an appropriate node context; the implicit signature alone does not validate the report's line schema. Wrong lexical decimals raise FORG0001 in both report versions. Values are formatted to two display decimals, without claiming a general accounting model. ## 12. Implementation **C04 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Expression/call/focus reconciliation](../EXPRESSION-CALL-FOCUS-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S4-focus. Pipeline whole-value/fixed-focus, focus-function implicit/explicit signatures, lexical capture/restoration and accepted mapping syntax are mapped. Mapping arrow extra arguments incorrectly see mapped-item focus rather than the containing focus. Use for $u in ... return F($u,A...) when extra arguments depend on outer dot/position/size. C03 constructor capture/type coverage remains distinct. Host/profile propagation belongs to C06. This is bounded production/profile evidence, not full grammar or AC-04 acceptance. Thirty new manifest cases use the existing CatalogExampleTests public execution path: 18 focused values/grammar/focus probes, four explicit 3.1 refusals and eight complete stylesheet reports. Sixteen successful XPath cases also assert a 3.1 refusal; two compatible forms retain baseline results. No engine, test runner, compatibility level or gate is changed. The reports use the default Legacy host with effective stylesheet versions 3.0/4.0, not an exhaustive host/module/package matrix. ## 13. Sample Code Input: ``. Both complete stylesheets yield `BOLT=25.00|NUT=10.00|FREE=0.00|lines=3;total=35.00`. Empty input yields `lines=0;total=0.00`; reordered input changes label order while retaining count/total. An invalid quantity `oops` raises FORG0001. [Full examples](../examples/focus-function-syntax/README.md) include every fixture, expected result, context and runnable file. ## 14. Performance Notes The report makes a bounded number of passes over N lines/amounts and emits O(N) labels. Function items and sequence materialization may allocate; no speed or memory advantage over the baseline is claimed. Use the benchmark harness for measured claims. Focus functions do not make the report streaming or parallel. ## 15. Known Uses Applicable evidence under the owner-approved AC-03 policy: `focus-syntax-report-3-normal`, `focus-syntax-report-4-normal`, their empty/reordered/invalid counterparts, and the `focus-syntax-*` probes in [the manifest](../examples/cases.json), executed by [CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs). All 30 case IDs and receipt hashes are recorded in [the slice audit](../FOCUS-FUNCTION-SYNTAX.json). Named existing tests in [VersionGateTests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs): `Compile_FocusFunction_31Mode_ThrowsXpst0003`, `Evaluate_FocusFunction_SpecExamples`, `Evaluate_FocusFunction_BindsArgumentAsWholeContextValue`, `Evaluate_FocusFunction_AfterMappingArrow`, `Evaluate_FocusFunction_WrongArityThrows`, `Evaluate_Pipeline_SetsFixedFocusPositionOneSizeOne`, `Evaluate_Pipeline_FocusRestoredAfterEvaluation`. **No feature-specific qt4 gated-set assignment is made here**; named engine tests and runnable public examples are the explicit evidence. This does not assert that upstream lacks broader tests or claim whole-set conformance. The policy amendment does not automatically close acceptance of this or other entries. ## 16. Related Features [Pipeline](pipeline-operator.md), [mapping arrow](mapping-arrow.md), [zero-argument focus constructors](focus-functions.md), [keyword arguments](keyword-arguments.md), [coverage reconciliation](../COVERAGE-RECONCILIATION.md). Record casts/coercion/updates remain the next separate D3 scope.

Input: ```xml ``` Complete [4.0 report](../examples/focus-functions/audit/import-40.xpath): ```xquery string-join(for $line in parse-xml('')/deliveries/line return concat($line/@id, '|', $line/@quantity ! xs:integer(), '|', $line/@price ! xs:decimal(), '|', $line/@date ! xs:date(), '|', $line/@active ! xs:boolean()), ';') ``` Output (id, quantity, price, promised date, active flag): ```text A|12|2.5|2026-10-12|true;B|5|4|2026-10-13|false ``` The [3.1 report](../examples/focus-functions/audit/import-31.xpath) uses explicit `(.)` constructor arguments and produces identical output. Performance Notes Expected class: per-item conversion. Invalid values still require error classification rather than a successful result. These are implementation expectations, not measured deltas. No benchmark is claimed; use the repository benchmark harness before making workload-specific speed or memory claims. ## 15. Known Uses Executable example IDs: `focus-functions-main`, `focus-functions-edge`, `focus-functions-before` in `CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome`. Existing unit evidence: [primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Language Alignment Read the behavior as XPath/XSLT semantics. Similar vocabulary in another programming language is not a compatibility promise. The accepted spelling is =!>. Map each item, not the whole input sequence; =>> is rejected. Under the pinned semantics, additional arguments retain the containing focus. Released Bosak instead evaluates focus-sensitive extra arguments under mapped-item focus (C04 G02). Use an explicit `for $u in $seq return f($u, ...)` when those arguments depend on dot, position or size; the simple unary examples do not certify that boundary. ## 7. Applicability Use this form when solving the stated task and the consumer permits the declared compatibility level. Keep the earlier baseline when the application requires 3.1 expressions or portable 3.0 stylesheets. The accepted spelling is =!>. Map each item, not the whole input sequence; =>> is rejected. ## 8. Structure ```xquery string-join((' FILTER-A ', ' BOLT-M8 ') =!> normalize-space(), ',') ``` This is the worked case's syntax, not a replacement for the full language grammar. Required namespaces and surrounding context are supplied in the linked complete files. ## 9. Participants XPath31Expression, CompileOptions, the parser/compiler, and the shared runtime/function library provide the public execution path. [Primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) identify the feature's implementation contract. The examples use public APIs only. ## 10. Collaborations The case combines source values, the named feature, and explicit output formatting. [Worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md) show how selection, construction, and business rejection fit into larger transformations. ## 11. Consequences Benefit: Apply the target call to each item and return the mapped sequence. Tradeoff: the declared compatibility level and edge rules become part of the consumer contract. The accepted spelling is =!>. Map each item, not the whole input sequence; =>> is rejected. ## 12. Implementation **C04 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Expression/call/focus reconciliation](../EXPRESSION-CALL-FOCUS-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S4-focus. Pipeline whole-value/fixed-focus, focus-function implicit/explicit signatures, lexical capture/restoration and accepted mapping syntax are mapped. Mapping arrow extra arguments incorrectly see mapped-item focus rather than the containing focus. Use for $u in ... return F($u,A...) when extra arguments depend on outer dot/position/size. C03 constructor capture/type coverage remains distinct. Host/profile propagation belongs to C06. This is bounded production/profile evidence, not full grammar or AC-04 acceptance. Compile the after/edge expressions at XPathCompatibility.XPath40. The baseline uses XPath31. The example harness checks default-mode refusal for successful 4.0 cases; negative cases pin the declared error. See [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs): it executes the published files from the [case manifest](../examples/cases.json). This documentation slice changes no engine source. ## 13. Sample Code Input is synthetic and declared directly in the complete expression. The [complete expression](../examples/mapping-arrow/main.xpath) yields `FILTER-A,BOLT-M8`. The [edge case](../examples/mapping-arrow/edge.xpath) yields `0`. No external resources or application variables are required. See the [example runner](../examples/README.md) for commands and host context. ## 14. Performance Notes Expected class: per-item mapping and result retention. Callback work and produced sequence size matter more than the spelling. These are implementation expectations, not measured deltas. No benchmark is claimed; use the repository benchmark harness before making workload-specific speed or memory claims. ## 15. Known Uses Executable example IDs: `mapping-arrow-main`, `mapping-arrow-edge`, `mapping-arrow-before` in `CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome`. Existing unit evidence: [primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Chapter-level evidence does not promote a qt4tests set into GatedSets; conformance status remains owned by the harness and delivery records. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Compile_MappingArrow_31Mode_ThrowsXpst0003`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_MappingArrow_AppliesFunctionPerItem`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_MappingArrow_WithArgumentsPrependsContextItem`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). No feature-specific qt4 set assignment recorded here; unit evidence is listed explicitly. This is not a claim of absent upstream tests. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features See the [catalog index](../README.md), [worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md), and the alternatives in section 4. The case may be used independently of the larger chapters. *Created 2026-10-11: verified practical catalog example and earlier-version baseline.*

operators-and-syntax/method-call-operato.text:
Method-Call Operator =?>

Catalog entry — Operators & syntax · Deferred

**C11 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-3.md) records 2 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Verified deferred decision and alternative**. No method dictionary or nominal/union dispatch implementation or future tier commitment follows. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. **C07 lifecycle review — 26 October 2026:** [Current disposition and correction receipts](../LIFECYCLE-RECONCILIATION.md) distinguish delivered scope, retained history and pending acceptance. Six closure workpackages remain; no feature or profile promotion. ## 1. Name and Classification **Method-call operator `=?>`** — **Deferred** (deliberately not implemented). Spec: XPath 4.0 §4.22.3 (operator summary), [QT4CG issue #2219](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/issues/2219). Deferral recorded: REQ-118 dossier §1.2 "Still moving — do NOT build yet" (semantics changed 25 June 2026). **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [XPath 4.0: methods and method calls](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-methods). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #77](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/77), [immutable mainline revision `27bc663b`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/27bc663b71b948318f69ee1f23173ac63046a525) (2026-10-08). This is the adoption/disposition dossier delivery, not implementation of the refused shape. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Object-style method invocation on a value: the right-hand name is resolved against a method dictionary for the *type* of the left-hand value, so `$value =?> method(args)` dispatches to the method registered for that type rather than a plain in-scope function. ## 3. Also Known As "Method lookup operator". (No renames on record — the issue is semantic churn, not naming.) ## 4. History / Supersedes None — new capability; there is no 3.x idiom it replaces. The nearest 3.1/4.0 workaround it would relieve: | Before | After (if landed) | |---|---| | `map:get($m, "key")`, `array:get($a, 1)` — per-type function names a user must know | `$m =?> get("key")` — one call syntax, type-driven dispatch | ## 5. Motivation Type-directed dispatch would let maps, arrays, and future extensible types share call syntax, easing the "which module owns this operation?" burden. It is also the gateway shape for any future extensible-type story. ## 6. Language Alignment Prior art: Smalltalk/Objective-C message send, C# extension-method invocation syntax, Kotlin receiver types. Drift watch: XPath would dispatch on the **XDM type + registered method dictionary**, not on object identity or inheritance — and the *exact* resolution rules (what happens for unions, for `item()`, for user-defined types) are the part the WG changed in June 2026. ## 7. Applicability Not applicable — Bosak does not implement this operator. This entry exists so the deferral is a recorded decision rather than an absence. ## 8. Structure Not recorded — the grammar shape is among the things the draft may still adjust. Re-derive from the current WG Review Draft before any implementation attempt. ## 9. Participants None in Bosak. Implementation seam when the time comes: parser operator table, `ApplyBinaryOperator` dispatch in `VmEngine`, and interaction with the type-matching machinery used by `instance of` / `typeswitch`. ## 10. Collaborations Any future design would interact with delivered choice types, existing function lookup and bounded XSLT-defined nominative records. Their delivery does not implement method dispatch; full nominal declaration/model contracts remain separately limited. ## 11. Consequences Deferral leaves the operator unavailable. Consumers can use the supplied direct `map:*`/`array:*` alternatives; refusal and alternative checks remain necessary. Their passing results do not implement method dispatch or certify every possible replacement. ## 12. Implementation No implementation is adopted. The C07 probes verify `XPST0003` in XPath30, XPath31, XPath40 and XPath40Experimental. Any future implementation or tier decision requires a separately scoped review; this disposition makes no promotion commitment. ## 13. Sample Code No method-call syntax is committed. Do not cargo-cult `$x =?> f()` from draft-era blog posts. Use a verified stable alternative for a packing-plan array: [main.xpath](../examples/method-call-alternative/main.xpath) evaluates `array:size(['FILTER-A', 'BOLT-M8'])` to `2`; the [empty-array case](../examples/method-call-alternative/edge.xpath) returns `0`. Both run at `XPath31` and claim no support for `=?>`. ## 14. Performance Notes Not applicable (not implemented). Design note for the future: type-dictionary dispatch would add a per-call dictionary probe on the hot path — measure against the direct-function-call baseline in `benchmarks/Bosak.Benchmarks` before promoting out of experimental. ## 15. Known Uses No implementation evidence for the deferred operator is claimed. Published stable alternatives are `method-call-alternative-main` and `method-call-alternative-edge` in `CatalogExampleTests`. These checks do not promote or implement method-call syntax. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Compile_MappingArrow_31Mode_ThrowsXpst0003`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_MappingArrow_AppliesFunctionPerItem`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_MappingArrow_WithArgumentsPrependsContextItem`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Decision record, not an engine delivery or a qt4 set promotion. Tests below pin the supported/refused alternatives. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features - [mapping-arrow-gtgt.md](../rejected/mapping-arrow-gtgt.md) — the `=`-family rename history (`=>>` → `=!>`); if `=?>` ever ships, its name is the one stable thing about it so far. - `fn:scan` ([experimental/fn-scan.md](../experimental/fn-scan.md)) — an example of a separately adopted Experimental feature. Its adoption does not supersede the recorded method-call deferral or determine a future implementation tier. *Entry created 2026-10-10 (REQ-126 scaffold). Re-validate against the WG Review Draft before implementing.*
