operators-and-syntax/numeric-literals.md.text:
Numeric literals and digit separators

Frozen XPath 4.0 - bounded executable reference

**C11 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-3.md) records 4 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Verified bounded literal grammar**. Delivered malformed-separator fix remains closed; literals do not create arbitrary-precision decimal arithmetic or unrestricted generic casts. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. **Public1.23.7 - 23 October2026:** EQName bracket parsing, inline-record signature gates and numeric separator boundaries are [published and verified](../../RELEASE-1.23.7-PUBLICATION.md). Current catalog74 entries/2,893 documentation checks; REQ-126/AC-03 remain partial. Braid dependency1.23.4 unchanged. Earlier source/unpublished checkpoints below are historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Hexadecimal/binary integer literals and underscore separators** - **Frozen 4.0**, REQ-118 S3. Lowercase `0x` and `0b` introduce integer literals. Separators are permitted inside decimal, hexadecimal and binary digit groups, including the fraction and exponent groups of decimal/double literals. Ordinary XPath 3.0/3.1 syntax remains available; these extensions require 4.0. Current comparison: [immutable grammar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/b4723ff52fd9d4fabf2b4cd33bd44f21939c512c/specifications/grammar-40/xpath-grammar.xml), productions NumericLiteral, HexIntegerLiteral, BinaryIntegerLiteral, DecimalLiteral, DoubleLiteral, Digits, HexDigits and BinaryDigits. Upstream master was refreshed on 23 October 2026 at this revision. It is a current comparison pin, not a recovered historical adoption pin. [Delivery audit](../NUMERIC-LITERALS.md) separates the existing syntax from the source1.23.7 boundary correction; public release remains1.23.4. ## 2. Intent Make a bit mask or a large threshold readable in source code while retaining the numeric value and ordinary arithmetic semantics. ## 3. Also Known As Based integer literals; digit separators. `0xFF` is an integer, not an xs:hexBinary byte value. Binary literals are numbers, not xs:base64Binary values. Uppercase hex digits are accepted; uppercase prefixes `0X` and `0B` are refused. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1 use decimal `255` instead of `0xFF`, `4` instead of `0b0100`, and `1000` instead of `1_000`. The paired [3.0 stylesheet](../examples/numeric-literals/report-3.xsl) and [4.0 stylesheet](../examples/numeric-literals/report-4.xsl) keep the same telemetry report algorithm; only the constants change. Literals do not introduce a new runtime numeric type or relax input casting. ## 5. Motivation A telemetry feed stores flags and counts as decimal attributes. A report selects readings with bit 4 set and count at least 1000. The mask is easier to inspect in binary and the threshold easier to read with grouping. The [complete task](../examples/numeric-literals/README.md) includes normal, empty, reordered and invalid inputs and exact output. ## 6. Language Alignment The prefixes resemble C-family source literals; the exact XPath grammar governs the boundaries. Repeated internal underscores such as `1__000` and `0xFF__FF` are valid under the pinned draft. Each nonempty digit group starts and ends in a digit: `1._2`, `1.2_` and `1e_2` are invalid. A sign is a unary operator, not part of the integer token. Source separators do not extend the XML Schema lexical forms accepted by xs:integer: `xs:integer('1_000')` and `xs:integer('0xFF')` still fail FORG0001. ## 7. Applicability Use these constants in authored XPath/XSLT 4.0 expressions. Keep external decimal attributes in their declared lexical format, and select a 3.0/3.1-compatible spelling when generating an older stylesheet. This entry verifies ordinary Legacy-host effective3.0/4.0 stylesheets, not every package, XQuery or host override context. ## 8. Structure ```xpath 0xFF + 0b1_000 + 1_000 ``` The sum is1263. `1_2.3__4` is decimal12.34; `1_2.5e+0_2` is double1250. A decimal point may have no following digits (`1_2.`), and a decimal may omit its integer part (`.1_2`). If a fraction/exponent group is present, its separators cannot be at an edge. ## 9. Participants [XPathLexer](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Parser/Lexer/XPathLexer.cs) scans version-sensitive numeric tokens. [XPathParser](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Parser/Ast/XPathParser.cs) removes separators and computes based integer values. The public XPath31Expression/CompileOptions surface selects the compatibility level. No new public API is added. ## 10. Collaborations In the report the binary constant and hexadecimal zero form the mask; idiv/mod test the flag arithmetically. A separated threshold filters counts. xsl:for-each preserves input order, and sum builds the total from parsed decimal attribute values. The literals do not implement bitwise operators or alter data conversion. ## 11. Consequences The supplied checks cover integer/decimal/double identity, a value above Int64 range, negative unary application, numeric map/array lookup keys, valid internal repeated separators, malformed groups, wrong radix digits and version refusals. Bosak uses bounded .NET numeric representations; one above-Int64 example does not certify arbitrary-precision integer/decimal support. Other numeric adjacency, Unicode digit and overflow behavior is outside this bounded correction. No performance improvement is claimed. ## 12. Separators are permitted inside decimal, hexadecimal and binary digit groups, including the fraction and exponent groups of decimal/double literals. Ordinary XPath 3.0/3.1 syntax remains available; these extensions require 4.0.

sections.2: Make a bit mask or a large threshold readable in source code while retaining the numeric value and ordinary arithmetic semantics.
sections.3: Based integer literals; digit separators. `0xFF` is an integer, not an xs:hexBinary byte value. Binary literals are numbers, not xs:base64Binary values. Uppercase hex digits are accepted; uppercase prefixes `0X` and `0B` are refused.
sections.4: In 3.1 use decimal `255` instead of `0xFF`, `4` instead of `0b0100`, and `1000` instead of `1_000`. The paired [3.0 stylesheet](../examples/numeric-literals/report-3.xsl) and [4.0 stylesheet](../examples/numeric-literals/report-4.xsl) keep the same telemetry report algorithm; only the constants change. Literals do not introduce a new runtime numeric type or relax input casting.
sections.5: A telemetry feed stores flags and counts as decimal attributes. A report selects readings with bit 4 set and count at least 1000. The mask is easier to inspect in binary and the threshold easier to read with grouping. The [complete task](../examples/numeric-literals/README.md) includes normal, empty, reordered and invalid inputs and exact output.
sections.6: The prefixes resemble C-family source literals; the exact XPath grammar governs the boundaries. Repeated internal underscores such as `1__000` and `0xFF__FF` are valid under the pinned draft. Each nonempty digit group starts and ends in a digit: `1._2`, `1.2_` and `1e_2` are invalid. A sign is a unary operator, not part of the integer token. Source separators do not extend the XML Schema lexical forms accepted by xs:integer: `xs:integer('1_000')` and `xs:integer('0xFF')` still fail FORG0001.
sections.7: Use these constants in authored XPath/XSLT 4.0 expressions. Keep external decimal attributes in their declared lexical format, and select a 3.0/3.1-compatible spelling when generating an older stylesheet. This entry verifies ordinary Legacy-host effective3.0/4.0 stylesheets, not every package, XQuery or host override context.
sections.8:
```xpath
0xFF + 0b1_000 + 1_000
```

The sum is1263. `1_2.3__4` is decimal12.34; `1_2.5e+0_2` is double1250. A decimal point may have no following digits (`1_2.`), and a decimal may omit its integer part (`.1_2`). If a fraction/exponent group is present, its separators cannot be at an edge.

The public XPath31Expression/CompileOptions surface selects the compatibility level. No new public API is added.
sections.10: In the report the binary constant and hexadecimal zero form the mask; idiv/mod test the flag arithmetically. A separated threshold filters counts. xsl:for-each preserves input order, and sum builds the total from parsed decimal attribute values. The literals do not implement bitwise operators or alter data conversion.

Otherwise operator

Practical reference: Frozen 4.0

**C11 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-3.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited released spelling; current grammar mismatch**. C04-G01: retain frozen spelling and historical adoption uncertainty separately from the current review; no automatic rename/adoption. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Otherwise operator** - **Frozen 4.0**. Delivery family: [REQ-118](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) / [REQ-123 registry](../../FEATURE_REQUESTS.md). Section provenance: See the linked REQ dossiers and implementation evidence. [Primary implementation evidence](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) records the shipped behavior; this entry adds executable user-facing examples under REQ-126, rather than announcing a new engine feature. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [XPath 4.0: otherwise expressions](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-otherwise), [guarded expressions](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-guarded-expressions). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #85](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/85), [immutable mainline revision `5ca72268`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/5ca722686041fc701f8c25c00808eb8169a63053) (2026-10-08). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Select the fallback for empty-sequence input. ## 3. Also Known As Use the name and spelling in this entry and its executable files. Related functions or instruction forms are described in the primary test evidence; no additional alias is adopted here. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1, use if (exists($value)) then $value else $fallback. Compare the [complete earlier-version baseline](../examples/otherwise-operator/before.xpath) with the [complete expression](../examples/otherwise-operator/main.xpath). Both yield `No purchase order` for this synthetic input. They demonstrate this task, not universal equivalence of the two mechanisms. ## 5. Motivation An invoice label needs a fallback when an optional reference is absent. Select the fallback for empty-sequence input. Keeping this task explicit makes it possible to choose the feature for a practical reason and verify what the receiving application will see. ## 6. Language Alignment Read the behavior as XPath/XSLT semantics. Similar vocabulary in another programming language is not a compatibility promise. Empty string, false, and zero are present values. This operator is not JavaScript truthiness or a universal null conversion. ## 7. Applicability Use this form when solving the stated task and the consumer permits the declared compatibility level. Keep the earlier baseline when the application requires 3.1 expressions or portable 3.0 stylesheets. Empty string, false, and zero are present values. This operator is not JavaScript truthiness or a universal null conversion. ## 8. Structure ```xquery () ?? 'No purchase order' ``` This is the worked case's syntax, not a replacement for the full language grammar. Required namespaces and surrounding context are supplied in the linked complete files. ## 9. Participants XPath31Expression, CompileOptions, the parser/compiler, and the shared runtime/function library provide the public execution path. [Primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) identify the feature's implementation contract. The examples use public APIs only. ## 10. Collaborations The case combines source values, the named feature, and explicit output formatting. [Worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md) show how selection, construction, and business rejection fit into larger transformations. ## 11. Consequences Benefit: Select the fallback for empty-sequence input. Tradeoff: the declared compatibility level and edge rules become part of the consumer contract. Empty string, false, and zero are present values. This operator is not JavaScript truthiness or a universal null conversion. ## 12. Implementation **C04 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Expression/call/focus reconciliation](../EXPRESSION-CALL-FOCUS-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S3-otherwise. Released ?? preserves empty-versus-present, whole-sequence value, precedence, containing focus and guarded dynamic-error controls. Current draft spells the operator otherwise and is not accepted by either 4.0 profile. Do not advertise ?? as the pinned normative spelling. Closed-host static binding needs its own review; the public API accepts runtime variable/function context. This is bounded production/profile evidence, not full grammar or AC-04 acceptance. Compile the after/edge expressions at XPathCompatibility.XPath40. The baseline uses XPath31. The example harness checks default-mode refusal for successful 4.0 cases; negative cases pin the declared error. See [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs): it executes the published files from the [case manifest](../examples/cases.json). This documentation slice changes no engine source. ## 13. Sample Code Input is synthetic and declared directly in the complete expression. The [complete expression](../examples/otherwise-operator/main.xpath) yields `No purchase order`. The [edge case](../examples/otherwise-operator/edge.xpath) yields `0`. No external resources or application variables are required. See the [example runner](../examples/README.md) for commands and host context. ## 14. Performance Notes Expected class: a branch and empty-sequence observation. The fallback expression contributes cost only when selected. These are implementation expectations, not measured deltas. No benchmark is claimed; use the repository benchmark harness before making workload-specific speed or memory claims. ## 15. Known Uses Executable example IDs: `otherwise-operator-main`, `otherwise-operator-edge`, `otherwise-operator-before` in `CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome`. Existing unit evidence: [primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Chapter-level evidence does not promote a qt4tests set into GatedSets; conformance status remains owned by the harness and delivery records. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Compile_Otherwise_Default31Mode_ThrowsXpst0003`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Compile_Otherwise_XPath30Mode_ThrowsXpst0003`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_Otherwise_EmptyLeftYieldsRight`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). No feature-specific qt4 set assignment recorded here; unit evidence is listed explicitly. This is not a claim of absent upstream tests. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features See the [catalog index](../README.md), [worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md), and the alternatives in section 4. The case may be used independently of the larger chapters. *Created 2026-10-11: verified practical catalog example and earlier-version baseline.*

operators-and-syntax/sequence-collection.text:
Iteration across collection sequences

Frozen 4.0

**C11 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-3.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Verified bounded multi-container iteration**. Not a full generic collection/type-model promotion. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Iteration across collection sequences — Frozen 4.0.** [Bosak PR #87](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/87) / [immutable revision `ec793559`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/ec79355936a29ac70eeea3ae47e4c4e2ee00d813). This is the shipped engine delivery. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [XPath collection iteration](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-for-expressions). Historical adopted specification source revision was not retained; this remains an explicit provenance gap. ## 2. Intent Process parcels or inventory updates spread across several arrays or maps. ## 3. Also Known As Use the exact spellings in the linked examples; no undocumented aliases are adopted. ## 4. History / Supersedes The initial REQ-118 stability table deferred sequences of arrays/maps, but S4 shipped this extension. for member binds complete array members, including multi-item sequences; for key/value binds map entries. Positional counting continues across the outer collection sequence. Non-array/non-map input is XPTY0141. Map entry ordering is not an application sorting contract. ## 5. Motivation Process parcels or inventory updates spread across several arrays or maps. The order-routing chapter places validation before dispatch so rejected records stay available for repair. ## 6. Language Alignment Nested loops that flatten array members can destroy a parcel boundary. Map entry order should not be treated as stable business order; explicitly sort when presentation order matters. ## 7. Applicability Use within the declared compatibility and business contract. Deferred/rejected contracts require explicit alternatives; they must not be advertised as implemented. ## 8. Structure ```xquery string-join(for member $parcel in ([('FILTER-A','BOLT-M8')], ['MANUAL']) return string(count($parcel)), ',') ``` This complete expression demonstrates the stated contract, not the full grammar. ## 9. Participants The public XPath API compiles at the manifest mode and evaluates without application variables. The routing chapter additionally supplies an XML document context. ## 10. Collaborations The routing planner passes an XDM map to portable XSLT through a required parameter. See [the full chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md). ## 11. Consequences The initial REQ-118 stability table deferred sequences of arrays/maps, but S4 shipped this extension. for member binds complete array members, including multi-item sequences; for key/value binds map entries. Positional counting continues across the outer collection sequence. Non-array/non-map input is XPTY0141. Map entry ordering is not an application sorting contract. Nested loops that flatten array members can destroy a parcel boundary. Map entry order should not be treated as stable business order; explicitly sort when presentation order matters. ## 12. Implementation **C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S4-iteration. Members and map-entry values remain whole sequences, positions continue across container sequences, empty collections bind nothing, and invalid container items refuse XPTY0141. Container iteration preserves containing focus. Do not flatten member boundaries or infer portable map entry order. Complete typed iteration combinations and host bindings remain outside bounded controls. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows. The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) runs the exact files, asserts declared results/errors, and checks default-3.1 refusal for successful 4.0 forms. No engine code changes or conformance promotions are included. ## 13. Sample Code [arrays.xpath](../examples/sequence-collection-iteration/arrays.xpath): returns `2,1` at mode 40. [maps.xpath](../examples/sequence-collection-iteration/maps.xpath): returns `BOLT-M8=5,FILTER-A=2` at mode 40. [invalid.xpath](../examples/sequence-collection-iteration/invalid.xpath): raises `XPTY0141` at mode 40. ## 14. Performance Notes Predicates and duplicate checks scan their inputs; partitioning allocates arrays and retains accepted nodes. These are qualitative expectations, not benchmark results. Stateful or expensive callbacks change workload costs. ## 15. Known Uses Executable IDs: `sequence-collection-iteration-arrays`, `sequence-collection-iteration-maps`, `sequence-collection-iteration-invalid`. [`Evaluate_ForMember_SequenceOfArraysCountsPositionsAcrossArrays`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_ForKeyValue_PositionalCountsAcrossMaps`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). No additional gate promotion is claimed by this decision record. [Gate runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs). ## 16. Related Features [Catalog index](../README.md), [routing chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md), [structural records](../type-system/structural-records.md), [experimental scan](../experimental/fn-scan.md).

rejected/directional-scan.md.text:
Directional scan names

Rejected / superseded

**C11 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-3.md) records 2 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Verified rejected names**. No right-scan equivalence is inferred from reversing sequences. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Directional scan names — Rejected / superseded.** [Bosak PR #77](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/77) / [immutable revision `27bc663b`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/27bc663b71b948318f69ee1f23173ac63046a525). This is a disposition dossier, not implementation of the refused/deferred shape. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [fn:scan](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-scan), [QT4CG proposal history](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/pull/2824). Historical adopted specification source revision was not retained; this remains an explicit provenance gap. ## 2. Intent Explain why running stock balances use the experimental scan contract. ## 3. Also Known As Use the exact spellings in the linked examples; no undocumented aliases are adopted. ## 4. History / Supersedes The recorded scan-left/scan-right proposals consolidated into fn:scan, a left-fold scan. Bosak fn:scan remains experimental even though its conformance set is promoted. Do not promise a right-fold alias: reversing input and reversing results is not generally equivalent for noncommutative operations. The adopted scan returns array-wrapped states; consult its entry for that contract. ## 5. Motivation Explain why running stock balances use the experimental scan contract. The order-routing chapter places validation before dispatch so rejected records stay available for repair. ## 6. Language Alignment A fold returning only the final state and a scan returning intermediate states have different results. Direction matters for subtraction and string construction. ## 7. Applicability Use within the declared compatibility and business contract. Deferred/rejected contracts require explicit alternatives; they must not be advertised as implemented. ## 8. Structure ```xquery fn:scan-left((1,2), 0, function($a,$b){$a+$b}) ``` This complete expression demonstrates the stated contract, not the full grammar. ## 9. Participants The public XPath API compiles at the manifest mode and evaluates without application variables. The routing chapter additionally supplies an XML document context. ## 10. Collaborations The routing planner passes an XDM map to portable XSLT through a required parameter. See [the full chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md). ## 11. Consequences The recorded scan-left/scan-right proposals consolidated into fn:scan, a left-fold scan. Bosak fn:scan remains experimental even though its conformance set is promoted. Do not promise a right-fold alias: reversing input and reversing results is not generally equivalent for noncommutative operations. The adopted scan returns array-wrapped states; consult its entry for that contract. A fold returning only the final state and a scan returning intermediate states have different results. Direction matters for subtraction and string construction. ## 12. Implementation The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) runs the exact files, asserts declared results/errors, and checks default-3.1 refusal for successful 4.0 forms. No engine code changes or conformance promotions are included. ## 13. Sample Code [left.xpath](../examples/directional-scan/left.xpath): raises `XPST0017` at mode experimental. [right.xpath](../examples/directional-scan/right.xpath): raises `XPST0017` at mode experimental. ## 14. Performance Notes Predicates and duplicate checks scan their inputs; partitioning allocates arrays and retains accepted nodes. These are qualitative expectations, not benchmark results. Stateful or expensive callbacks change workload costs. ## 15. Known Uses Executable IDs: `directional-scan-left`, `directional-scan-right`. No additional gate promotion is claimed by this decision record. [Gate runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs). ## 16. Related Features [Catalog index](../README.md), [routing chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md), [structural records](../type-system/structural-records.md), [experimental scan](../experimental/fn-scan.md).

rejected/extensible-map-types.md.text:
Extensible map type proposal

Rejected proposal; record alternatives shipped

**C11 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-3.md) records 2 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Verified rejected proposal and record alternatives**. Keep structural membership, cast, coercion and annotation-aware lookup separate; C05 defects remain. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Extensible map type proposal — Rejected proposal; record alternatives shipped.** [Bosak PR #77](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/77) / [immutable revision `27bc663b`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/27bc663b71b948318f69ee1f23173ac63046a525). This is a disposition dossier, not implementation of the refused/deferred shape. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [XPath structural records](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-structural-record-types), [XPath record casts](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#casting-to-record). Historical adopted specification source revision was not retained; this remains an explicit provenance gap. ## 2. Intent Make surplus-field policy explicit when importing an order record. ## 3. Also Known As Use the exact spellings in the linked examples; no undocumented aliases are adopted. ## 4. History / Supersedes The dossier rejects the historical extensible-map-type proposal. This does not reject map(*) or typed maps. Shipped structural records provide field contracts, but record casts and coercion differ: casts discard surplus keys; coercion rejects them with XPTY0004. The dossier shorthand saying coercion discards entries is inaccurate for the delivered annotation model. ## 5. Motivation Make surplus-field policy explicit when importing an order record. The order-routing chapter places validation before dispatch so rejected records stay available for repair. ## 6. Language Alignment An open map and a closed record are not interchangeable. Silent removal of unknown fields is a cast policy, not the normal function-argument coercion policy. ## 7. Applicability Use within the declared compatibility and business contract. Deferred/rejected contracts require explicit alternatives; they must not be advertised as implemented. ## 8. Structure ```xquery map:size(map {'id':'R1','extra':'ignored'} cast as record(id as xs:string)) ``` This complete expression demonstrates the stated contract, not the full grammar. ## 9. Participants The public XPath API compiles at the manifest mode and evaluates without application variables. The routing chapter additionally supplies an XML document context. ## 10. Collaborations The routing planner passes an XDM map to portable XSLT through a required parameter. See [the full chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md). ## 11. Consequences The dossier rejects the historical extensible-map-type proposal. This does not reject map(*) or typed maps. Shipped structural records provide field contracts, but record casts and coercion differ: casts discard surplus keys; coercion rejects them with XPTY0004. The dossier shorthand saying coercion discards entries is inaccurate for the delivered annotation model. An open map and a closed record are not interchangeable. Silent removal of unknown fields is a cast policy, not the normal function-argument coercion policy. ## 12. Implementation The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) runs the exact files, asserts declared results/errors, and checks default-3.1 refusal for successful 4.0 forms. No engine code changes or conformance promotions are included. ## 13. Sample Code [cast.xpath](../examples/extensible-map-types/cast.xpath): returns `1` at mode 40. [coercion.xpath](../examples/extensible-map-types/coercion.xpath): raises `XPTY0004` at mode 40. ## 14. Performance Notes Predicates and duplicate checks scan their inputs; partitioning allocates arrays and retains accepted nodes. These are qualitative expectations, not benchmark results. Stateful or expensive callbacks change workload costs. ## 15. Known Uses Executable IDs: `extensible-map-types-cast`, `extensible-map-types-coercion`. [`Cast_DiscardsSurplusKeys`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/RecordTypeTests.cs), [`Coercion_SurplusKeys_XPTY0004`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/RecordTypeTests.cs). No additional gate promotion is claimed by this decision record. [Gate runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs). ## 16. rejected/mapping-arrow-gtgt.md.text:
Mapping Arrow =>> (Original Spelling)

Catalog entry — Rejected / Superseded

**C11 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-3.md) records 3 contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Verified rejected spelling and bounded replacement**. This proves Bosak refusal/replacement scope, not an exact external rename/adoption history or corrected mapping-extra focus. Review completion is not final owner acceptance; earlier checkpoints remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Mapping arrow, original spelling `=>>`** — **Rejected–Superseded**. Bosak never shipped this spelling; the engine implemented the renamed form directly. Disposition recorded: REQ-118 dossier §1.2 "Deliberately rejected / renamed (do not implement old shapes)". **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [XPath 4.0: accepted mapping-arrow syntax](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-mapping-arrow-expression). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #77](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/77), [immutable mainline revision `27bc663b`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/27bc663b71b948318f69ee1f23173ac63046a525) (2026-10-08). This is the adoption/disposition dossier delivery, not implementation of the refused shape. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent (Of the accepted feature this spelling belonged to.) Apply the function once per item, passing that item as its first argument: `$seq =!> f()` corresponds to `for $x in $seq return f($x)`. The ordinary arrow `$seq => f()` passes the whole sequence as one argument. The simple map operator `!` instead establishes each item as the context for its right-hand expression; argument passing and context binding are distinct mechanisms. ## 3. Also Known As `=!>` — the accepted name (mapping arrow). Formerly spelled `=>>` in earlier drafts; renamed during draft stabilization. qt4tests pin the accepted spelling. ## 4. History / Supersedes The rejected spelling and its replacement are recorded in the REQ-118 audit; Bosak implements the accepted form in its S4 grammar slice. A 3.1 baseline uses `for $x in $seq return f($x)`. See the [accepted mapping-arrow entry](../operators-and-syntax/mapping-arrow.md) for the verified migration pair. The current specification link documents the accepted syntax; an exact historical rename revision remains part of the provenance work. ## 5. Motivation Recorded for completeness: the superseded spelling exists in draft-era examples, conference slides, and early blog posts. A user pasting such material gets a parse error and deserves a searchable answer. ## 6. Language Alignment The accepted operator performs per-item function application, comparable in purpose to mapping a collection. XPath passes each item as the first function argument; it does not establish that item as the right-hand expression's context in the way `!` does. The historical reason for choosing the replacement spelling needs its own source; no visual resemblance to other operators establishes it. ## 7. Applicability **Do not use.** `=>>` raises XPST0003 at every Bosak compatibility level, including frozen `XPath40`. Use `=!>`. ## 8. Structure Not applicable — the spelling is not in the grammar. Accepted form: `Expr "=!>" ArrowFunction`. ## 9. Participants None. The parser's operator table has no `=>>` token; drafts-era sources parse-fail positionally at the `>`. ## 10. Collaborations None. ## 11. Consequences Of the rejection: zero engine surface for the old spelling, one parse-error class for pasted old material, and no version-gate complexity (there is no "compat level that accepts `=>>`"). ## 12. Implementation None, deliberately. If a parser change ever accidentally accepts `=>>`, that is a defect against this entry. ## 13. Sample Code Run these as independent queries. The first uses frozen `XPath40`; the second deliberately refuses the old spelling: ~~~xquery string-join((' FILTER-A ', ' BOLT-M8 ') =!> normalize-space(), ',') (: → "FILTER-A,BOLT-M8" — one call per product code :) ~~~ ~~~xquery (' FILTER-A ') =>> normalize-space() (: → XPST0003 at every level — old spelling, never implemented :) ~~~ ## 14. Performance Notes Not applicable. ## 15. Known Uses `rejected-mapping-arrow-main` and `rejected-mapping-arrow-edge` in `CatalogExampleTests` verify an accepted product-code normalization and rejection of the old spelling. See [the accepted mapping-arrow case](../operators-and-syntax/mapping-arrow.md) and [complete rejection file](../examples/rejected-mapping-arrow/edge.xpath). qt4tests pin only the accepted `=!>` spelling (part of the frozen gate's grammar slices). No test uses `=>>`. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Compile_MappingArrow_31Mode_ThrowsXpst0003`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_MappingArrow_AppliesFunctionPerItem`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_MappingArrow_WithArgumentsPrependsContextItem`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Decision record, not an engine delivery or a qt4 set promotion. Tests below pin the supported/refused alternatives. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features - [Pipeline operator](../operators-and-syntax/pipeline-operator.md) — whole-value function application, distinct from per-item mapping. - [method-call-operator.md](../operators-and-syntax/method-call-operator.md) — the third `=?>` member of the family, deferred for semantic (not naming) churn. - [fn-scan.md](../experimental/fn-scan.md) — the "consolidated before stabilization" sibling class (`scan-left`/`scan-right` → `fn:scan`); the same rule applies: old shapes do not parse. *Entry created 2026-10-10 (REQ-126 scaffold).*

string-join((' FILTER-A ', ' BOLT-M8 ') =!> normalize-space(), ',')

~~~

  (: → XPST0003 at every level — old spelling, never implemented :)
~~~

rejected/obsolete-quantifier-functions.m.text:
Never-adopted quantifier names

Rejected

**C12 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-4.md) records three contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Verified rejected names and quantified alternative**. No cross-language alias or universal duplicate/partition contract is adopted. Final owner acceptance remains C13; earlier checkpoints are historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Never-adopted quantifier names — Rejected.** [Bosak PR #77](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/77) / [immutable revision `27bc663b`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/27bc663b71b948318f69ee1f23173ac63046a525). This is a disposition dossier, not implementation of the refused/deferred shape. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [fn:all-equal](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-all-equal), [fn:some](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-some), [fn:every](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xpath-functions-40/Overview.html#func-every). Historical adopted specification source revision was not retained; this remains an explicit provenance gap. ## 2. Intent Prevent guessed function names from becoming accidental compatibility promises. ## 3. Also Known As Use the exact spellings in the linked examples; no undocumented aliases are adopted. ## 4. History / Supersedes REQ-118 records fn:all and fn:some-of as names that never existed in the adopted surface. Use all-equal/all-different for sequence equality and some/every for boolean predicates. These are different contracts; there is no universal mechanical rename from fn:all. ## 5. Motivation Prevent guessed function names from becoming accidental compatibility promises. The order-routing chapter places validation before dispatch so rejected records stay available for repair. ## 6. Language Alignment Names borrowed from other languages are not XPath aliases. Equality of all values differs from every value satisfying a predicate. ## 7. Applicability Use within the declared compatibility and business contract. Deferred/rejected contracts require explicit alternatives; they must not be advertised as implemented. ## 8. Structure ```xquery fn:all((1,1)) ``` This complete expression demonstrates the stated contract, not the full grammar. ## 9. Participants The public XPath API compiles at the manifest mode and evaluates without application variables. The routing chapter additionally supplies an XML document context. ## 10. Collaborations The routing planner passes an XDM map to portable XSLT through a required parameter. See [the full chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md). ## 11. Consequences REQ-118 records fn:all and fn:some-of as names that never existed in the adopted surface. Use all-equal/all-different for sequence equality and some/every for boolean predicates. These are different contracts; there is no universal mechanical rename from fn:all. Names borrowed from other languages are not XPath aliases. Equality of all values differs from every value satisfying a predicate. ## 12. Implementation The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) runs the exact files, asserts declared results/errors, and checks default-3.1 refusal for successful 4.0 forms. No engine code changes or conformance promotions are included. ## 13. Sample Code [all.xpath](../examples/obsolete-quantifier-functions/all.xpath): raises `XPST0017` at mode 40. [some-of.xpath](../examples/obsolete-quantifier-functions/some-of.xpath): raises `XPST0017` at mode 40. [alternative.xpath](../examples/obsolete-quantifier-functions/alternative.xpath): returns `true` at mode 40. ## 14. Performance Notes Predicates and duplicate checks scan their inputs; partitioning allocates arrays and retains accepted nodes. These are qualitative expectations, not benchmark results. Stateful or expensive callbacks change workload costs. ## 15. Known Uses Executable IDs: `obsolete-quantifier-functions-all`, `obsolete-quantifier-functions-some-of`, `obsolete-quantifier-functions-alternative`. No additional gate promotion is claimed by this decision record. [Gate runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs). ## 16. Related Features [Catalog index](../README.md), [routing chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md), [structural records](../type-system/structural-records.md), [experimental scan](../experimental/fn-scan.md).

rejected/xpath-switch-expression.md.text:
XPath switch expression

Rejected in XPath

**C12 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-4.md) records three contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Verified XPath refusal and conditional alternative**. Host grammar acceptance does not transfer to standalone XPath; XQuery4 remains outside this contract. Final owner acceptance remains C13; earlier checkpoints are historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **XPath switch expression — Rejected in XPath.** [Bosak PR #77](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/77) / [immutable revision `27bc663b`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/27bc663b71b948318f69ee1f23173ac63046a525). This is a disposition dossier, not implementation of the refused/deferred shape. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [XPath conditional expressions](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-conditionals), [XSLT switch instruction](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xslt-40/Overview.html#element-switch). Historical adopted specification source revision was not retained; this remains an explicit provenance gap. ## 2. Intent Choose a routing branch using a construct in the actual host language. ## 3. Also Known As Use the exact spellings in the linked examples; no undocumented aliases are adopted. ## 4. History / Supersedes XPath has no switch expression in the adopted grammar. Use if/then/else or map lookup for XPath dispatch. xsl:switch is an XSLT instruction; XQuery switch is a separate language construct and is not rejected by this XPath decision. ## 5. Motivation Choose a routing branch using a construct in the actual host language. The order-routing chapter places validation before dispatch so rejected records stay available for repair. ## 6. Language Alignment Language alignment is local to the host grammar. XQuery or XSLT acceptance does not make an expression legal in XPath. ## 7. Applicability Use within the declared compatibility and business contract. Deferred/rejected contracts require explicit alternatives; they must not be advertised as implemented. ## 8. Structure ```xquery switch ('NORTH') case 'NORTH' return 1 default return 0 ``` This complete expression demonstrates the stated contract, not the full grammar. ## 9. Participants The public XPath API compiles at the manifest mode and evaluates without application variables. The routing chapter additionally supplies an XML document context. ## 10. Collaborations The routing planner passes an XDM map to portable XSLT through a required parameter. See [the full chapter](../worked-examples/order-routing/README.md). ## 11. Consequences XPath has no switch expression in the adopted grammar. Use if/then/else or map lookup for XPath dispatch. xsl:switch is an XSLT instruction; XQuery switch is a separate language construct and is not rejected by this XPath decision. Language alignment is local to the host grammar. XQuery or XSLT acceptance does not make an expression legal in XPath. ## 12. Implementation The [manifest harness](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) runs the exact files, asserts declared results/errors, and checks default-3.1 refusal for successful 4.0 forms. No engine code changes or conformance promotions are included. ## 13. Sample Code [refusal.xpath](../examples/xpath-switch-expression/refusal.xpath): raises `XPST0003` at mode 40. [alternative.xpath](../examples/xpath-switch-expression/alternative.xpath): returns `dispatch` at mode 31. ## 14. Performance Notes Predicates and duplicate checks scan their inputs; partitioning allocates arrays and retains accepted nodes. These are qualitative expectations, not benchmark results. Stateful or expensive callbacks change workload costs. ## 15. Known Uses Executable IDs: `xpath-switch-expression-refusal`, `xpath-switch-expression-alternative`. No additional gate promotion is claimed by this decision record. [Gate runner](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Conformance40/ConformanceRunner40.cs). ## 16. type-system/choice-types.md.text:
Choice item types

Practical reference: Frozen 4.0

**C12 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-4.md) records three contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited membership/cast; matching-coercion blocker**. C05-K02: six fresh controls still convert an already-matching string to an earlier integer alternative; explicit-cast success does not resolve this. Final owner acceptance remains C13; earlier checkpoints are historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Choice item types** - **Frozen 4.0**. Delivery family: [REQ-118](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) / [REQ-123 registry](../../FEATURE_REQUESTS.md). Section provenance: REQ-118 S6a; choice item type evidence in VersionGateTests. [Primary implementation evidence](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) records the shipped behavior; this entry adds executable user-facing examples under REQ-126, rather than announcing a new engine feature. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [XPath 4.0: choice item types](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-choice-item-types). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #89](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/89), [immutable mainline revision `83d152ff`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/83d152ffdba55fe160f33366fa14ed2922fa2f9d) (2026-10-08). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Express the permitted alternatives in one item type. ## 3. Also Known As Use the name and spelling in this entry and its executable files. Related functions or instruction forms are described in the primary test evidence; no additional alias is adopted here. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1, combine individual instance-of tests with or. Compare the [complete earlier-version baseline](../examples/choice-types/before.xpath) with the [complete expression](../examples/choice-types/main.xpath). Both yield `true` for this synthetic input. They demonstrate this task, not universal equivalence of the two mechanisms. ## 5. Motivation A legacy order identifier can be an integer or a string, but not a fractional amount. Express the permitted alternatives in one item type. Keeping this task explicit makes it possible to choose the feature for a practical reason and verify what the receiving application will see. ## 6. Language Alignment Read the behavior as XPath/XSLT semantics. Similar vocabulary in another programming language is not a compatibility promise. Explicit cast tries alternatives in order. Coercion must preserve an already-matching alternative, but Bosak currently converts matching strings to an earlier integer alternative (C05-K02). The instance-of examples only test membership and do not perform conversion. ## 7. Applicability Use this form when solving the stated task and the consumer permits the declared compatibility level. Keep the earlier baseline when the application requires 3.1 expressions or portable 3.0 stylesheets. Explicit cast tries alternatives in order. Coercion must preserve an already-matching alternative, but Bosak currently converts matching strings to an earlier integer alternative (C05-K02). The instance-of examples only test membership and do not perform conversion. ## 8. Structure ```xquery 'PO-8801' instance of (xs:integer|xs:string) ``` This is the worked case's syntax, not a replacement for the full language grammar. Required namespaces and surrounding context are supplied in the linked complete files. ## 9. Participants XPath31Expression, CompileOptions, the parser/compiler, and the shared runtime/function library provide the public execution path. [Primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs) identify the feature's implementation contract. The examples use public APIs only. ## 10. Collaborations The case combines source values, the named feature, and explicit output formatting. [Worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md) show how selection, construction, and business rejection fit into larger transformations. ## 11. Consequences Benefit: Express the permitted alternatives in one item type. Tradeoff: the declared compatibility level and edge rules become part of the consumer contract. Explicit cast tries alternatives in order. Coercion must preserve an already-matching alternative, but Bosak currently converts matching strings to an earlier integer alternative (C05-K02). The instance-of examples only test membership and do not perform conversion. ## 12. Implementation **C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S6-types. Membership, explicit casts and coercion are separate. Cast alternatives are attempted in order; already-matching choice coercion currently converts a string to an earlier integer alternative, contrary to the current matched-alternative rule. K02 retains typed let/argument/return failures with independent expectations. Namespace/type aliases are host-defined, not standalone global registrations. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows. **C03 review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Constructor/type reconciliation](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.md) verifies Membership is distinct from coercion; Already-matching alternatives and ordered coercion of unmatched untyped values; 3.1 choice grammar refusal. **Boundary:** The tested integer/string alternatives do not certify every schema union, function/record alternative or error-precedence combination. Schema union/list context has separate named evidence. Ownership: T03, T05. Per-path controls and named schema/API/host evidence are retained in the [review matrix](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.json); no whole-type or AC-04 acceptance follows. Compile the after/edge expressions at XPathCompatibility.XPath40. The baseline uses XPath31. The example harness checks default-mode refusal for successful 4.0 cases; negative cases pin the declared error. See [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs): it executes the published files from the [case manifest](../examples/cases.json). This documentation slice changes no engine source. ## 13. Sample Code Input is synthetic and declared directly in the complete expression. The [complete expression](../examples/choice-types/main.xpath) yields `true`. The [edge case](../examples/choice-types/edge.xpath) yields `false`. No external resources or application variables are required. See the [example runner](../examples/README.md) for commands and host context. ## 14. Performance Notes Expected class: alternative type matching/coercion. The number and ordering of alternatives affect the work performed. These are implementation expectations, not measured deltas. No benchmark is claimed; use the repository benchmark harness before making workload-specific speed or memory claims. ## 15. Known Uses Executable example IDs: `choice-types-main`, `choice-types-edge`, `choice-types-before` in `CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome`. Existing unit evidence: [primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). Chapter-level evidence does not promote a qt4tests set into GatedSets; conformance status remains owned by the harness and delivery records. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Compile_ChoiceItemType_31Mode_ThrowsXpst0003`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_Choice_InstanceOf_AnyAlternativeMatches`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs), [`Evaluate_Choice_Cast_FirstCoercibleAlternativeWins`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/VersionGateTests.cs). No feature-specific qt4 set assignment recorded here; unit evidence is listed explicitly. This is not a claim of absent upstream tests. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features See the [catalog index](../README.md), [worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md), and the alternatives in section 4. The case may be used independently of the larger chapters. *Created 2026-10-11: verified practical catalog example and earlier-version baseline.*

type-system/nominative-records.md.text:
Nominative records: host-defined identity

21 October 2026

**C12 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-4.md) records three contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Verified bounded XSLT nominal identity**. Package visibility, transitive imports, complete static/default field combinations and arbitrary host registration remain bounded by C03/C05/C06. Final owner acceptance remains C13; earlier checkpoints are historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Bounded XSLT-defined identity is implemented in public1.23.2; this is not a standalone XPath declaration facility or a complete promotion of the historical deferred proposal.** [Current mapping](../TYPE-PATTERN-GRAMMAR.md). ## 2. Intent Explain why a host-declared name can matter beyond the field shape of a record. ## 3. Also Known As Named/nominal/nominative record identity in the tested XSLT declaration context. ## 4. History / Supersedes The original PR77 disposition at27bc663b and its earlier blanket deferral prose are retained in the [historical snapshot](../../history/REQ126-NOMINATIVE-RECORDS-SNAPSHOT-20261021.md). Later XSLT source supplies bounded named identity. This does not recover historical adopted specification pins or claim a new standalone XPath feature. ## 5. Motivation Distinct application interfaces may share a field named x while requiring different declared identities. ## 6. Language Alignment Unlike a structural alias, nominal identity is not established by matching fields alone. A C# or TypeScript name does not register a type in Bosak; the compiled XSLT declaration provides the tested context. ## 7. Applicability Use the tested XSLT declaration/constructor path. A bare XPath expression without the host-defined type context cannot assume these names are registered. ## 8. Structure Declare t:point and t:other with identical x fields; compare constructor results using instance-of or `record(t:point)` pattern. See complete fixtures rather than treating the name as a globally available XPath keyword. ## 9. Participants [xsl:record-type](../deferred/xslt-record-type.md) supplies the context and constructor; [RecordPattern](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Patterns/RecordPattern.cs) tests the value without coercing it. ## 10. Collaborations Structural record aliases can describe field shapes separately; map patterns can inspect keys/entry sequences. None is a synonym for nominal identity. ## 11. Consequences Equal fields need not satisfy a different named type. Binding/function conversion rules require separate evidence; an identity check does not establish every coercion/recursive/package rule. ## 12. Implementation **C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S8-patterns. Fresh version-4 stylesheets in both hosts cover array/member sequences, map missing-versus-empty/surplus keys, aliases, annotated records and nominal identity. Predicates can fail to match without propagating their dynamic errors in the tested forms. No claim of complete declaration/import/package visibility, every composite pattern, generic JNode dispatch or earlier-profile promotion. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows. **C03 review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Constructor/type reconciliation](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.md) verifies Host-defined nominal identity differs from plain map shape; Constructor and typed-map coercion paths; Tested select/body/trailing defaults and static constructor/coercion values in Legacy and Xslt40Draft version-4 stylesheets. **Boundary:** Bounded defaults/static fields are verified in both named hosts; no blanket claim of missing support remains for those forms. Import/package identity, visibility, recursion, global-initializer timing and all static override/cast/update combinations still require separate evidence. Ownership: T04. Per-path controls and named schema/API/host evidence are retained in the [review matrix](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.json); no whole-type or AC-04 acceptance follows. New manifest checks use default Legacy host and effective version4.0, hence frozen XPath40. Legacy3.0 declaration/pattern refusals are explicit. Host selection, module/package identity, imports and authoring contexts need their own applicable tests; no exhaustive cross-context claim follows. No engine behavior changes. ## 13. Sample Code [nominal-own](../examples/intake-types/nominal-own.xsl), [nominal-other](../examples/intake-types/nominal-other.xsl), [type-nominal-own](../examples/intake-types/type-nominal-own.xsl) and [type-nominal-other](../examples/intake-types/type-nominal-other.xsl) give positive and negative examples. The older standalone [structural alternative](../examples/nominative-records/alternative.xpath) remains unchanged. ## 14. Performance Notes Cost follows the value/type/pattern being checked and any conversion/materialization. Field/member walks and predicates can add work; no benchmark, universal speedup or measured memory claim is supplied. ## 15. Known Uses New nominal and record-pattern rows plus [Xslt40RecordPatternTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40RecordPatternTests.cs). No new XPath GatedSets member or upstream acceptance is inferred from host-specific XSLT examples. ## 16. Related Features [Structural records](structural-records.md), [item aliases](../deferred/xslt-item-type.md), [grammar inventory](../TYPE-PATTERN-GRAMMAR.md).

Current catalog74 entries/2,893 documentation checks; REQ-126/AC-03 remain partial. Braid dependency1.23.4 unchanged. Earlier source/unpublished checkpoints below are historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Record updates (`but with`)** - **Frozen 4.0**, REQ-118 S6b. The result is a new record with the original record's type annotation; merged values must satisfy that annotation through coercion. This entry maps existing structural behavior, not a new nominal declaration facility. Delivery: [PR #90](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/90), immutable `ca6e9c27cf4c62953763f800bdef2610ff64789a`; [RecordTypeTests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/RecordTypeTests.cs) pins source behavior. Current review pin, refreshed22 October 2026: [expressions XML](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/b4723ff52fd9d4fabf2b4cd33bd44f21939c512c/specifications/xquery-40/src/expressions.xml), `id-with-expression`, `id-item-coercion-rules`, `casting-to-record`, `id-structural-record-types`. This is a current comparison, not a recovered historical adoption pin. The bounded signature-gate correction is in unpublished source 1.23.6; public 1.23.4 already supplies the documented4.0 record behavior. ## 2. Intent Construct a changed record while keeping its declared field constraints and leaving the original value available. ## 3. Also Known As A ButWithExpr performs a record update by construction. It is not an in-place assignment, a database mutation, or the discarded extensible-map proposal. The operands are record(*) and map(*); the record annotation supplies the result type. ## 4. History / Supersedes A 3.1 adapter can select/validate fields, convert values and create a replacement map with map:merge/use-last. The [complete baseline](../examples/record-contracts/report-3.xsl) does that for the stock task. It has no record annotation and is not a universal replacement for record coercion. [The 4.0 report](../examples/record-contracts/report-4.xsl) casts the imported map, then constructs its amended record. ## 5. Motivation A stock feed supplies quantity and delta. The report must show both the imported quantity and adjusted quantity, preserve row order and reject invalid lexical numbers. Record update makes a changed typed value explicit while retaining the before value. [Complete input/output and repair contract](../examples/record-contracts/README.md) makes the task independently runnable. ## 6. Language Alignment This is XPath's annotation-driven reconstruction, not JavaScript object spread or an unrestricted immutable dictionary update. Undeclared fields and noncoercible values fail. A cast may discard surplus keys and convert a lexical string to an integer; update uses coercion and therefore does not automatically perform that lexical cast. Optional empty values are entries whose values are empty, not absent keys. Structural records are distinct from XSLT-defined nominal identity. ## 7. Applicability Use it after establishing the target record annotation. At import boundaries, deliberately select cast versus coercion: cast filters extras; coercion rejects them. Supply correctly typed update values or convert them explicitly. The stock task casts @delta to integer before updating qty. This example permits negative adjustments and does not enforce a nonnegative-stock rule. ## 8. Structure ```xpath ((map{'a':1} cast as record(a as xs:integer)) but with map{'a':2})?a ``` This is the runnable `record-contract-update-value` probe and returns2. The original-preservation probe produces `1|2` from before/after lookups. ## 9. Participants [XPathParser](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Parser/Ast/XPathParser.cs) handles record syntax and but-with expressions. [VmEngine](../../../src/Bosak.XPath.Runtime/Vm/VmEngine.cs) applies the existing annotation/coercion path. [RecordTypeTests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/RecordTypeTests.cs) and the public [documentation runner](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) provide named evidence; no new public API is added. ## 10. Collaborations Cast constructs the import record, adding a present-but-empty optional note and dropping import-only trace. Update merges the replacement quantity and recoerces to the left annotation. The output keeps the original quantity and adjusted value in a row map. Map access and record lookup are distinct: map:get can inspect a missing key without the record lookup's undeclared-field error. ## 11. Consequences Unknown fields, a plain-map left operand, a non-map right operand and an empty required field raise XPTY0004 in the supplied probes. Integer-to-double promotion is checked; arbitrary string-to-integer update casting is not implied. Optional fields may be set to empty while retaining key presence. Nested structural conversion and declaration order are bounded tested cases, not proof of every composite/nominal type combination. ## 12. Implementation **C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S6-update. Updates reconstruct under the existing annotation, retain the original value and reject unknown or noncoercible replacement fields. Field order, empty values and nested promotion retain bounded evidence. Do not generalize structural updates to all nominal/static/package/recursive record combinations. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows. **C03 review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Constructor/type reconciliation](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.md) verifies Annotation-preserving reconstruction retains the original value; Unknown fields, plain-map left operand and invalid replacement values refuse; Optional empty values retain key presence; nested promotion and field order are bounded. **Boundary:** Update uses coercion, not lexical import casting. Structural examples do not establish every nominal static/default-field update, method or package context. Ownership: T04, T05. Per-path controls and named schema/API/host evidence are retained in the [review matrix](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.json); no whole-type or AC-04 acceptance follows. Thirty-five XPath probes cover cast/coercion/update distinctions; three explicit 3.1 refusal cases and eight complete3.0/4.0 reports bring the slice to46 documentation checks. The first run exposed a record-signature gate leak in old profiles, separate from value semantics. [The parser finding](../INLINE-RECORD-TYPE-GATE.md) and 44 dedicated API regressions preserve the failures and bounded correction. The new examples do not invent or promote a qt4 gate. ## 13. Sample Code The [complete report](../examples/record-contracts/README.md) uses `` and yields `BOLT:10->12|NUT:4->3|items=2;total=15` in both versions. Empty input yields `items=0;total=0`; reordered input changes line order; invalid delta `oops` raises FORG0001. No external variables or resources are needed. Report stylesheets specify namespaces and all context. ## 14. Performance Notes Reconstruction checks declared fields and may recursively convert nested values; it can allocate a new record and entries. The report retains before/after values and is not a streaming/persistence benchmark. No speed or memory advantage over the baseline is claimed; use the benchmark harness for measured workloads. ## 15. Known Uses Applicable AC-03 evidence: `record-contract-update-value`, `record-contract-update-original`, `record-contract-update-annotation`, `record-contract-update-extra`, `record-contract-update-promote`, `record-contract-update-empty-optional` and the report cases, all enumerated in [the slice audit](../RECORD-CONTRACTS.json) and [manifest](../examples/cases.json), run by CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome. Named [RecordTypeTests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/RecordTypeTests.cs): `ButWith_ResultKeepsRecordAnnotation`, `ButWith_UnknownField_XPTY0004`, `ButWith_PlainMapLhs_XPTY0004`, `ButWith_CoercesRhsValuesToFieldTypes`, `ButWith_ResultEntriesFollowDeclarationOrder`. [InlineRecordTypeVersionGateTests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/InlineRecordTypeVersionGateTests.cs) independently verifies44 version/signature controls. No feature-specific qt4 gated-set assignment is made. Historical upstream RecordType fixtures reflect an older draft; named tests and executable examples are explicit applicable evidence, not whole-suite conformance or automatic AC-03 closure. ## 16. Related Features [Structural record casts/coercion](structural-records.md), [typed-let coercion](typed-let-coercion.md), [XSLT named-record identity](nominative-records.md), [rejected extensible-map types](../rejected/extensible-map-types.md), [current grammar/acceptance reconciliation](../COVERAGE-RECONCILIATION.md).
