type-system/structural-records.md.text:
Structural record types

Practical reference: Frozen 4.0

**C12 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-4.md) records three contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Verified bounded conversion and annotation**. No full schema/type-context acceptance. C05-K03 still affects destructuring unknown annotated fields; ordinary-map empty lookup is separate. Final owner acceptance remains C13; earlier checkpoints are historical. **XSLT host/type review — 21 October 2026:** [Current mapping](../TYPE-PATTERN-GRAMMAR.md) distinguishes stylesheet aliases, conversion in bindings and noncoercing type/pattern tests. Named XSLT record identity is a separate bounded published contract; this does not add standalone XPath declarations. ## 1. Name and Classification **Structural record types** - **Frozen 4.0**. Delivery family: [REQ-118](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) / [REQ-123 registry](../../FEATURE_REQUESTS.md). Section provenance: REQ-118 S6b; structural record evidence in RecordTypeTests. [Primary implementation evidence](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/RecordTypeTests.cs) records the shipped behavior; this entry adds executable user-facing examples under REQ-126, rather than announcing a new engine feature. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [XPath 4.0: structural record types](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-structural-record-types), [item coercion](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-item-coercion-rules), [but with operator](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xquery-40/xpath-40.html#id-with-expression). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #90](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/90), [immutable mainline revision `ca6e9c27`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/ca6e9c27cf4c62953763f800bdef2610ff64789a) (2026-10-08). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Cast the agreed shape to an annotated record before using the record type contract. ## 3. Also Known As Use the name and spelling in this entry and its executable files. Related functions or instruction forms are described in the primary test evidence; no additional alias is adopted here. ## 4. History / Supersedes In 3.1, validate the map keys and field values explicitly. Compare the [complete earlier-version baseline](../examples/structural-records/before.xpath) with the [complete expression](../examples/structural-records/main.xpath). Both yield `EUR` for this synthetic input. They demonstrate this task, not universal equivalence of the two mechanisms. ## 5. Motivation An adapter receives a small map with invoice ID and currency fields. Cast the agreed shape to an annotated record before using the record type contract. Keeping this task explicit makes it possible to choose the feature for a practical reason and verify what the receiving application will see. ## 6. Language Alignment Read the behavior as XPath/XSLT semantics. Similar vocabulary in another programming language is not a compatibility promise. A plain map is not an annotated record in Bosak. Coercion policy and undeclared fields must be understood before adapting broad payloads. ## 7. Applicability Use this form when solving the stated task and the consumer permits the declared compatibility level. Keep the earlier baseline when the application requires 3.1 expressions or portable 3.0 stylesheets. A plain map is not an annotated record in Bosak. Coercion policy and undeclared fields must be understood before adapting broad payloads. ## 8. Structure ```xquery (map { 'invoiceId': 'INV-1042', 'currency': 'EUR' } cast as record(invoiceId as xs:string, currency as xs:string))?currency ``` This is the worked case's syntax, not a replacement for the full language grammar. Required namespaces and surrounding context are supplied in the linked complete files. ## 9. Participants XPath31Expression, CompileOptions, the parser/compiler, and the shared runtime/function library provide the public execution path. [Primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/RecordTypeTests.cs) identify the feature's implementation contract. The examples use public APIs only. ## 10. Collaborations The case combines source values, the named feature, and explicit output formatting. [Worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md) show how selection, construction, and business rejection fit into larger transformations. ## 11. Consequences Benefit: Cast the agreed shape to an annotated record before using the record type contract. Tradeoff: the declared compatibility level and edge rules become part of the consumer contract. A plain map is not an annotated record in Bosak. Coercion policy and undeclared fields must be understood before adapting broad payloads. The [record-contract delivery](../RECORD-CONTRACTS.md) and [complete stock task](../examples/record-contracts/README.md) add bounded value/error comparisons and the separate [record-update entry](record-updates.md). | Contract | Cast | Coercion / record update | |---|---|---| | Extra source key | Discarded when outside the target record fields | Rejected with XPTY0004. | | String quantity to integer | Cast when required; invalid lexical value raises FORG0001 | A string is not automatically an integer; supplied parameter/update probes raise XPTY0004. | | Missing optional field | Create a key whose value is empty | Create that present empty entry; it is not absence. | | Missing/empty required field | XPTY0004 | XPTY0004. | | Numeric/nested conversion | Keep matching values or apply the field cast | Apply field coercion recursively; tested integer-to-double promotion. | | Field order | Constrained by the target record | Coercion/recoercion follows field declaration order in the probes. | | record(*) | Assertion of an already annotated record | A plain map is not itself an annotated record. | | Changed value | Construct a record | but with reconstructs under the existing annotation; original value remains available. | These are tested structural cases, not exhaustive casts, nominal static/default fields or host declarations. Source1.23.6 also fixes an earlier-profile inline-signature leak; [the finding](../INLINE-RECORD-TYPE-GATE.md) preserves the original failing3.1 refusals instead of treating them as supported syntax. ## 12. Implementation **C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S6-record-conversion, S6-update. C03 cast/coercion/lookup boundaries remain: casts filter surplus fields, coercion rejects them, optional keys become present empty entries, and ordinary maps are not annotated records. Full composite/nominal/static/default/package and error-eagerness combinations remain unaccepted; bounded nominal defaults from C03 remain supported. Updates reconstruct under the existing annotation, retain the original value and reject unknown or noncoercible replacement fields. Field order, empty values and nested promotion retain bounded evidence. Do not generalize structural updates to all nominal/static/package/recursive record combinations. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows. **C03 review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Constructor/type reconciliation](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.md) verifies Cast constructs an annotated record and discards surplus fields; Coercion rejects surplus fields and recursively coerces declared fields; Required/optional emptiness, declaration order, record(*) and undeclared lookup/map:get distinctions. **Boundary:** A plain map is not an annotated record. Structural matches do not require annotation identity with the tested target, while named identity remains host-defined. Complete record/nominal/schema conversion combinations are not inferred. Ownership: T04, T05. Per-path controls and named schema/API/host evidence are retained in the [review matrix](../CONSTRUCTOR-TYPE-RECONCILIATION.json); no whole-type or AC-04 acceptance follows. Compile the after/edge expressions at XPathCompatibility.XPath40. The baseline uses XPath31. The example harness checks default-mode refusal for successful 4.0 cases; negative cases pin the declared error. See [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs): it executes the published files from the [case manifest](../examples/cases.json). This documentation slice changes no engine source. ## 13. Sample Code Input is synthetic and declared directly in the complete expression. The [complete expression](../examples/structural-records/main.xpath) yields `EUR`. The [edge case](../examples/structural-records/edge.xpath) yields `false`. No external resources or application variables are required. See the [example runner](../examples/README.md) for commands and host context. ## 14. Performance Notes Expected class: field-dependent validation/coercion and record construction. Nested field contracts can add further work. These are implementation expectations, not measured deltas. No benchmark is claimed; use the repository benchmark harness before making workload-specific speed or memory claims. ## 15. Known Uses Executable example IDs: `structural-records-main`, `structural-records-edge`, `structural-records-before` in `CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome`. Existing unit evidence: [primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/RecordTypeTests.cs). Chapter-level evidence does not promote a qt4tests set into GatedSets; conformance status remains owned by the harness and delivery records. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Coercion_BuildsAnnotatedRecord`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/RecordTypeTests.cs), [`Coercion_MissingFieldBecomesEmptyEntry`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/RecordTypeTests.cs), [`Coercion_SurplusKeys_XPTY0004`](../../../tests/Bosak.XPath.Api.Tests/RecordTypeTests.cs). Hand-written tests pin annotated-record semantics; the delivery explicitly identified upstream `prod-RecordType` as an older draft. Do not infer promotion from these tests. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features [XSLT named-record boundary](../deferred/xslt-record-type.md) separates named stylesheet declarations from this shipped XPath structural contract. It also separates supported structural bindings from named identity; older deferral and source snapshots remain historical. See [record updates](record-updates.md), the [catalog index](../README.md), [worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md), and the alternatives in section 4. The case may be used independently of the larger chapters. *Created 2026-10-11: verified practical catalog example and earlier-version baseline.*

Benefit: Cast the agreed shape to an annotated record before using the record type contract. Tradeoff: the declared compatibility level and edge rules become part of the consumer contract. The [record-contract delivery](../RECORD-CONTRACTS.md) and [complete stock task](../examples/record-contracts/README.md) add bounded value/error comparisons and the separate [record-update entry](record-updates.md).

| Contract | Cast | Coercion / record update |
|---|---|---|
| Extra source key | Discarded when outside the target record fields | Rejected with XPTY0004. |
| String quantity to integer | Cast when required; invalid lexical value raises FORG0001 | A string is not automatically an integer; supplied parameter/update probes raise XPTY0004. |
| Missing optional field | Create a key whose value is empty | Create that present empty entry; it is not absence. |
| Missing/empty required field | XPTY0004 | XPTY0004. |
| Numeric/nested conversion | Keep matching values or apply the field cast | Apply field coercion recursively; tested integer-to-double promotion. |
| Field order | Constrained by the target record | Coercion/recoercion follows field declaration order in the probes. |
| record(*) | Assertion of an already annotated record | A plain map is not itself an annotated record. |
| Changed value | Construct a record | but with reconstructs under the existing annotation; original value remains available. |

These are tested structural cases, not exhaustive casts, nominal static/default fields or host declarations. xslt-instructions/compound-patterns.md.text:
Compound template patterns and dispatch

21 October 2026

**C12 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-4.md) records three contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Verified bounded pattern sets and priorities**. The delivered minimum-priority correction remains closed. Complete current pattern/model combinations, schema and generic JNode semantics remain outside this bounded review. Final owner acceptance remains C13; earlier checkpoints are historical. **C07 lifecycle review — 26 October 2026:** [Current disposition and correction receipts](../LIFECYCLE-RECONCILIATION.md) distinguish delivered scope, retained history and pending acceptance. Six closure workpackages remain; no feature or profile promotion. **Public1.23.4 — 22 October 2026:** Union-minimum and EQName URI-punctuation priority corrections are [published and verified](../../RELEASE-1.23.4-PUBLICATION.md). Opening-bracket URI parsing remains separately limited. Earlier unpublished delivery records below are historical. **22 October 2026 — EQName priority correction, source 1.23.4:** Effective 4.0 name-test priority ignores URI punctuation; earlier profiles retain their existing behavior. [Scope, regressions and validation](../EQNAME-PATTERN-PRIORITY.md). Opening-bracket URI parsing remains a separate limitation. Public release remains 1.23.2; REQ-126 stays In Progress. Prior delivery records below retain their historical versions and outcomes. **22 October 2026 — source 1.23.3:** 4.0 node unions now use the minimum alternative default priority, aligned with the pinned current draft. The two catalog reproducers now expect `competitor`; their prior 1.23.2 observations remain recorded. 3.0 dispatch, explicit priorities and single-rule 4.0 `next-match` are preserved. [Correction and validation](../UNION-MINIMUM-PRIORITY.md). Public release remains 1.23.2; REQ-126 stays In Progress. Earlier delivery snapshots below are historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Implemented bounded XSLT 4.0 compound contexts in public 1.26.3.** The union-minimum, EQName URI-priority and opening-bracket parsing corrections are delivered. [C05 review](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) retains their verified scope and the remaining pattern/model limits. [The original review](../COMPOUND-PATTERN-GRAMMAR.md) and dated 1.23.x observations remain historical. ## 2. Intent Combine node membership tests and dispatch priorities without confusing set parsing, rule identity or item-pattern context. ## 3. Also Known As Union pattern, intersect/except pattern, grouped XNode pattern and effective-version-sensitive dispatch in the reviewed contexts. ## 4. History / Supersedes The complete3.0 baseline uses predicate conditions and explicit priorities; the4.0 report uses grouped set/union patterns. Earlier technical outputs are observations, not universal semantic equivalence. Original source delivery revisions and historical adoption gaps remain in the review/audit. ## 5. Motivation A manual publisher must hold blocked/draft articles even when other readiness conditions match, while keeping review cases visible and output order stable. ## 6. Language Alignment Pattern operators do not inherit every XPath-expression or C#/SQL precedence intuition. Parenthesized XNode contexts can differ from unparenthesized item patterns. A priority selects a rule after membership; it does not change which nodes satisfy a set expression. ## 7. Applicability Use supporting XSLT contexts with explicit business priorities. Source1.23.3 corrects implicit union priority to the pinned minimum; public1.23.2 retains the recorded discrepancy. ## 8. Structure Reviewed shapes include `(A intersect B) except C`, `A | B`, `A union B` and parenthesized XNode forms. These are descriptive shapes; complete XML namespaces and expression context are in the [reports](../examples/manual-patterns/README.md), not an exhaustive grammar. ## 9. Participants [PatternCompiler](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Patterns/PatternCompiler.cs) handles validation/membership; [TemplateRule](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Stylesheet/TemplateRule.cs) computes priority and retains rule identity. No public API change. ## 10. Collaborations Combine rule membership with explicit priority, modes, sorted apply-templates and bounded next-match chains. Type/map/array pattern categories are mapped [separately](structured-value-patterns.md). ## 11. Consequences Grouping can change membership;4.0 node unions have a single rule identity in the tested chains. Source1.23.3 uses the pinned minimum alternative priority; public1.23.2 retains maximum. An explicit priority is an application policy, not a conformance fix for the engine. ## 12. Implementation **C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S8-compound. Left-associative intersect/except and grouped membership pass. Delivered 4.0 union-minimum priority, EQName URI-punctuation priority and bracket parsing pass; older uncorrected notices remain historical. Earlier-profile priority compatibility, next-match identity and uncommon mixed pattern contexts retain named unit evidence rather than a blanket whole-pattern acceptance. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows. New manifest cases use default Legacy host with root/local effective3.0/4.0 versions. Local template overrides are tested. No new complete host/module/package/authoring context matrix or gate promotion is claimed. ## 13. Sample Code Run normal, empty and reordered [manual reports](../examples/manual-patterns/README.md). Compare [set-left40](../examples/manual-patterns/set-left40.xsl) and [set-grouped40](../examples/manual-patterns/set-grouped40.xsl). The [union reproducer](../examples/manual-patterns/union-max40.xsl) verifies the source1.23.3 minimum-priority correction; [explicit priority](../examples/manual-patterns/union-explicit40.xsl) is the safe supported control. ## 14. Performance Notes Matching costs depend on operands, candidate count, paths and predicates. Priority/rule storage can affect dispatch work. No measured speedup, benchmark or universal memory result is claimed. ## 15. Known Uses New manual-patterns cases; existing Xslt40SetPatternAssociativityTests, Xslt40UnionPatternTests, Xslt40SetPatternPriorityTests and Xslt40ParenthesizedItemPatternTests are linked in the [review](../COMPOUND-PATTERN-GRAMMAR.md). sections.2: Combine node membership tests and dispatch priorities without confusing set parsing, rule identity or item-pattern context.

Instruction separators

Practical reference: Bosak XSLT 4.0 surface

**C12 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-4.md) records three contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Verified bounded iteration separators**. No universal streaming, arbitrary serialization or callback/sequence-constructor combination claim. Final owner acceptance remains C13; earlier checkpoints are historical. **C06 host/profile review — 26 October 2026:** [Bounded reconciliation](../HOST-PROFILE-RECONCILIATION.md) maps this entry to current pinned instruction/host rules and named tests. Seven workpackages remain; instruction comparison, complete static-mode evidence and host/adoption limits remain explicit. No acceptance or profile promotion. Earlier notices remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Instruction separators** - **Bosak XSLT 4.0 surface**. Delivery family: [REQ-118](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) / [REQ-123 registry](../../FEATURE_REQUESTS.md). Section provenance: REQ-118 S7/S8; corresponding local XSLT surface tests. [Primary implementation evidence](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40SurfaceTests.cs) records the shipped behavior; this entry adds executable user-facing examples under REQ-126, rather than announcing a new engine feature. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [XSLT 4.0: for-each separator](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xslt-40/Overview.html#for-each-separator), [apply-templates separator](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xslt-40/Overview.html#apply-templates-separator). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #91](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/91), [immutable mainline revision `c0427907`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/c0427907002a355f6662ddcdc7412ad8f4a18846) (2026-10-08). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Insert a delimiter between iterations without adding a trailing delimiter. ## 3. Also Known As Use the name and spelling in this entry and its executable files. Related functions or instruction forms are described in the primary test evidence; no additional alias is adopted here. ## 4. History / Supersedes Use string-join or explicit position checks in 3.0. Compare the [complete earlier-version baseline](../examples/instruction-separators/before.xsl) with the [complete stylesheet](../examples/instruction-separators/transform.xsl). Both yield `FILTER-A, BOLT-M8` for this synthetic input. They demonstrate this task, not universal equivalence of the two mechanisms. ## 5. Motivation Print a compact list of product codes for a picking label. Insert a delimiter between iterations without adding a trailing delimiter. Keeping this task explicit makes it possible to choose the feature for a practical reason and verify what the receiving application will see. ## 6. Language Alignment Read the behavior as XPath/XSLT semantics. Similar vocabulary in another programming language is not a compatibility promise. The separator is between iterations; emitted text and empty iteration bodies need deliberate handling. ## 7. Applicability Use this form when solving the stated task and the consumer permits the declared compatibility level. Keep the earlier baseline when the application requires 3.1 expressions or portable 3.0 stylesheets. The separator is between iterations; emitted text and empty iteration bodies need deliberate handling. ## 8. Structure ```xml ``` This is the worked case's syntax, not a replacement for the full language grammar. Required namespaces and surrounding context are supplied in the linked complete files. ## 9. Participants The stylesheet compiler and TransformEngine execute the instruction; the contained expressions use the existing XPath engine. [Primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40SurfaceTests.cs) identify the feature's implementation contract. The examples use public APIs only. ## 10. Collaborations The case combines source values, the named feature, and explicit output formatting. [Worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md) show how selection, construction, and business rejection fit into larger transformations. ## 11. Consequences Benefit: Insert a delimiter between iterations without adding a trailing delimiter. Tradeoff: the declared compatibility level and edge rules become part of the consumer contract. The separator is between iterations; emitted text and empty iteration bodies need deliberate handling. ## 12. Implementation The complete draft-instruction file declares version="4.0". Bosak recognizes these implemented instruction surfaces; its instruction support is separate from XPathCompatibility. Embedded expressions in these files remain XPath 3.1. The companion baseline declares version="3.0". See [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs): it executes the published files from the [case manifest](../examples/cases.json). This documentation slice changes no engine source. ## 13. Sample Code Input is synthetic and declared directly in the complete expression, or in [main.xml](../examples/instruction-separators/main.xml) for an instruction example. The [complete stylesheet](../examples/instruction-separators/transform.xsl) yields `FILTER-A, BOLT-M8`. The [edge case](../examples/instruction-separators/edge.xml) yields an empty string. No external resources or application variables are required. See the [example runner](../examples/README.md) for commands and host context. ## 14. Performance Notes Expected class: iteration output with separator insertion. Output volume remains proportional to selected labels and delimiters. These are implementation expectations, not measured deltas. No benchmark is claimed; use the repository benchmark harness before making workload-specific speed or memory claims. ## 15. Known Uses Executable example IDs: `instruction-separators-main`, `instruction-separators-edge`, `instruction-separators-before` in `CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome`. Existing unit evidence: [primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40SurfaceTests.cs). Chapter-level evidence does not promote a qt4tests set into GatedSets; conformance status remains owned by the harness and delivery records. **Named implementation evidence:** [`ForEach_Separator_BetweenItems`](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40SurfaceTests.cs), [`ForEach_Separator_WithSort`](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40SurfaceTests.cs), [`ForEach_Separator_EmptyAndSingleItem_NoSeparator`](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40SurfaceTests.cs). Not a qt4 expression-set feature. XSLT evidence uses the named instruction tests below; no upstream XSLT gate promotion is claimed. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features See the [catalog index](../README.md), [worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md), and the alternatives in section 4. The case may be used independently of the larger chapters. *Created 2026-10-11: verified practical catalog example and earlier-version baseline.*

xslt-instructions/module-profiles.md.text:
Module and used-package profile propagation

Bosak host policy - bounded executable reference

**C12 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-4.md) records three contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Verified bounded direct module policy**. Direct nonconflicting examples do not establish arbitrary transitive graphs, import precedence, package versions, override/accept/expose or full lexical defaults. C06 complete static-detection mode remains unproved. Final owner acceptance remains C13; earlier checkpoints are historical. **C06 host/profile review — 26 October 2026:** [Bounded reconciliation](../HOST-PROFILE-RECONCILIATION.md) maps this entry to current pinned instruction/host rules and named tests. Seven workpackages remain; instruction comparison, complete static-mode evidence and host/adoption limits remain explicit. No acceptance or profile promotion. Earlier notices remain historical. **Public 1.23.8 - 23 October 2026:** The function default-mode fix and host/module profile coverage are [published and verified](../../RELEASE-1.23.8-PUBLICATION.md). Current catalog:76 entries/3,073 documentation checks. REQ-126/AC-03 remain partial; Braid smoke/acceptance is separate. Earlier source/unpublished/PR checkpoints below are historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Module/profile propagation** - implemented Bosak host composition, with an opt-in experimental XSLT draft profile and frozen embedded XPath 4.0. The same compilation host applies to a directly included, imported or used-package module, while expression selection and forwards-compatible validation retain the dependency's own effective version. This is not a new grammar feature or an experimental XPath promotion. Profile implementation: [cc07d50f8a55bdca907d398d4916d95cbed36734](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/cc07d50f8a55bdca907d398d4916d95cbed36734). This slice depends on the separate [function default-mode fix](../../XSLT-FUNCTION-DEFAULT-MODE.md), [PR416](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/416), source 1.23.8 unpublished; public 1.23.7 is unchanged. Current comparison: [immutable XSLT XML](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/b4723ff52fd9d4fabf2b4cd33bd44f21939c512c/specifications/xslt-40/src/xslt.xml), include/import/use-package/backwards/forwards/modes sections, refreshed on 23 October 2026. This is not recovered historical adoption. [Audit](../MODULE-PROFILE-BOUNDARIES.md). ## 2. Intent Move a transformation function into a dependency without losing the selected compiler host or silently replacing the dependency's declared version with the principal stylesheet's version. ## 3. Also Known As Include/import module loading and used-package compilation. An XSLT package name/package-version here identifies an XML library package; it is distinct from the Bosak NuGet release version. Include, import and use-package are different composition mechanisms, not interchangeable aliases. ## 4. History / Supersedes Each relation has a baseline library at version 3.0 using explicit if/then/else and a version 4.0 library using otherwise. The principal report remains version 3.0 and calls the same quantity function. The six complete report/library pairs in [the task](../examples/module-profiles/README.md) run under both hosts. This is Bosak compatibility policy, not a promise that an arbitrary XSLT 3.0 processor can run a 4.0 library. ## 5. Motivation A shared order-quantity function defaults a missing quantity to1 while retaining explicit zero. It can be maintained in one dependency rather than duplicated in a principal template. The examples separate library migration from the principal version and verify namespace, URI and registration setup together with the actual report. ## 6. Language Alignment The current XSLT draft gives included/imported modules and packages their own declaration/static-context rules. Bosak propagates the selected processor host through compilation; it does not overwrite the child version. Legacy's hybrid policy selects embedded XPath by effective version, whereas Xslt40Draft supplies frozen 4.0 even in a 3.0 library. The tests use nonconflicting function names to isolate that policy. They do not establish import precedence, override/accept/expose semantics, or general equivalence between composition mechanisms. ## 7. Applicability Use this reference for one direct include/import edge or one registered used package loaded from local files, compiled with either public host profile. Multi-hop graphs, package version ranges, overrides, schema/static parameters, dynamic evaluate, authoring, streaming, remote/resource-policy behavior and complete default-mode propagation are outside this slice. ## 8. Structure | Dependency effective version | Legacy host | Draft host | |---|---|---| |3.0 | The supplied otherwise expression refuses XPST0003, regardless of principal 3.0/4.0 | Frozen4.0 expression succeeds | |4.0 | Frozen4.0 expression succeeds, even with a 3.0 principal | Frozen4.0 expression succeeds | | Module3.0 with local function4.0 | Local override enables the supplied 4.0 expression | Remains frozen 4.0 | | Module4.0 with local function3.0 | Local override refuses the supplied 4.0 expression | Remains frozen 4.0 | The selected host's forwards-compatible ceiling still applies to the child's effective version:3.0 for Legacy and4.0 for Draft. A future-version principal does not make a known-version child forwards compatible in Draft. scan remains unavailable under both hosts in the supplied 4.0 libraries. ## 9. Participants [XsltCompiler](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Api/XsltCompiler.cs) captures ProcessorProfile and the URI resolver. [Stylesheet](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Stylesheet/Stylesheet.cs) resolves includes, imports and used packages. [XsltFunctionLibrary.RegisterPackage](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Api/XsltFunctionLibrary.cs) maps a package name/version to an absolute module URI. The [catalog runner](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) supplies optional per-case package registrations and always cleans them in finally; its existing package-registry collection serializes these tests with other registry users. ## 10. Collaborations An app/main.xsl principal resolves ../library/module.xsl relative to its own file URI for include/import. A package principal uses a synthetic URN and exact package-version 1.0, registered to the corresponding absolute XML file URI before compilation. The library declares p:quantity and its own version. The principal passes each line node, preserves order and sums the returned quantities. Registry setup is caller/test setup; the XML file does not embed a compiler profile. ## 11. Consequences Changing the principal's version alone does not promote a 3.0 dependency in Legacy. A4.0 dependency does not promote unrelated principal expressions either; this entry tests calls into the library, not every caller expression. Unknown attributes on the supplied apply-templates instruction follow the child/local version and inherited host. Those validation probes exposed an independent function default-mode bug: legal success cases raised XTSE0020 after validation. The separate fix preserves their expected results rather than recording the bug as supported behavior. ## 12. Implementation The 114 cases are 66 focused host/version/static/validation/refusal controls and 48 complete report runs. Before package setup the baseline was70pass/44fail:38 missing-registration failures and six default-mode failures. Scoped registrations changed this to105pass/9fail, revealing the same runtime issue in packages too. On the isolated fix all 114 pass with unchanged expected results. The runner adds optional packages metadata and cleanup on both success and failure; rows without it preserve their prior setup. [Machine audit](../MODULE-PROFILE-BOUNDARIES.json). ## 13. Sample Code For each relation, [the complete task](../examples/module-profiles/README.md) links the baseline and mixed-version principal/library files. With [normal.xml](../examples/module-profiles/normal.xml), both variants under both hosts emit `A=2|B=1|C=0|lines=3;total=3`. Empty input emits `lines=0;total=0`; reordered input changes line order; invalid integer text raises FORG0001. All namespaces, fixtures, dependency locations, package registrations and expected results are supplied. The library expression `(xs:integer($line/@qty) ?? 1)` is actually executed in the4.0 variants. ## 14. Performance Notes These examples verify compilation policy and module loading, not a performance optimization. Each run compiles real local files and may allocate a separate package/module context. No compile-cache, concurrency or timing benefit is claimed. Reusing a compiled executable or resolving larger graphs needs separate measurements and contracts. ## 15. Known Uses Applicable AC-03 evidence: `module-profile-include-root4-module3-legacy`, `module-profile-import-root3-module4-legacy`, `module-profile-package-root4-module3-draft40`, `module-profile-package-root4-module4-local3-legacy`, `module-profile-import-validation-root5-module4-draft40`, `module-profile-package-static-root4-module3-draft40` and `module-profile-package-report-module40-normal-legacy`, plus all 114 cases listed in [the audit](../MODULE-PROFILE-BOUNDARIES.json) and [manifest](../examples/cases.json). Named [ProcessorProfileTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/ProcessorProfileTests.cs) methods ModulesInheritProfile, ModuleValidationInheritsProfile and UsedPackageInheritsProfile provide independent API evidence. This XSLT host/module contract has no applicable XPath-only gate assignment; no gate is invented or promoted. ## 16. Related Features [Ordinary stylesheet profiles](processor-profiles.md), [otherwise](../operators-and-syntax/otherwise-operator.md), [function default-mode correction](../../XSLT-FUNCTION-DEFAULT-MODE.md) and [coverage reconciliation](../COVERAGE-RECONCILIATION.md). General package visibility/version resolution, transitive graphs and full lexical default-mode contexts remain follow-ups. REQ-126 and D2/D3/D4/AC03 remain partial.

This is Bosak compatibility policy, not a promise that an arbitrary XSLT 3.0 processor can run a 4.0 library.
sections.5: A shared order-quantity function defaults a missing quantity to1 while retaining explicit zero. It can be maintained in one dependency rather than duplicated in a principal template. The examples separate library migration from the principal version and verify namespace, URI and registration setup together with the actual report.
sections.6: The current XSLT draft gives included/imported modules and packages their own declaration/static-context rules. Bosak propagates the selected processor host through compilation; it does not overwrite the child version. Legacy's hybrid policy selects embedded XPath by effective version, whereas Xslt40Draft supplies frozen 4.0 even in a 3.0 library. The tests use nonconflicting function names to isolate that policy. They do not establish import precedence, override/accept/expose semantics, or general equivalence between composition mechanisms.
sections.7: Use this reference for one direct include/import edge or one registered used package loaded from local files, compiled with either public host profile. Multi-hop graphs, package version ranges, overrides, schema/static parameters, dynamic evaluate, authoring, streaming, remote/resource-policy behavior and complete default-mode propagation are outside this slice.
sections.8:
| Dependency effective version | Legacy host | Draft host |
|---|---|---|
|3.0 | The supplied otherwise expression refuses XPST0003, regardless of principal 3.0/4.0 | Frozen4.0 expression succeeds |
|4.0 | Frozen4.0 expression succeeds, even with a 3.0 principal | Frozen4.0 expression succeeds |
| Module3.0 with local function4.0 | Local override enables the supplied 4.0 expression | Remains frozen 4.0 |
| Module4.0 with local function3.0 | Local override refuses the supplied 4.0 expression | Remains frozen 4.0 |

The selected host's forwards-compatible ceiling still applies to the child's effective version:3.0 for Legacy and4.0 for Draft. A future-version principal does not make a known-version child forwards compatible in Draft. scan remains unavailable under both hosts in the supplied 4.0 libraries.
sections.9: [XsltCompiler](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Api/XsltCompiler.cs) captures ProcessorProfile and the URI resolver. [Stylesheet](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Stylesheet/Stylesheet.cs) resolves includes, imports and used packages. [XsltFunctionLibrary.RegisterPackage](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Api/XsltFunctionLibrary.cs) maps a package name/version to an absolute module URI. The [catalog runner](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) supplies optional per-case package registrations and always cleans them in finally; its existing package-registry collection serializes these tests with other registry users.
sections.10: An app/main.xsl principal resolves ../library/module.xsl relative to its own file URI for include/import. A package principal uses a synthetic URN and exact package-version 1.0, registered to the corresponding absolute XML file URI before compilation. The library declares p:quantity and its own version. The principal passes each line node, preserves order and sums the returned quantities. Registry setup is caller/test setup; the XML file does not embed a compiler profile.
sections.11: Changing the principal's version alone does not promote a 3.0 dependency in Legacy. A4.0 dependency does not promote unrelated principal expressions either; this entry tests calls into the library, not every caller expression. Unknown attributes on the supplied apply-templates instruction follow the child/local version and inherited host. Those validation probes exposed an independent function default-mode bug: legal success cases raised XTSE0020 after validation. The separate fix preserves their expected results rather than recording the bug as supported behavior.
sections.12: The 114 cases are 66 focused host/version/static/validation/refusal controls and 48 complete report runs. Before package setup the baseline was70pass/44fail:38 missing-registration failures and six default-mode failures. Scoped registrations changed this to105pass/9fail, revealing the same runtime issue in packages too. On the isolated fix all 114 pass with unchanged expected results. The runner adds optional packages metadata and cleanup on both success and failure; rows without it preserve their prior setup. [Machine audit](../MODULE-PROFILE-BOUNDARIES.json).
sections.13: For each relation, [the complete task](../examples/module-profiles/README.md) links the baseline and mixed-version principal/library files. With [normal.xml](../examples/module-profiles/normal.xml), both variants under both hosts emit `A=2|B=1|C=0|lines=3;total=3`. Empty input emits `lines=0;total=0`; reordered input changes line order; invalid integer text raises FORG0001. All namespaces, fixtures, dependency locations, package registrations and expected results are supplied. The library expression `(xs:integer($line/@qty) ?? 1)` is actually executed in the4.0 variants.
sections.14: These examples verify compilation policy and module loading, not a performance optimization. Each run compiles real local files and may allocate a separate package/module context. No compile-cache, concurrency or timing benefit is claimed. Reusing a compiled executable or resolving larger graphs needs separate measurements and contracts.
sections.15: Applicable AC-03 evidence: `module-profile-include-root4-module3-legacy`, `module-profile-import-root3-module4-legacy`, `module-profile-package-root4-module3-draft40`, `module-profile-package-root4-module4-local3-legacy`, `module-profile-import-validation-root5-module4-draft40`, `module-profile-package-static-root4-module3-draft40` and `module-profile-package-report-module40-normal-legacy`, plus all 114 cases listed in [the audit](../MODULE-PROFILE-BOUNDARIES.json) and [manifest](../examples/cases.json). Named [ProcessorProfileTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/ProcessorProfileTests.cs) methods ModulesInheritProfile, ModuleValidationInheritsProfile and UsedPackageInheritsProfile provide independent API evidence. This XSLT host/module contract has no applicable XPath-only gate assignment; no gate is invented or promoted.
sections.16: [Ordinary stylesheet profiles](processor-profiles.md), [otherwise](../operators-and-syntax/otherwise-operator.md), [function default-mode correction](../../XSLT-FUNCTION-DEFAULT-MODE.md) and [coverage reconciliation](../COVERAGE-RECONCILIATION.md). General package visibility/version resolution, transitive graphs and full lexical default-mode contexts remain follow-ups. REQ-126 and D2/D3/D4/AC03 remain partial.

xslt-instructions/processor-profiles.md.text:
Stylesheet versions and processor profiles

Bosak host policy - bounded executable reference

**C12 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-4.md) records three contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Verified bounded frozen host policy**. Neither profile implements all current draft syntax or enables Experimental scan. C06-H01 requires a complete static-detection mode; lazy timing alone is not classified as a defect. Final owner acceptance remains C13; earlier checkpoints are historical. **C06 host/profile review — 26 October 2026:** [Bounded reconciliation](../HOST-PROFILE-RECONCILIATION.md) maps this entry to current pinned instruction/host rules and named tests. Seven workpackages remain; instruction comparison, complete static-mode evidence and host/adoption limits remain explicit. No acceptance or profile promotion. Earlier notices remain historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **Version/profile boundary** - implemented Bosak host policy. Legacy is the default compatibility profile; Xslt40Draft is an opt-in experimental XSLT processor profile whose embedded XPath is frozen 4.0. This is not a new language feature or a promotion to XPath40Experimental. Public/source 1.23.7 already provides this API. Original profile delivery: [cc07d50f8a55bdca907d398d4916d95cbed36734](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/cc07d50f8a55bdca907d398d4916d95cbed36734). Current comparison: [immutable XSLT XML](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/b4723ff52fd9d4fabf2b4cd33bd44f21939c512c/specifications/xslt-40/src/xslt.xml), sections backwards, backwards-3.0, forwards and standard-attributes, refreshed against upstream master on 23 October 2026. This comparison pin does not recover a historical adopted specification revision. [Delivery audit](../HOST-PROFILE-BOUNDARIES.md). ## 2. Intent Choose an execution host explicitly and understand how a local version declaration affects XPath syntax and forwards-compatible validation within that host. ## 3. Also Known As Processor capability/profile, effective stylesheet version, embedded XPath compatibility and forwards-compatible ceiling are separate concepts. XsltProcessorProfile.Xslt40Draft and XPathCompatibility.XPath40Experimental are different API settings; the former does not enable experimental XPath functions. ## 4. History / Supersedes The [baseline report](../examples/host-profiles/report-baseline.xsl) uses ordinary 3.0 expressions. The [mixed-version report](../examples/host-profiles/report-local40.xsl) keeps a 3.0 root but places version 4.0 on its template and uses the otherwise operator. Both are executed under both Bosak hosts. A local 4.0 block is not a portable way to give an arbitrary XSLT 3.0 processor XPath 4.0 capability; these are Bosak host contracts. ## 5. Motivation An order report defaults an absent quantity to1 while preserving an explicit zero. Migrating one template allows a compact otherwise expression without changing the root version. A caller still needs to know whether its host treats a lower local version as a syntax boundary. [The complete task](../examples/host-profiles/README.md) gives input, all instructions, exact results and malformed-data behavior. ## 6. Language Alignment The pinned XSLT 4.0 draft defines effective version from the nearest applicable [xsl:]version attribute, with special rules including xsl:output. It defines no 3.0-versus4.0 compatibility-mode differences for a 4.0 processor. The draft profile's acceptance of frozen 4.0 XPath within version 3.0 is therefore intentional. Bosak Legacy is its preserved compatibility policy, not an assertion that it exactly emulates every W3C3.0 processor: it uses a 3.0 forwards-compatible ceiling while selecting embedded XPath 4.0 at effective versions at least 4.0. ## 7. Applicability Use this entry when compiling an ordinary stylesheet with XsltCompiler or generating a locally versioned block. This slice excludes includes/imports, used packages, schema/static parameters, authoring/edit APIs, dynamic evaluate, streaming, detailed fallback behavior and versions1.0/2.0. Existing tests elsewhere may cover some of those paths; this entry does not claim their full matrix. ## 8. Structure | Host | Embedded XPath in the supplied ordinary expression paths | Forwards-compatible ceiling | |---|---|---| | Legacy (default) | Effective version below 4.0 selects XPath 3.1; at least 4.0 selects frozen 4.0 |3.0 | | Xslt40Draft (explicit opt-in) | Frozen4.0 independently of local 3.0/4.0 version |4.0 | A non-root XSLT instruction uses unqualified version; a literal result element uses xsl:version. The nearest declaration wins. xsl:output/@version selects serialization behavior and does not promote the surrounding stylesheet's XPath level. The ceiling describes capability-sensitive forwards compatibility; it does not enable arbitrary future syntax. ## 9. Participants [XsltCompiler.ProcessorProfile](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Api/XsltCompiler.cs) selects the public host enum [XsltProcessorProfile](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Api/XsltProcessorProfile.cs). [Stylesheet](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Stylesheet/Stylesheet.cs) resolves GetEffectiveVersion, GetXPathCompatibility and IsForwardsCompatibleElement. The [catalog runner](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs) supplies the explicitly requested host to the public compiler, retaining Legacy as the default for all older rows. ## 10. Collaborations In the mixed-version report, the root 3.0 declaration remains outside the locally4.0 template. The template's selection, per-line expression and total inherit4.0 in Legacy. Draft supplies frozen 4.0 throughout either stylesheet. Static use-when, shadow-produced select expressions, AVTs and ordinary select expressions have separate focused controls; changing a serializer version is not a shortcut for changing their host. ## 11. Consequences A Legacy 4.0 stylesheet with a local 3.0 instruction refuses 0x10 with XPST0003; Draft accepts it. A3.0 Legacy root with a local 4.0 template accepts it. Under Draft, an unknown unqualified apply-templates attribute at effective4.0 raises XTSE0090; above 4.0 it is ignored. Legacy's tested apply-templates path ignores it above 3.0. These are bounded instruction controls, not a certification of every unknown attribute/instruction. scan remains unavailable with XPST0017 under both XSLT hosts, including Draft. Runtime malformed quantities still raise FORG0001. ## 12. Implementation Fifty focused host/version cases plus sixteen full report runs execute66 manifest cases through the public compiler. The initial runner forced Legacy and produced56 passes/10 failures against rows requesting Draft. Those failures are retained as a runner limitation, not an engine defect. The runner now accepts explicit processorProfile values legacy/draft40 and rejects unknown spellings; omitted values preserve Legacy. Existing manifest rows and outcomes are unchanged. No engine, public API, version, gate or release changes. [Machine audit](../HOST-PROFILE-BOUNDARIES.json). ## 13. Sample Code The actual [mixed-version stylesheet](../examples/host-profiles/report-local40.xsl) declares version 3.0 on xsl:stylesheet and version 4.0 on xsl:template. Its quantity expression is `(xs:integer(@qty) ?? 1)`. With [normal.xml](../examples/host-profiles/normal.xml), both profiles produce `A=2|B=1|C=0|lines=3;total=3`, exactly matching the baseline. Empty input yields `lines=0;total=0`; reordered rows change line order; `qty="oops"` raises FORG0001. [Task and fixtures](../examples/host-profiles/README.md) include full context and all outcomes. Host configuration is the public ProcessorProfile property; each manifest row states it explicitly. ## 14. Performance Notes Host/version selection is compilation policy, not a performance optimization. Both reports parse and sum quantities per reading; no timing/allocation comparison is claimed. Compilation captures the profile; existing named tests separately verify behavior when a compiler is reused. ## 15. Known Uses Applicable AC-03 evidence: `host-profile-select-root3-legacy`, `host-profile-select-root3-draft40`, `host-profile-select-root4-local3-draft40`, `host-profile-ancestor-root3-wrapper4-local3-legacy`, `host-profile-avt-root3-draft40`, `host-profile-use-when-root3-draft40`, `host-profile-future-attribute-root4-draft40`, `host-profile-report-local40-normal-legacy` and all other cases in [the audit](../HOST-PROFILE-BOUNDARIES.json) and [manifest](../examples/cases.json), run by CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome. This host/compiler/XSLT contract has no applicable XPath-only gate assignment. Named [ProcessorProfileTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/ProcessorProfileTests.cs): DraftXPathIndependentOfVersion, LocalVersion, StaticXPathProfile, UnknownAttributeMatrix, CompilationCapturesProfile and DefaultAndInvalidProfile provide independent public-API evidence. The shadow controls generate a 4.0 select expression from a string-valued shadow attribute; they do not certify every4.0 form inside the shadow expression itself. No gate is invented or promoted. ## 16. Related Features [Numeric literals](../operators-and-syntax/numeric-literals.md), [otherwise](../operators-and-syntax/otherwise-operator.md), [xsl:select](xsl-select.md) and [coverage reconciliation](../COVERAGE-RECONCILIATION.md). Package/import propagation is a subsequent bounded slice, not implied acceptance from this entry. REQ-126 and D2/D3/D4/AC-03 remain partial.

xslt-instructions/structured-value-patte.text:
Type, map and array template patterns

21 October 2026

**C12 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-4.md) records three contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Verified bounded structured matching**. C05-K01 generic model/JNode and complete nested schema/nominal pattern combinations remain limited; no universal generic-node promotion. Final owner acceptance remains C13; earlier checkpoints are historical. **Compound-pattern follow-up supplied — 21 October 2026:** [New bounded mapping](../COMPOUND-PATTERN-GRAMMAR.md) now covers set/union grouping, priority and rule identity, with a separately labelled current-draft union-priority gap. Original counts/queues below describe their earlier checkpoint. ## 1. Name and Classification **Implemented bounded XSLT4.0 surface in public1.23.2.** This entry maps tested type, record, map-entry and array-member patterns; it is not the complete pattern grammar. [Pinned source/deliveries](../TYPE-PATTERN-GRAMMAR.md). ## 2. Intent Dispatch structured values to template rules while keeping key presence, member cardinality, type annotation and nominal identity explicit. ## 3. Also Known As Type pattern, string-key map pattern, array member pattern and named record pattern in their respective reviewed forms. ## 4. History / Supersedes The intake [3.0 baseline](../examples/intake-types/report-3.xsl) uses a named template and explicit predicates. The [4.0 report](../examples/intake-types/report-4.xsl) uses structured-value template patterns. Same results for these fixtures do not establish universal equivalence or a general grammar migration. ## 5. Motivation Route valid line maps and nonempty SKU arrays while making zero quantities and empty bundles visible as review cases. ## 6. Language Alignment Pattern syntax is not XPath constructor syntax. `array(atomic(xs:integer)+)` in match differs from a sequence type in @as. Matching does not perform the annotation/conversion that an @as binding may apply. ## 7. Applicability Use when the consumer supports the relevant XSLT host/effective-version contract. Prefer the portable named-template form when targeting3.0 processors. ## 8. Structure Reviewed shapes: `~t:shape`, `record(t:point)`, `{'v':.?}`, `{'v':.,*}` and `array(atomic(xs:integer)+)`. Namespace prefixes, context and complete files are in the [example family](../examples/intake-types/README.md). These shapes do not replace the normative grammar. ## 9. Participants [PatternCompiler](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Patterns/PatternCompiler.cs), [StringKeyMapPattern](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Patterns/StringKeyMapPattern.cs), [ArrayPattern](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Patterns/ArrayPattern.cs) and [RecordPattern](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Patterns/RecordPattern.cs). ## 10. Collaborations Use named aliases for type tests, explicit conversion at bindings, and explicit template priorities where application policy needs them. The report uses disjoint map/array patterns and explicit priorities rather than claiming all default-priority interactions. ## 11. Consequences A closed map pattern rejects extra keys unless opened; optional entry values still require the key. Member occurrence indicators constrain each sequence, not array size. Empty arrays can satisfy universal member constraints; business nonempty checks remain explicit. ## 12. Implementation **C05 grammar review — 26 October 2026, published 1.26.3:** [Type/collection/pattern reconciliation](../TYPE-COLLECTION-PATTERN-RECONCILIATION.md) covers S8-patterns. Fresh version-4 stylesheets in both hosts cover array/member sequences, map missing-versus-empty/surplus keys, aliases, annotated records and nominal identity. Predicates can fail to match without propagating their dynamic errors in the tested forms. No claim of complete declaration/import/package visibility, every composite pattern, generic JNode dispatch or earlier-profile promotion. Independent expected results and remaining ownership are retained; no whole-grammar/model or AC-04 acceptance follows. New manifest checks use default Legacy host and effective version4.0, hence frozen XPath40. Legacy3.0 declaration/pattern refusals are explicit. Host selection, module/package identity, imports and authoring contexts need their own applicable tests; no exhaustive cross-context claim follows. No engine behavior changes. ## 13. Sample Code [map-empty-present](../examples/intake-types/map-empty-present.xsl) versus [map-empty-missing](../examples/intake-types/map-empty-missing.xsl); [array-vacuous](../examples/intake-types/array-vacuous.xsl) versus [array-empty-member](../examples/intake-types/array-empty-member.xsl); six full [reports](../examples/intake-types/README.md). ## 14. Performance Notes Cost follows the value/type/pattern being checked and any conversion/materialization. Field/member walks and predicates can add work; no benchmark, universal speedup or measured memory claim is supplied. ## 15. Known Uses New intake-types map/array/type rows; [map-entry tests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40MapEntryPatternTests.cs), [array tests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40ArrayPatternTests.cs) and [type tests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40TypePatternTests.cs). No new qt4tests gate membership; applicable-gate acceptance remains partial. ## 16. Related Features [xsl:item-type](../deferred/xslt-item-type.md), [xsl:record-type](../deferred/xslt-record-type.md), [switch/array/select](../SWITCH-ARRAY-SELECT-GRAMMAR.md), [full bounded inventory](../TYPE-PATTERN-GRAMMAR.md).

Intent Construct members in stylesheet content and consume the resulting array. ## 3. Also Known As Use the name and spelling in this entry and its executable files. Compare the [complete earlier-version baseline](../examples/xsl-array/before.xsl) with the [complete stylesheet](../examples/xsl-array/transform.xsl). Both yield `2` for this synthetic input. They demonstrate this task, not universal equivalence of the two mechanisms. ## 5. Motivation Build an array of picking-label product codes. Construct members in stylesheet content and consume the resulting array. Keeping this task explicit makes it possible to choose the feature for a practical reason and verify what the receiving application will see. ## 6. Language Alignment Read the behavior as XPath/XSLT semantics. Similar vocabulary in another programming language is not a compatibility promise. With select alone, each item becomes a member. With for-each plus select, each focused input produces one sequence-valued member, including an empty one; explicit array-member also retains a whole sequence. ## 7. Applicability Use this form when solving the stated task and the consumer permits the declared compatibility level. Keep the earlier baseline when the application requires 3.1 expressions or portable 3.0 stylesheets. With select alone, each item becomes a member. With for-each plus select, each focused input produces one sequence-valued member, including an empty one; explicit array-member also retains a whole sequence. ## 8. Structure ```xml ``` This is the worked case's syntax, not a replacement for the full language grammar. Required namespaces and surrounding context are supplied in the linked complete files. ## 9. Participants The stylesheet compiler and TransformEngine execute the instruction; the contained expressions use the existing XPath engine. [Primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40ArraySwitchTests.cs) identify the feature's implementation contract. The examples use public APIs only. ## 10. Collaborations The case combines source values, the named feature, and explicit output formatting. [Worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md) show how selection, construction, and business rejection fit into larger transformations. ## 11. Consequences Benefit: Construct members in stylesheet content and consume the resulting array. Tradeoff: the declared compatibility level and edge rules become part of the consumer contract. With select alone, each item becomes a member. With for-each plus select, each focused input produces one sequence-valued member, including an empty one; explicit array-member also retains a whole sequence. ## 12. Implementation The complete draft-instruction file declares version="4.0". Bosak recognizes these implemented instruction surfaces; its instruction support is separate from XPathCompatibility. Embedded expressions use effective compatibility: under the default Legacy host, effective version4.0 selects frozen XPath40 and a local3.0 override selects XPath31. An explicit Xslt40Draft host selects frozen XPath40 independently of lower local version. Known-instruction recognition is separate from these expression gates. The companion baseline declares version="3.0". Sequence-valued members can retain additional items. These are implementation expectations, not measured deltas. xslt-instructions/xsl-select.md.text:
xsl:select: XPath in stylesheet text

21 October 2026

**C12 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-4.md) records three contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Verified bounded XPath body instruction**. CDATA is an XML authoring mechanism; complete schema/static/package/resource combinations and global static-detection mode remain unaccepted. Final owner acceptance remains C13; earlier checkpoints are historical. ## 1. Name and Classification **xsl:select — implemented Bosak XSLT4.0 surface.** [Body-expression delivery `69a7cfd3`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/69a7cfd3c84e405c037be41786464950d1c06696); [current source review](../SWITCH-ARRAY-SELECT-GRAMMAR.md). This entry documents shipped behavior under REQ-126, not a new engine feature. Historical adopted specification revision is not recovered; current review pin is3230573afe246f1b502ed2e22d187ce9928155b1 section `select-instruction`. ## 2. Intent Return an XPath expression result while keeping a multiline expression in XML text or CDATA rather than a quoted XML attribute. ## 3. Also Known As Text-body XPath evaluation. `xsl:sequence/@select` is the earlier alternative, not an alias for the new instruction. ## 4. History / Supersedes The [3.0 dispatch report](../examples/dispatch-grammar/report-3.xsl) uses value-of/attribute expressions; the [4.0 report](../examples/dispatch-grammar/report-4.xsl) uses xsl:select for report fragments. Both explicitly create text. Arbitrary returned maps, arrays and nodes require their own receiving context; text conversion is not universal equivalence. ## 5. Motivation Keep both quote characters, braces and formatting readable in dispatch/report expressions. XML escaping is still needed for ordinary text containing markup delimiters; CDATA avoids those escapes subject to XML's CDATA terminator rule. ## 6. Language Alignment The body is XPath, not JavaScript or an XSLT sequence constructor. Literal braces belong to XPath maps/strings, not AVT or expand-text interpolation. Returning items does not imply writing text nodes. ## 7. Applicability Use when the receiving Bosak host permits the implemented draft surface. Use portable3.0 instructions when portability is required. Validate structured results through their consumer rather than stringifying them unintentionally. ## 8. Structure ```xml ``` Complete namespace/context declarations are in [select-cdata.xsl](../examples/dispatch-grammar/select-cdata.xsl). Optional as applies result conversion/type checks. Only permitted leading fallbacks precede expression text; this is a descriptive shape, not a complete grammar. ## 9. Participants [Stylesheet](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Stylesheet/Stylesheet.cs) validates content and selects expression compatibility; [TransformEngine](../../../src/Bosak.Xslt/Runtime/TransformEngine.cs) evaluates it with the caller's context. No new public API is introduced. ## 10. Collaborations Combine with variables/functions for structured values and value-of for explicit text output. The dispatch report uses arrays and switch without flattening away empty batch members. ## 11. Consequences Improves expression readability but adds a draft instruction dependency. Adjacent atomic values can gain separators during tree construction; explicit text construction matters. Optional result types can raise XPTY0004. ## 12. Implementation Default Legacy host uses effective version:3.0 expressions use XPath31,4.0 uses frozen XPath40, and local overrides matter. Known instruction recognition is separate: Bosak accepts the tested simple xsl:select forms under3.0, but this is not portable3.0 syntax. Explicit Xslt40Draft host selects frozen XPath40 independently of local lower version. [Version matrix](../SWITCH-ARRAY-SELECT-GRAMMAR.md#recognition-is-distinct-from-compatibility). ## 13. Sample Code Run the complete [report](../examples/dispatch-grammar/README.md) against normal, empty and reordered input. The [focus](../examples/dispatch-grammar/select-focus.xsl) and [text-focus](../examples/dispatch-grammar/select-focus-text.xsl) files distinguish item results from explicit text. The [required-empty](../examples/dispatch-grammar/select-required-empty.xsl) file intentionally fails XPTY0004. ## 14. Performance Notes Cost is dominated by the XPath expression and its result materialization. CDATA changes XML authoring, not an execution complexity guarantee. No measured speed or memory improvement is claimed. ## 15. Known Uses New manifest IDs include dispatch-grammar-select-cdata, select-coercion, select-type-error, select-required-empty, select-focus/text and expression-root30/root40/local30/local40. [Xslt40SelectTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40SelectTests.cs) and [ArraySelectNativeBoundaryTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/ArraySelectNativeBoundaryTests.cs) supply additional source/native evidence. No applicable XPath qt4tests expression set or new GatedSets member exists for this XSLT instruction; AC-03 acceptance remains partial. ## 16. xsl:switch

Practical reference: Bosak XSLT 4.0 surface

**C12 contract/evidence review — 26 October 2026:** [Per-entry receipt](../SEMANTIC-REVIEW-BATCH-4.md) records three contract groups with exact examples, context, applicable evidence and language-alignment limits. Status: **Limited selection; incomparable-comparison blocker**. C06-H02: both fresh host controls still return empty instead of XPTY0004. Ordinary dispatch success does not certify full general-comparison semantics. Final owner acceptance remains C13; earlier checkpoints are historical. **Grammar/version review — 21 October 2026:** [Current pinned mapping](../SWITCH-ARRAY-SELECT-GRAMMAR.md) and [complete dispatch comparison](../examples/dispatch-grammar/README.md) distinguish known-instruction recognition, effective XPath version, raw result types and actual text delivery. Public1.23.2 is verified; historical provenance gaps remain. ## 1. Name and Classification **xsl:switch** - **Bosak XSLT 4.0 surface**. Delivery family: [REQ-118](../../REQ-118-xpath-xslt-40.md) / [REQ-123 registry](../../FEATURE_REQUESTS.md). Section provenance: REQ-118 S7/S8; corresponding local XSLT surface tests. [Primary implementation evidence](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40ArraySwitchTests.cs) records the shipped behavior; this entry adds executable user-facing examples under REQ-126, rather than announcing a new engine feature. **External specification references (current drafts; links checked 2026-10-11):** [XSLT 4.0: conditional processing with xsl:switch](https://qt4cg.org/specifications/xslt-40/Overview.html#xsl-switch). See the [catalog source policy](../README.md#external-specifications-and-source-documentation) for adopted-revision provenance. **Delivery provenance:** [PR #92](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/pull/92), [immutable mainline revision `2a62ad4d`](https://github.com/Fytala-Charles/Bosak/commit/2a62ad4d9f72d2614887c260e8856de0a6617350) (2026-10-08). This identifies the engine delivery; later documentation examples do not redefine that delivery. **Adopted specification revision:** the historical dossiers refer to live draft sections, but do not retain an immutable specification-source revision for this entry. That provenance gap remains explicit. Current section links checked on 2026-10-11 are navigation references, not proof of the adopted snapshot. See the [provenance ledger](../PROVENANCE.md). ## 2. Intent Match a selector against branch test values. ## 3. Also Known As Use the name and spelling in this entry and its executable files. Related functions or instruction forms are described in the primary test evidence; no additional alias is adopted here. ## 4. History / Supersedes Use xsl:choose and repeat the selector in each condition. Compare the [complete earlier-version baseline](../examples/xsl-switch/before.xsl) with the [complete stylesheet](../examples/xsl-switch/transform.xsl). Both yield `expedite` for this synthetic input. They demonstrate this task, not universal equivalence of the two mechanisms. ## 5. Motivation Route a task by a single priority selector. Match a selector against branch test values. Keeping this task explicit makes it possible to choose the feature for a practical reason and verify what the receiving application will see. ## 6. Language Alignment Read the behavior as XPath/XSLT semantics. Similar vocabulary in another programming language is not a compatibility promise. Tests are values compared with the selector using general comparison, not boolean guards. The otherwise branch handles absent/unrecognized values. Incomparable numeric/Boolean operands currently return empty instead of the required XPTY0004 in both hosts (C06-H02); the ordinary string-dispatch example does not cover that gap. ## 7. Applicability Use this form when solving the stated task and the consumer permits the declared compatibility level. Keep the earlier baseline when the application requires 3.1 expressions or portable 3.0 stylesheets. Tests are values compared with the selector using general comparison, not boolean guards. The otherwise branch handles absent/unrecognized values. Incomparable numeric/Boolean operands currently return empty instead of the required XPTY0004 in both hosts (C06-H02); the ordinary string-dispatch example does not cover that gap. ## 8. Structure ```xml ``` This is the worked case's syntax, not a replacement for the full language grammar. Required namespaces and surrounding context are supplied in the linked complete files. ## 9. Participants The stylesheet compiler and TransformEngine execute the instruction; the contained expressions use the existing XPath engine. [Primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40ArraySwitchTests.cs) identify the feature's implementation contract. The examples use public APIs only. ## 10. Collaborations The case combines source values, the named feature, and explicit output formatting. [Worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md) show how selection, construction, and business rejection fit into larger transformations. ## 11. Consequences Benefit: Match a selector against branch test values. Tradeoff: the declared compatibility level and edge rules become part of the consumer contract. Tests are values compared with the selector using general comparison, not boolean guards. The otherwise branch handles absent/unrecognized values. Incomparable numeric/Boolean operands currently return empty instead of the required XPTY0004 in both hosts (C06-H02); the ordinary string-dispatch example does not cover that gap. ## 12. Implementation The complete draft-instruction file declares version="4.0". Bosak recognizes these implemented instruction surfaces; its instruction support is separate from XPathCompatibility. Embedded expressions use effective compatibility: under the default Legacy host, effective version4.0 selects frozen XPath40 and a local3.0 override selects XPath31. An explicit Xslt40Draft host selects frozen XPath40 independently of lower local version. Known-instruction recognition is separate from these expression gates. The companion baseline declares version="3.0". See [CatalogExampleTests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Documentation/CatalogExampleTests.cs): it executes the published files from the [case manifest](../examples/cases.json). This documentation slice changes no engine source. ## 13. Sample Code Input is synthetic and declared directly in the complete expression, or in [main.xml](../examples/xsl-switch/main.xml) for an instruction example. The [complete stylesheet](../examples/xsl-switch/transform.xsl) yields `expedite`. The [edge case](../examples/xsl-switch/edge.xml) yields `review`. No external resources or application variables are required. See the [example runner](../examples/README.md) for commands and host context. ## 14. Performance Notes Expected class: selector conversion followed by branch-value comparisons. The number and cost of branch tests matter. These are implementation expectations, not measured deltas. No benchmark is claimed; use the repository benchmark harness before making workload-specific speed or memory claims. ## 15. Known Uses Executable example IDs: `xsl-switch-main`, `xsl-switch-edge`, `xsl-switch-before` in `CatalogExampleTests.PublishedExample_MatchesDeclaredOutcome`. Existing unit evidence: [primary tests](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40ArraySwitchTests.cs). Chapter-level evidence does not promote a qt4tests set into GatedSets; conformance status remains owned by the harness and delivery records. **Named implementation evidence:** [`Switch_LookupTable_SelectBranches`](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40ArraySwitchTests.cs), [`Switch_TestSequences_DaysInMonth`](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40ArraySwitchTests.cs), [`Switch_GeneralComparison_NumericPromotion`](../../../tests/Bosak.Xslt.Tests/Xslt40ArraySwitchTests.cs). Not a qt4 expression-set feature. XSLT evidence uses the named instruction tests below; no upstream XSLT gate promotion is claimed. These references describe existing evidence; this documentation update does not rerun or promote the full conformance suite. ## 16. Related Features See the [catalog index](../README.md), [worked chapters](../worked-examples/README.md), and the alternatives in section 4. The case may be used independently of the larger chapters. *Created 2026-10-11: verified practical catalog example and earlier-version baseline.* Updated21 October2026: dispatch-grammar array/switch cases add exact source-node identity, empty-member and3.0/4.0 host/version evidence without changing engine semantics.
